venues.name: Dishoom Covent Garden
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.
venues.address: 12 Upper St Martin's Ln, London WC2H 9FB, UK

reviews.text: A modern restaurant in a great central location serving excellent quality Indian dishes. Pretty huge menu can be quite overwhelming but does offer plenty of choice. Fantastic curries including mutton which was excellent and monkfish as well as the classic Chicken Ruby. The Biryani was great with a jackfruit option for the non meat eaters and the black daal was amazing! Some excellent drink options too with refreshing lassis, trendy cocktails and the classic Kingfisher beer and Thums Up Asian cola. Would recommend booking in advance as gets very busy with queues often spanning round the block. Service can be touch and go particularly during busy periods where you’re often fighting to get someone’s attention but overall a great experience with delicious food.

Dishoom doesn’t need a critical review. It’s buzzing like the AI boom. Always has a line out the door, especially this original location. They dine you fast so don’t be discouraged by the long lines. We walked in on a busy Saturday evening & managed to snag a table in 30 mins. The vibe of the restaurant is electric, two floors packed with customers & waiters running around harmoniously. It’s really a well run restaurant with top customer service. The menu is intriguing & drool worthy. We tried a bunch of the things - pav bhaji, house chaat, chicken ruby, garlic naan & Kashmiri Chili ice cream. All taste good, but not out of this world good. They do the nail that Bombay Irani cafe vibe & overall it’s a crowd pleaser of a place. Dishoom is an impressive place to visit but isn’t necessarily a memorable one. Again, it doesn’t need this critique as it does a commendable job and it’s gonna thrive for years to come.

WORTH. THE. HYPE.  This was the best Indian food we've had since...being in India and it's not even close.  We waited maybe 20 minutes for a table for 6 (5 humans and a toddler) which wasn't bad in my opinion.  Our waiter insanely attentive.  We ordered drinks and I wanted to try their chai, but he said I should have something fun so he made it a ~naughty chai~ but then also brought me a regular chai just to try it too.  He brought out a milk for our toddler and it was just slightly warmed (nice touch).  We talked about how we went to Dehli a few years ago and that's where our waiter was from originally, so he brought us out a local dish that we didn't try while we were there.. very thoughtful!  You name it, we got it to try.. vegetable samosas, chili chicken, butter chicken, chicken biryani (the cranberries were actually a surprisingly great touch), the House Black Daal, the broccoli salad, cheese naan, garlic naan, raita.. nothing missed.  We stuffed ourselves silly.  We also came here to celebrate my mother-in-law's birthday and at the end he brought out THREE desserts for her which was insanely nice.  I swear it was the most welcoming restaurant and atmosphere.  I wish I could come back every month.

venues.image_alt: Dishoom Covent Garden — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Gymkhana
venues.description: Tandoor oven roasts, sigri charcoal grills and seasonal curries at Raj-era themed Indian restaurant.

reviews.text:
We visited Gymkhana for lunch and opted for the lunch set menu for two. The portions were generous and perfect for sharing, which is clearly the core part of the lunch set menu concept.

The butter chicken was rich and flavourful, and the bread basket complemented everything beautifully. The aloo chaat starter was another highlight incredibly tasty and the perfect way to start the meal.

We also tried the Goat Methi Keema and Salmon Tikka, which were slightly saltier than our preference not bad by any means, but we personally prefer a milder seasoning. The Falooda dessert was decent but not particularly memorable compared to the rest of the dishes. For that reason, we would rate the food 4/5 overall, while still acknowledging that several dishes were outstanding.

The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the staff were exceptionally friendly and attentive. They took the time to explain each dish as it was served, which added a thoughtful touch to the whole experience. We were there for a birthday celebration and to our surprise, they brought out a birthday cake and a greeting card such a lovely gesture!

Overall, we left very happy. Great food, great service and a memorable experience. It is slightly on the expensive side, but definitely worth trying at least once. Highly recommended!

We had an absolutely wonderful experience! The food was simply amazing — every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. The ambiance made the whole experience even better, with a warm and inviting atmosphere that felt both elegant and comfortable. What truly stood out was the service — the staff were attentive, friendly, and went out of their way to make sure everything was perfect. A truly memorable dining experience that I’d love to repeat! A very special thank you to Kishor, who made our dining experience truly memorable and worth visiting the restaurant.

Gymkhana was a good experience and some food items were really tasty as well. Loved their beet root pao and aloo chaat. The desserts were delicious too. Loved the kheer.

We were seated in the Vault dining area and the service was top notch. Vaibhav
was an amazing host and took great care of us and offered valuable recommendations too.
The quantity of the portions was also great. I did not expect the portions to be this bigat a Michelin restaurant, but was pleasantly surprised.

Why the 4 stars?

I was expecting a bit more visual appeal from both the food and drinks, especially considering the two-star rating. The plating felt quite ordinary to me.
Also, didn't feel value for money given their expensive prices.

Overall a good experience though and would recommend everyone to try once at least.

venues.description: The India - Fleet Street is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, The India - Fleet Street provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 8 Crane Ct, Fleet St, London EC4A 2EJ, UK

reviews.text: Had a fabulous time at the restaurant. Khalid provided great service. The food was tasty and served on time. I liked the portions. And the taste is very close to authentic. Will definitely come back
I really enjoyed my time in the restaurant. Khalid and his team were very kind and they gave me great recommendations. I really appreciated the great service!

We had a wonderful dinner here! The tandoori starters were smoky and full of flavor, the lamb shank was tender and fell off the bone, the chicken paprikash was rich and comforting, and the onion bhaji was perfectly crisp without being greasy. The poppadoms were light and crunchy, served with tasty dips to start the meal off just right. Every dish was fresh, well-seasoned, and beautifully presented.

The service was impeccable, friendly, attentive, and very accommodating, which made the whole experience even better.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic, flavorful Indian cuisine with top-notch hospitality. We will definitely be back!

venues.name: The India - Cannon Street
venues.description: Classic Indian dishes served in 3 candlelit underground rooms with whitewashed, vaulted ceilings.
venues.address: 21 College Hill, Cannon St, London EC4R 2RP, UK

reviews.text: Totally deserves 5 stars, food was delicious fresh, beautiful and with a decent price. The stuff was efficient friendly and nice. I took one star from the atmosphere even that the place has good music and very nice look since it's underground, and a vent was missing.

We loved the express lunch sets ~£14 for 2 courses (starter & main).  The veggie samosas were hot, crispy and comforting. The mains come with rice and naan (which was the most delicious naan I've ever had - soft, thin and fluffy). Recommend the chicken jalfrezt and chicken madras (great if you like spicy food).

The Cannon Indian Street is a great spot to enjoy authentic flavors. The food was really good, well-prepared, and full of taste. The ambiance was lively and welcoming, making the overall dining experience even better. A nice place to go for Indian street-style food with a modern touch.

venues.name: Maharaja of India
venues.description: Traditional Indian cuisine and tandoori specialities served in a contemporary room in neutral tones.
venues.address: 19A Charing Cross Rd, London WC2H 0ET, UK

reviews.text:
⭐ 5

Absolutely incredible experience! This Indian restaurant exceeded all my expectations. The butter chicken,Shashlik Roshila,Garlic Chilly Chicken was rich and flavorful, and the garlic naan was perfectly crisp and soft at the same time.Tandoori Chicken was nicely cooked and juicy.Everything tasted fresh and was beautifully presented.

The staff were warm, welcoming, and happy to make recommendations (which were spot-on). The service was quick but never rushed. The ambiance is cozy and inviting, with traditional decor that adds to the overall experience.

There are tons of vegetarian options too, which is a big plus. Pricing is very reasonable for the quality you get.

Definitely one of the best Indian meals I’ve had—will be back soon and recommending it to everyone.

I visited this restaurant after seeing many great reviews, but my experience didn’t really match the expectations. I arrived at 1:30 PM and the place was nearly empty, yet it took around 35 minutes for our food to arrive, even though we only ordered two curries.

Many reviews mentioned friendly service, but we were served by a different staff member who was just average, not particularly warm or attentive. The butter chicken was a little bland and average, and the other curry tasted just average or even a lil below. Quite overpriced as well considering the portion.

Nayem was an excellent host!! (More than a waiter) he was a teacher of indian cuisine!! Im traveling from Mexico and people told me i MUST try indian food in london, specifically CHICKEN BIRYANI. Nayem even gave me a special yoghurt sauce for my biryani! Gave me a great indian beer!! MAHA RAJA is your best option! A few steps from Trafalgar Square!!

venues.name: Chettinad Restaurant
venues.description: Tamil food with many vegetarian options, served in an understated dining room with Indian touches.

reviews.text: Chettinad Restaurant offers a vibrant taste of South India. The Kappa Mincurry blends spicy minced meat with soft tapioca bold and earthy. Chicken Biryani is fragrant, with tender chicken and rich spices. The Masala Dosa is crisp, filled with flavourful potato, and paired with fresh chutneys and sambar. Warm service and authentic ambience elevate the experience. A perfect spot for those craving traditional Chettinad flavours with a touch of finesse.

Best Indian food in town. It serves especially southern Indian food, which suits my taste more as I love hot food. The lamb madras and the house special king prawn, sooooo nice!!!! The service is good, and the decor is very fancy. Defo 5 star review!

We walked past this place and decided to pop in for lunch. We were initially the only guest and another table came later. Service was good. I had the prawn curry which had a heavy tomato base that I wasn’t keen on. This wasn’t mentioned in the menu and I was a little disappointed as I had avoided another dish because it mentioned tomatoes in the description. My paratha was lovely. Restaurant clean and well presented.

venues.description: Dishoom Kensington is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.vicinity: Barkers Shopping Arcade, 4 Derry St, London

reviews.text:
This place offers a unique dining experience with its retro-inspired interior and welcoming atmosphere. The service was excellent—friendly waiters. 🍳
The filled breakfast naan was a perfect start, and the chocolate lava dessert with vanilla chili ice cream was simply divine. A must-try spot for great food and warm service!

Went here based on YouTube travel videos.

Also, made a reservation ahead of time because of its popularity.

If you like spicy food, this is the place for you.

We've had spicy food in Southern California, but in comparison to how it was here, what we had before was toned down. There's no holding back at this restaurant.

I wondered why the portions seemed small and just contributed it to European culture until I realized the food is so spicy that we could only eat so much in one sitting.

The servers were friendly enough, although I wish they had left the pitcher of water on our table instead of us waiting for them to refill our cups. Better yet, milk might have been better.

As for the restaurant itself, it's a mix of retro and modern.

The bathrooms were really retro, like the toilets had the pull chain and the sink had the 2 different faucets for hot and cold.

It's a nice restaurant, just know that eating the food here is like being on an episode of "Hot Ones".

Just love Dishroom. A chain overall the London, but consistent good quality food, great service, and beautiful ambiance. We tried what the waiter recommended. The are all good. Even the dessert - rice pudding is good not so sweet. This place is definitely one of the best restaurants in London.

venues.description: Dishoom Carnaby is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Dishoom Carnaby provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
I was wondering why so many people queueing to the place. It’s modern Indian cuisine.

Tasty, good price vs quality, but same time nothing beyond the universe.
Incredibly well organized the booking process and service in general.

I love open kitchen style, it builds the trust and confidence in a food.

Only one dish with prawns and it’s not the best which I tried. However lamb was delicious

We walked in from the street with no reservations and I feel we got the last table. We had such a good experience. With everything. The service was very friendly and helpful. The food was excellent and very delicious. Especially the salad we had was worth mentioning. I would eat that every day if possible 😍. I will work hard at home to try replicate that🫶🏻

Stopped by this Indian restaurant and was immediately taken by the great view — definitely a lovely setting. There was a long line, but they managed it well by seating us in the bar area while we waited, which was a nice touch. The service stood out — especially our server, who was fantastic and genuinely friendly, making us feel welcome throughout.

Unfortunately, the food didn’t quite live up to expectations and lacked the depth of flavour I was hoping for. That said, the prices were reasonable, and the overall experience was still enjoyable. Would consider giving it another try.

venues.name: Dishoom Shoreditch
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.

reviews.text: This is a nice restaurant with very friendly staff. It seems to be quite popular, as it was really full and we had to make reservations a few days in advance. The food is good, however, the drinks and coffee were excellent. My friends ordered the chocolate pudding and really seemed to enjoy it. While the dishes aren’t quite as authentic as I expected—more tailored to the local community’s taste—I think it’s still worth experiencing for yourself. Overall, it’s a pretty okay restaurant.

I tried Indian food for the first time with my husband – a very special experience! Everything was different from what we know of Turkish or German cuisine, very flavoursome and interesting. Some dishes took a bit of getting used to, but we really enjoyed trying everything. The atmosphere was great, the staff very friendly and attentive, and we especially appreciated the dessert offered on the house. Definitely worth trying for anyone curious about Indian cuisine.

Wonderful food, venue and staff! We came with our 3 month old, was promptly seated with quick access to a baby change toilet. We had a great waitress who answered any questions we had, made recommendations and helped resolve a minor food 'issue' quickly. Plenty of staff on hand for all tables. Decor and vibe is lovely in here, chatted to other people on our long table too who were interested in the little one.

Food was excellent, as was the drink. We had a non alcoholic cocktail and a crumble sour, which was amazing! Sharing a photo of the food, it was all so excellent, you must try the chilli toast and any curry you fancy. Samosas are great too!

We paid and stayed at the table for a bit to feed the little one, no rush! The manager even helped fill our flask with boiling water before we left, which helped relax us for the next two hours before a feed was due.

Only minor downside would be I think north of £7 for a can of beer is extortionate.

Would come back again!

venues.name: Dishoom King's Cross
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.

reviews.text: It had been ten years since the last time I visited the King’s Cross location and it was just as good as I remembered. Every dish was full of flavor and perfect for sharing. Since we didn’t have a reservation, glad we showed up early for a blue hair dinnertime as the line was long outside when we left. So be prepared to wait during busy times, but it’s worth the wait.

It was my first time trying Indian food, and it was absolutely delicious! The flavors were rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and even though the restaurant was quite busy, the food came out quickly. Such a wonderful experience — I’m really impressed!

Visiting Dishoom King’s Cross for the first time was a real treat, and it certainly lived up to its reputation. My wife had been before, so she already knew what to expect, but for me it was something completely new. We were slightly pressed for time as we had a train to catch back up north, so I was a little worried about queues and delays. Sure enough, when we arrived there was already a queue forming outside, and the weather looked like it was about to turn. Thankfully, the team at Dishoom were quick to act – we were seated outside almost immediately, and service began straight away. That efficiency made a big difference, as it meant we could relax and enjoy the meal without clock-watching.

The setting itself was welcoming, even outdoors. Despite the looming rain, the atmosphere carried the lively, bustling energy that Dishoom is known for. There’s a sense that you’re part of something bigger than just a restaurant – more like a communal dining experience where everyone is there for the same reason: good food and a warm vibe. By the time we were leaving, the rain had just started to fall, which made the timing feel almost perfect.

As for the food, it really was excellent. Everything we ordered arrived quickly and was cooked to perfection. Dishoom has a reputation for bold, flavourful Indian dishes that balance authenticity with modern touches, and that was exactly what we experienced. From the seasoning to the presentation, nothing felt rushed despite our limited time. It’s rare to feel both unhurried and well-looked after in such a busy spot, but the staff managed it brilliantly.

Overall, Dishoom King’s Cross was a fantastic first-time experience for me. Efficient service, delicious food, and great timing meant we left full, happy, and on schedule for our train.

venues.name: Kricket Soho
venues.description: A classic & creative selection of Indian-inspired dishes & cocktails in a contemporary eatery.

reviews.text: Absolutely love this busy but tasty Indian in soho.  Don’t miss out on their rotating list of curries, mains, starters and sides.  Each bite was better than the one before.  Had the venison curry which was absolutely remarkable. I want to go back immediately.
It was a lovely dinner, we had a great time. The mix of flavours and textures was incredible. It wasn't our first time eating Indian food, but these dishes were delicious.

Husband and I had a wonderful experience here sitting at the Chef’s Counter. The server assisted with the number of dishes to ensure we didn’t over order. Had amazing , krispy,  deliciously seasoned Kerlan Fried Chicken and a tender, flavorful Venison Lal Maas. We added cucumber Raita and it was the perfect bite to accompany the venison. Leek and potato Paratha was the best bread to eat with the venison and raita. Wonderful meal!

venues.image_alt: Kricket Soho — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Punjab Restaurant
venues.description: Informal 1940s Covent Garden restaurant with traditional tandoori dishes and Punjabi specialities.

reviews.text:
While in London, we were headed to a restaurant in the West End and a gentleman named Christopher guided us to our destination
He was a very king man and we got talking about food, especially curry and he suggested going to Punjab.
He said it was very delicious and it wouldn’t break the bank.
A Few days later we decided to try Punjab.
He was spot on!
The food was superb and the service was impeccable.
Honestly the best butter chicken I’ve  had in my life.
Kingfisher beer is now a fan favourite
Highly recommend this restaurant if you’re in the area
Cheers

We made a reservation in advance – and it was a good thing, since the restaurant was full.
The staff was kind and patient, even when we had some difficulty understanding parts of the menu.
The food arrived fairly quickly, and it was tasty, unique, and even a bit spicy 😅.
The place has a special atmosphere that combines history, culture, and cuisine – a truly enjoyable experience!
Overall, the restaurant is excellent, and I highly recommend it.

This is by far my favourite Indian restaurant in London, I come here over and over again. The food is exquisite and caters to all. The atmosphere is cute, it's a big location so suitable for many types of groups. The location is great as well. Staff are really friendly and helpful.

venues.name: Colonel Saab
venues.description: Fancy restaurant with an old-world vibe offering creative Indian cooking, plus cocktails.

reviews.text: The food and setting was spectacular.. a very different menu to any other with everything absolutely delicious. We tried dishes that were completely unknown to us, which makes for an exciting change. The Banarasi cocktail was excellent. The service was polite and courteous, though we caught them just as the kitchen was closing and they were setting up for the evening, so we may have not got the best of their attentions. Already looking forward to going back and trying the full tasting menu.

I recently went for afternoon tea at Colonel Sahab, and it turned out to be a truly delightful experience. The ambiance had a charming mix of elegance and warmth, making it perfect for a relaxed afternoon. The service was attentive without being overbearing, which added to the comfort.

The food was beautifully presented—fancy yet rooted in Indian flavors, giving the whole spread a unique twist. Every bite felt fresh and thoughtfully crafted.

Now, here’s an unpopular opinion—I’m not really a chai person. Instead, I opted for a citrus chamomile tea, which was refreshing, light, and soothing. My friend went with the classic chai, and I have to admit—it smelled heavenly and tasted amazing too.

It is on the pricier side, but the overall experience makes it worth it—great food, lovely drinks, and a calm, welcoming atmosphere. I’d definitely recommend it if you’re looking to indulge in a refined afternoon tea with an Indian touch.

Amazing place. The staff are super friendly, the menu is well structured with lots of options for everyone and a great mix of different flavours and textures. The wine list is built to match the food. I had the prawn chimichi started and the fish curry as a main. The food was cooked to perfection and full of flavour. My waiter, Rony, was attentive, smiley and seemed genuinely pleased to be serving my table. I used to manage restaurants and he is sort of person I would have employed in a heartbeat, a true example of what hospitality should be.

The restaurant was busy as well, on a Monday! Which made for a great atmosphere.  Lots of happy diners and a really nice dining room with perfect lighting and lovely decor.

I don’t live in London, but the next time I’m back here I will be making a beeline for Colobel Saab!

venues.image_alt: Colonel Saab — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Aladin Brick Lane
venues.description: Bangladeshi, Indian and Pakistani curries, baltis and grills in small, bring-your-own restaurant.

reviews.text:
Mediocre at best, and as others have said a lot of the reviews are not real. Lacking flavor and spice, and everything served warm.

Lamb samosa were dry and lacked flavor. Shrimp "Blast" was not fresh, and had a strong smell and was mealy - this was supposed to be thier award winning dish. Lamb kurma was gritty and way too sweet. The naan was quite good, but the paratha was gummy. Veggie biryani was decent.  Best part of the meal was the pappadums - although menu says thet are .75p/ea, but somehow got charged £6 for 5 (we made sure to count).

I am sure that they were well reviewed in the past, but thier best days are long behind them. Service was really lacking, and they constantly seem put out just to get us water. Too bad we didn't have Jack serve us, who seems to be mentioned the exact same way in soooo many reviews.

Finally, make sure to check your bill, they seem to just tack on charges. Our bill came to £88.65, but adding it I can't understand how.

I do not recommend at all.

Best  meal ever, lamb bouzjon was fabulous as was everything.  Dudu, Manna and Kawsar  and Abdul were wonderful. Great service, great food, everyone should try this place. Jen and John from Australia 🇦🇺  5 stars 🌟 🌟🌟🌟🌟

Went here yesterday as a birthday treat given to me by my wife.
Food was excellent , service was very good and attentive decor a little dated but not an issue, would come here again.
Atmosphere i marked down simply because we were the only ones in there as it was early.

reviews.text: What a gem of a restaurant. The ambience and decor are excellent from the moment you walk through the door. We sat upstairs which is great for an intimate couple meal. The waiters are pleasant, polite and the service is brisk and efficient. The selection of dishes is very good and all the food was delicious. The highlight of the meal was the theatrical dessert with a dry ice vapour display around our coconut pannacota.

This place is simply amazing.  From the moment we walked in the door it was a next level experience.

The staff were extremely welcoming and focused on us feeling comfortable.

As we walked through the restaurant to the table upstairs the decor was beautifully laid out with gorgeous chandeliers and art from India.

Rajat was our waiter and he was the perfect balance of personable; helpful; and gracious.  We were going to a show so we were a little tight on time, but he made sure we were taken care without us feeling rushed.

Seriously this was one of if not the BEST Indian meals I have EVER had.  The flavors were elevated by the careful crafting of the ingredients and spices by the chef.  Each dish we tried made us pause; close our eyes; and say, “wow”.

It was so good that even though we were going to the show, we had to try the desserts.  They were so good none of us would share!  I got the milk cake and each bite took on an added note that rotated between floral; salty; and crunchy with a well balanced level of sweetness as its base.

Please do yourself a favor and give this place a try….you will not be disappointed.

If I could give this restaurant a 10 star rating I would! We’re here visiting from Canada and had researched where to get amazing Indian food and this restaurant exceeded our wildest expectations! The service was impeccable and the food was melt in your mouth.

The only down side is that I know we won’t be able to get this amazing food back home - which just means we will be back a few more times before our flight.

If you’re coming to London this is a MUST!!!

reviews.text: We done the last minute booking yesterday at this restaurant for my daughters birthday party and it was absolutely outstanding experience, we enjoyed every moment. Food was extremely authentic flavourful you can literally taste in every bite, welcoming friendly staff specially thanks to Naz for the great service. Looking forward to visit again soon.

Yesterday, I had the pleasure of visiting “Bengal Tiger” for the first time, and I would definitely recommend it. The food was great, perfect for anyone who enjoys an authentic Indian cuisine.

The prices are very affordable, especially considering the generous portion sizes, and the restaurant’s spacious venue. Whether you’re dining alone, with friends or family, or celebrating with a large party, “Bengal Tiger” is a great choice. The beautifully designed interior adds to the experience, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere.

The staff is exceptionally friendly and welcoming, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. A special thank you to Amin for his outstanding service - he was attentive, professional, and made sure everything was perfect throughout my lunch. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Had the most amazing meal at Bengal Tiger Indian Cuisine! From the Ambience, to the exquisite meals and the service! Absolutely nothing to fault! Usman served us our meal and he was brilliant! From his recommendations to his knowledge of the meals on the menu, honestly this experience was worth it! We will definitely come back here soon!

reviews.text: I had a fantastic experience at this Indian restaurant yesterday. The food was absolutely delicious, full of flavor and beautifully presented. What really stood out was the service. Our waitress, Shivani, was outstanding. She took the time to explain the dishes to us, gave great recommendations, and made us feel really welcome. The service was attentive and excellent throughout. I’ll definitely be coming back and would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic food with excellent service!

An absolute gem!
Thank you Vatavaran for the most anmazing experience!
Very rare combination of beautiful decor, top notch service and the most delicious Indian food wrapped into a beautiful package that Vatavaran is!
We loved every dish, every conversation with the staff, every second we were there was precious, so much so that we’ve booked our pre- Xmas dinner with the management! Highly recommended, not many restaurants close to this level in Knightsbridge!
Thank you and will be back soon!
Best,
DR

Vatavaran is one of the best, if not the best Indian restaurant in London. My personal favourites on the menu are the aloo tikki, chicken pepper fry, goat shami kebab, lamb and the duck rogan Josh. The cocktails are wonderful, I would recommend the sehar and the kala. The staff are so amazing and the service is always well timed and very thoughtful. The decor is also done really well.

venues.name: Bombay Delight - Wimbledon
venues.description: Bombay Delight - Wimbledon is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Bombay Delight - Wimbledon provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: Bombay Delight, 271-273 The Broadway, London SW19 1SD, UK

reviews.text:
I have discovered the restaurant by chance when coming to Wimbledon. It was such a fantastic Indian restaurant that has various selection of menus and even has special regional menu from time to time. If you are looking for some new exciting Indian dishes, do come in for a try.

I have been there twice in the past few weeks as I can’t get enough of their awesome food. The taste is was great and reasonably priced.  The service was impeccable too.

Really lovely dinner here - it’s a warm quite jazzy atmosphere inside, and the staff who looked after us were absolutely lovely, looked after us really well. And the food! The dishes we ordered were fabulous, starters and mains, the menu had quite a few interesting dishes you don’t see in every Indian restaurant. They also had a nice special tennis menu on for the championship. We also had some cocktails which were delicious and big too. We’ll be back :)

My partner and I came to Bombay delights because it had such great reviews so we had to see for ourselves. We were not disappointed! From the moment we arrived the service was impeccable. We ate from the monthly food festival menu and their a la carter menu - both were delicious. Highly recommend Bombay Delights. Great food, great atmosphere, great service!

venues.name: Oorja Indian Dining
venues.description: Oorja Indian Dining is a indian restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Oorja Indian Dining provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine indian flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
I must say that this was a good surprise. We don’t usually eat Indian food. It was a lovely way to spend the evening eating Indian food. I like that they had a light on the table and when you touched it, they knew that you were ready to order the food was delicious we had k
Dill herb salmon, mango shrimp, curry smoked black Dalla chickpea MASALA butter, chicken and rice this restaurant isright in the theater district. They’ve only been open six months. The Decorations of this restaurant is really nice. The service was excellent. We will return when our next trip to. I had great aprons that you put on when you’re having dinner makes a great picture  thought that was a really cute idea. Also, at the end they gave you this box with herbs in it. We tried it has an interesting taste

We were looking for a highly rated Indian food experience. We were overwhelmed by the Dishoon line and found this amazing place and came in based on its rating. All I can say is WOW. The flavors, the service, the atmosphere, the cleanliness… everything was a 5 from us. I cannot even tell you what was my favorite because all of it was beyond delicious. Lovpreet took incredible care of us and guided us through a unique and flavorful journey via the menu. Just do the chef’s choice. You won’t be disappointed and you definitely get a lot of food, so come hungry. Also get a Masala chai tea. Ah-mazing.

Went to Oorja for their pre-theatre menu, and I’ll get the good thing out of the way first (there’s only one) - the food tastes really good, and their curries and starters have tons of flavour. That’s all!

What spoils the experience is their service, with the staff’s general apathy and lack of interest in doing their job (for a 12.5% service charge that too). They seated us at an unprepared table - missing napkins and the table lamp (which customers must switch to call for service). We sat for 20 mins with no service, waiting for the menu, or being asked for water. We looked around and figured we were missing the lamp, and we had to grab one from an empty table nearby. Ironically, staff keep walking around to fix small bits-and-bobs on empty tables, but never really eye the customers.

Even after finally placing an order, the service didn’t improve - we had different people tend to us at different times, as if they lacked coordination with each other.

The kicker to all this was at the end, when we asked someone from management to have the service charge removed. We whispered to him to have the charge removed so as not to embarrass the staff. But he took it personally, and shouted across the resto to his staff “hey remove the service charge and give this bill” - almost in a petty attempt to embarrass us. He had no questions to us to enquire what went wrong or what could be improved. Good luck showing that attitude.

Overall, felt like the place was run by petty, rude, amateur and unprofessional people (as also evidenced by some of their other confrontational responses to low-rated Google reviews). And this attitude flows through to the staff.

Right after we paid, one of the waiters promptly came and asked us to leave as they have another booking. They didn’t seem to care for the 20 mins we waited for the menus, or the time we waited for each of our courses.

venues.name: Trishna
venues.description: Upscale Indian dishes from the southwest coast using fish and coconut, plus wine pairings.

reviews.text:
We had a fantastic experience at Trishna celebrating my wife’s birthday!

Service: From the moment we arrived, the staff made us feel special. They greeted us with warm birthday wishes. A special thanks to Aneshwar, who went out of his way to accommodate our vegetarian preferences by modifying the weekday lunch set menu—it made the experience feel personal and inclusive. Call out to Preeta too for being extremely courteous through the meal. We were given fresh Plates & cutlery after every course, which added to the experience, since we didn’t mix dishes.

Food: The set menu was generous and filling, with a refined twist on Indian classics. Standouts included the aubergine vathakal, kofta, broccoli in tandoor and the unforgettable desserts—payesh and kheer, which were beautifully balanced and full of flavour.

Drinks: We’ve heard great things about their wine pairings, which are apparently excellent. Sadly, we didn’t get to try them this time—but definitely something to come back for.

The only slight downside was the Belu water being the only option at £3.50pp. It would be nice to have tap water offered as well.

All in all, a wonderful meal, exceptional service, and a warm, celebratory atmosphere. Highly recommended—especially for special occasions!

Excellent dining experience on my first trip to London! I had the summer tasting menu that’s available for lunch and early dinner, and it was the best Indian food I’ve ever had.

I ordered the quail appetizer, salmon appetizer, and eggplant curry main - all were outstanding and delicately spiced, with so many layers of flavor and textures. The mango cheesecake dessert was a wonderful end. I also felt welcomed as a solo diner which was appreciated.

5 star experience! Very friendly and helpful service. We explained our dietary restrictions and were given several recommendations for the tasting menu. The meal was excellent. We selected five courses thinking they would be small like other tasting menus we have experienced, but the portions were very generous. We ended up taking some home with us. The shrimp and squid starter and salmon were our favorite dishes but everything we tried was delicious. We went for my birthday and they brought out a candle to make it special. It was a delicious and memorable experience and we highly recommend this restaurant.

venues.name: Carlotta
venues.description: Carlotta is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Carlotta provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 77-78 Marylebone High St, London W1U 5JX, UK

reviews.text: Amazing food. Amazing service. Amazing waiters and waitresses. Everyone was so welcoming and friendly. I been here twice so far and loved every time I visited. I highly recommend this place. I would suggest the shrimp cocktails, they’re the best thing I’ve ever had!

We came with my husband, parents and 11 month baby. The decoration is really pretty and interesting style. The food is also tasty with the cesar salad, arrabiatta pasta, cod and beef. We had also the tiramisu which was creamy and yummy. And finally the waiter Khan was very caring, kind and professional.

Just went to this fun Italian spot tucked into one of London’s cutest neighborhoods — right along a lively shopping street where you can wander before or after your meal. The place has such a fun vibe — it’s buzzing, loud in a good way, with people having fun and plates flying out of the kitchen and drinks from the bar.
The food? Properly delicious. Think generous carpaccio, spicy pasta, tender meat, that feel straight out of Italy, and starters you’ll want to share (but probably won’t). The drinks are spot-on too — from classic cocktails to fun ones (didn’t try the wines ) that somehow makes everything taste even better.
One thing: the line is no joke. Everyone seems to want in, and I get why. Definitely book ahead unless you enjoy standing on the street watching everyone else eat. But honestly, once you’re inside, it’s worth the wait. The crowd is such a mix — locals, tourists, couples, big groups of friends — and it just adds to the whole atmosphere.
If you’re looking for somewhere lively, tasty, and full of energy, this place nails it

venues.name: Circolo Popolare
venues.description: Glam, atmospheric eatery, opulently decorated with  20,000 bottles, serving trattoria fare & drinks.

reviews.text:
A detailed mixed review for a Monday night visit. The setting of the restaurant is quite impressive, it’s lovely inside. However it is very popular so is very busy. The tables are extremely close together so it feels like you’re sat on top of your neighbours. The service is very mediocre.

The waitress took the order for your the meal and the first round of drinks that’s about it. I was extremely disappointed to witness a member of staff using the toilet without washing their hands. Quite off putting knowing this when you’ve just eaten your meal.

Food was very tasty and this would be the reason we would visit again. Reasonably priced and good portion sizes.

The dessert however was very disappointing and we felt ripped off when it arrived. £14 for a slice of what tasted like dry shop bought cold chocolate cake. A tiny amount of chocolate sauce on the top didn’t help with the dryness would defo avoid!

Overall a decent experience for the food alone but it sadly lets itself down in many other aspects.

Recommendations are required

My husband and I went to Circolo Popolare for our anniversary dinner, and it was such a wonderful experience.

Ambience: ★★★★★
The restaurant is absolutely stunning—perfect for a romantic date night. The interiors are beautifully decorated, featuring elegant Italian ceramic plates and a warm, inviting atmosphere. The place is spotless and well-kept, making it a delight to dine in.

Service:
The service was excellent—friendly, attentive, and quick, which made the evening even more enjoyable.

Food:
The quality of ingredients truly matches what you’d expect in Italy. We started with the Trio d’Olive, which was fresh and flavourful, and the Mozzarella in Carrozza—crispy on the outside, perfectly cheesy inside, and served with a delicious tomato sauce.

For my main, I had the Mafaldine al Tartufo, which was incredibly delicious—rich, aromatic, and bursting with truffle flavour. I highly recommend trying this dish.

My husband ordered the Tagliolini Granchio e Limone. It was decent, but didn’t quite match the wow factor of the truffle pasta.

Note: The only downside was that the toilets were a little dirty and had an unpleasant smell. However, this did not take away from the fact that the restaurant itself is really nice, clean, and beautifully maintained.

Overall, we had a memorable anniversary dinner, and I would definitely return—especially for that Mafaldine al Tartufo!

What a beautiful experience!
My husband and I spent our “thanksgiving” here, and we’re not disappointed! We started with the burrata- absolute perfection floating on a delicious tomato reduction. For our main course we paired the ragu with a Sicily wine, it was fresh and delicious. To end our beautiful experience, we had the tiramisu! Both the food, service, and atmosphere were outstanding- we will be back!

venues.image_alt: Circolo Popolare — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Ave Mario
venues.description: Cool Italian restaurant whipping up meat dishes, pizza, pasta & desserts, plus weekend brunch.

reviews.text: My first time at Ava Mario and I wanted to be sat downstairs as upstairs had a very different decor so asked to change seats. I’d say go downstairs if you want more of an experience. I was initially told that I couldn’t order the carbonara just for one person but then another waiter said I could which was great as I wanted a different dish to my daughter. The pasta was delicious but I was a little disappointed with the salad as I would’ve  liked more Gorgonzola and walnuts. I’d definitely revisit as I’d like to try more of the mains.

This place is a must do, great food and fun atmosphere.  If you are lucky enough to go down 3 levels to eat you will be eating kitchen side with a lively party atmosphere.  This place has truly great food and is also a fun place to hangout!
The place is beautiful inside and the foods are great. Lemon pie is a litle too much but ok, tiramisu is better! Carbonara was good but funghi pasta was amazing 10/10. I recommend it

venues.name: Grasso
venues.description: Grasso is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Grasso provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: I never ever leave reviews but I had to after my experience at Grasso yesterday with my mum. We were running late due to traffic delays and they were super understanding about it. The food was incredible, with huge portion sizes and lovely atmosphere/music! The staff were really friendly too. I would honestly recommend this to everyone!

Really lovely Italian-American restaurant. The Mozzarella Bites were the best I've ever had, as a vegetarian they were able to accommodate doing it not on top of the Nduja sauce and keeping it on the side. It had a good amount of Mozzarella and the hot honey twist was incredible. The pizza tasted New York style with a crispy base and a good amount of sauce on the pizza. We celebrated a birthday and the staff were incredible in assisting with candles, plates for a cake that was bought in from outside. I highly recommend and will be going back.

Very nice restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating. We arrived at around 20:15 on a Friday night and only sat down at 21:00 so definitely book in advance. The vibe was chill so we didn’t mind waiting. The service was very quick and the food also arrived quite quickly. Everything was delicious - the sauce was a 10/10.

venues.image_alt: Grasso — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Gloria
venues.description: Italian fare in an elevated dining room with a marble bar, mirrored ceiling, & rich, eclectic decor.
venues.address: 54-56 Great Eastern St, London EC2A 3QR, UK

reviews.text: We came here for my husband’s birthday and had such a lovely evening! The atmosphere was calm and romantic with low lighting, even though it was busy. The pasta and pizza were delicious, and the food overall was really tasty. Our server was super friendly and made the night feel extra special. Highly recommend!

My partner and I have been a handful of times and thd food is always amazing. Today we had wonderful service! We were well looked after by the server Gervasio for my partners birthday meal. Food was amazing and they were super attentive and caring towards a friend who has a few severe allergies. Our food did take a short while to come out but we deduced this might be due to the kitchen doing a full clean down for our friend with allergies before cooking their meal. Thank you so much we will absolutely be back again!

The atmosphere was superb. A big wow!!!
Based on our experience on fancy-decor restaurants that we have been, the foods did not strikingly impress us. But the foods here are exceptional. Perfectly cooked pastas. Intense flavors. Tiramisu and Cheesecake are  a must-try.   Probably placing this as my no.1 in category of Italian restaurants in London so far.

venues.image_alt: Gloria — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Padella
venues.description: Modern bistro with a short list of housemade pasta dishes accompanied by wine & Italianate drinks.
venues.address: Padella, Borough Market, 6 Southwark St, London SE1 1TQ, UK
venues.vicinity: Borough Market, Padella, 6 Southwark St, London

reviews.text: Fantastic little restaurant with friendly staff and quick service. Our host (sadly didn’t catch his name) was very welcoming, recommended serval dishes and provided a complimentary glass of wine. Food was served fast and hot. The tiramisu for dessert was to die for. Couldn’t recommend enough and will definitely be back :)

Loved our experience at Padella! We visited for the first time for lunch and arrived right as it opened for the day, which helped as the restaurant filled up quickly. Staff were courteous and friendly, and the kitchen was a well-oiled machine. Seated at the bar, we got a front row view of the action, which was part of the charm (highly recommend)! The pasta was well made and if you’re visiting London, you gotta check Padella out!

I appreciated the warm welcome. I was seated promptly and even allowed to change seats. The waitress, Nura, helped me with my order,  her suggestions were exceptional. I went for the Dexter beef shin ragu with Primitivo and Chianti. Let’s just say this is my new pasta spot. Can’t wait to come back. Thank you 🙏

venues.image_alt: Padella — international restaurant in Southwark

venues.name: Bocca di Lupo
venues.description: Authentic small or large plate Italian dining in compact restaurant with neighbouring gelateria.

reviews.text: This restaurant has been on my list for ages and I’m glad I finally came here! Service is so friendly and they make you feel very welcome. Every dish we ordered was beautifully served and tasted amazing! They even gave me a little birthday card and ice cream because it was my birthday! Love an Italian restaurant but this place is extra special! Will definitely be returning.

Popped in for lunch without a booking. Shown seats at the counter, which is by far the best! The menu is split between areas of Italy and you can go on a full culinary tour!
The service is excellent. you have the feeling of being treated like a beloved regular, even if it’s your first time.

I finally made it to Bocca di Lupo — and as an Italian, I can honestly say the food was delicious. It was a fantastic lads’ night!

We started with Manhattans on arrival, then enjoyed at the table:
•	Sage leaves with anchovy
•	Olives stuffed with minced pork & veal
•	Sea bream carpaccio with orange & rosemary
•	Ricotta & spinach ravioli with butter & sage
•	Pappardelle with venison stracotto
•	Roast teal with schiacciata con l’uva & guanciale

Highly recommended desserts:
•	Chocolate & marzipan ball with rum & raisins
•	Affogato al caffè
•	Uva fragola sorbet

All perfectly paired with a Teroldego Rotaliano Terrazze della Luna, 2023 — a smooth and elegant red.

A special thanks to James for the impeccable service — well done, buddy!

venues.image_alt: Bocca di Lupo — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Amalfi Ristorante - Argyll Street
venues.description: Casual, stylish restaurant preparing modern takes on Italian pizza, pasta & seafood.
venues.vicinity: Oxford Circus House, 25 Argyll St, London

reviews.text:
I’ll get straight to the point – this isn’t a restaurant I’d personally return to. I have to admit, I’m not the biggest fan of Italian food in general (even though I consider myself a foodie), so I’ll be a bit subjective there. But where I can be objective is in how the food was cooked, presented, and tasted.

My partner had the pasta, which was freshly made and tasted good, but it didn’t exactly blow her away – just a nice, decent dish. I had the steak, which was a premium cut, not a cheap one, but unfortunately it came out cold. It also wasn’t cooked perfectly to medium rare. It was still edible, and when the waiter asked how it was, I mentioned it was “good but cold” – though she ignored the second part and didn’t follow up or offer a solution.

The kids’ meal was generous, well-priced, and definitely one of the highlights. Cocktails were decent, and the service overall was polite and friendly. The restaurant itself was busy and felt a bit cramped – I assume they’ve added more tables to increase seating, which is understandable.

We only visited because we had a voucher, and while the overall experience was okay, if we had paid full price, I wouldn’t feel it was worth it. Just not somewhere I’d choose to come back to, unfortunately.

Really lovely atmosphere, accommodated our request to be early. Advised us NOT to order something and resulted in our bill being cheaper than if they had let us order. Food was delicious and obviously prepared fresh to order. Shout out to Monica who advised us on best dishes to order and gave us incredible service.

Georgous food, fast service.
Atmosphere stilted and staff hands off.
Lighting a bit too dim for us and toilets were not great. Whilst upstairs seating looked plush, there was a second room wirh awful bamboo seating and cheap looking decor. 15% service charge was automatically added to bill which was already expensive. Super expensive. Quite loud inside as tables close together.

venues.name: Como Garden
venues.description: Airy, plant-filled venue serving elevated Italian tapas, sides & desserts, plus wine & cocktails.
venues.address: 37-45 Kensington High St, London W8 5ED, UK

reviews.text: Went as a family of 5. Gorgeous interior! Very beautifully set out. Food was good, everything tasted great! Portions on the smaller side considering the prices. Service was ok, a bit on the slow side, but everyone was lovely. Overall I did enjoy the night, but personally I think people mainly go there because of the interior and for social media posts 😜.

The best Italian restaurant outside Italy in London! The lasagna was incredible, rich and full of flavor. We also had pizza with vegetables, pesto pasta, and a fresh salad with figs and grapes   all absolutely delicious. Excellent service and charming atmosphere. Highly recommend!

The food was okay. Nothing special. The server Lena was very very good. She went out of her way to please and serve nicely.

The manager was very standoffish and when he was asked to give napkins, he said they had run out of them and brought tissues to the table

venues.name: Faros Oxford Circus
venues.description: Faros Oxford Circus is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Faros Oxford Circus provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 22-24 Great Portland St, London W1W 8QS, UK
venues.vicinity: Highlight House, 22-24 Great Portland St, London

reviews.text: The food was just as good as people say. The beef ragu was delicious and had great deep flavors. We also enjoyed the cheese bread and truffle fries. But the thing that can make or break an experience is the waiter. We had Jass and this young man did an outstanding job taking care of all the outdoor patio tables and was always on top of things. Lovely place and I’m glad we were able to walk you and get a table. We sat outdoors and it was cold outside but with the heaters they have installed I was warm! To finish things we split the tiramisu and it was delicious just like every thing else. Great place and atmosphere was on point.

The food was incredible and the service was impeccable.  Ozzy was our waitor and he was very attentive.

We had the burrata salad which was very tasty, the octopus cappacio was not as good but then I guess octopus doesn't have a strong flavour anyway, but the beef cappacio was very good.

Now, the main courses, wow! The truffle pasta was my favourite, the pasta itself had a great texture, and what I liked the most is that it wasn't soaked in cream, which often happens with a mushroom/truffle pasta dish.  Then the beef Ragu tagliatelle was also great, the beef Ragu was well cooked and seasoned, the tagliatelle again had a great texture.  We also had the risotto mare, there were lots of seafood in it (big prawns, baby squid, clams) and it was definitely cooked with a suace made from the prawns heads, it was super tasty.  We also had the pizza and it was great too.

For dessert, we ordered the tiramisu and chocolate bomb, both were very tasty as well, but they were quite heavy, so we were glad that we shared the desserts amongst the four of us.

Great restaurant, will definitely go again, high recommend it to anyone that's looking for a good quality Italian restaurant to visit in central London.

Absolutely perfect from service, atmosphere and the food. Ozzy looked after our table and made us feel welcomed from start to finish. Starters and mains were above expectations finished off with the best tiramisu I have ever had!
Will definitely visit again and recommend anyone who comes to London.
Best to book ahead to avoid disappointmen

venues.name: Bocconcino Soho
venues.description: Chic Italian dining room & bar serving traditional wood-fired pizza & homemade pasta.
venues.address: 59 Great Marlborough St, London W1F 7JY, UK

reviews.text:
A beautiful spot with lively ambience, and delicious food. Definitely worth a visit if you're in Soho!!
I appreciated the thoughtful and tasty options available. Highlights for me included the vegetarian Tagliatelle with Black Summer Truffle, and the Ravioli stuffed with Spinach & Ricotta!! all of which felt indulgent and well‑prepared.
Service was warm and efficient.

The interior of the restaurant was lovely - stylish and thoughtfully designed, which made a great first impression. However, £18 for a few cherry tomatoes with buffalo cheese felt excessive, especially considering the portion size. The rest of the food was decent, but nothing that really stood out.

A rather odd moment was when my friend’s small bottle of water, which was on the table, was taken away by the staff with the promise to keep it for her - only for it never to be returned.

While the restaurant seems to aim for a fine dining experience, the details let it down. There were quite a few fruit flies around, and at one point a server (in a suit) actually had to catch one with a napkin while serving food - I had pointed it out, but still, not what you'd expect.

Our waitress was pleasant, but service was quite slow, particularly when it came time to pay. When we asked to split the bill by exact amounts, she seemed visibly annoyed, which was disappointing.

As we left, neither of the two hostesses at the front acknowledged us - no goodbye, no thank you - they were too busy chatting with each other, despite clearly seeing us leave.

We did pay the 13.5% service charge, but honestly, it didn’t feel earned. While some dishes were enjoyable, overall the experience didn’t meet expectations, and I wouldn’t return. There are plenty of other places offering better food and service for the same price - or less.

Really enjoyed their bottomless brunch! Food was delicious and our drinks were never empty. The restaurant is beautiful and loved the saxophone player. The waiters were extremely friendly and service was great. One thing to mention- we had already payed for the brunch online prior so when we received a bill on the day we had to correct this and show proof. Issue was sorted quickly though. Would definitely recommend and would come again!

venues.name: Luca
venues.description: Warm, vintage, brick-lined restaurant featuring an elevated Italian menu & fireside terrace seating.
venues.address: 88 St John St, London EC1M 4EH, UK

reviews.text: Chef's menu was pretty good value for money. Portion size was generous and definitely a decent menu with good protein. Culinary skills were clearly showcased in a variety of pasta and meat courses. Truly sensational. Bar counter was less comfortable, but when food was done to perfection, I tended to be less picky on many other things.

The fried potato was unexpectedly great, would highly recommend them as well as the scallops which were cooked perfectly complemented by the sauce. The pastas were also well presented and tasty but I did find them too salty.

The interior is beautiful and service is excellent as expected. Would be a great place for special occasions.

I’ve been to my fair share of Michelin star restaurants and Luca deservedly stands amongst the best in London. From the service, to the interior design/decor, all the way to the food. Attention to detail is something that is clearly drilled into the entire staff. The level of care and professionalism provided such a relaxed and memorable dining experience. We went for the Chefs Menu for 3 guests and every course was close to being faultless. It was a fine example of simplicity done right with fresh ingredients and textures. I found myself asking the waiter about certain elements in each course that caught my attention as I was eating.
As you would expect, the waiting staff was informative and attentive. It’s visibly obvious to see that the standards are set very high and it was hard for me to find faults with the service at any point.
Whenever I find similarities in specific dishes that I’ve had elsewhere, I tend to play the comparison game. Before going to Luca, the best fine dining pork dish I’d had was at Trinity in Clapham. On the chefs menu they served us a pork dish with beans and apricots. To say this was the standout dish by mile is an understatement, officially making it the best pork dish I’ve ever had. This is the true level of Michelin and it’s exactly what brings customers back for more.

Highly recommend

venues.name: Bancone Covent Garden
venues.description: Housemade pastas are offered with Prosecco & espresso in a chic setting with 3 dining counters.
venues.address: 39 William IV St, London WC2N 4DD, UK

reviews.text:
Let me start off with their famous Silk Handkerchiefs Walnut Butter pasta: it is flawless, I can still remember the taste and feeling, definetelt would wanna eat it again. Additionally Cacio and Pepe was equally good. We also tried burrata, which is nice but a bit pricey compared to what you get.

We visitied Bancone in an early afternoon, no reservation and we were seated in 5 minutes. It is open kitchen and as we were eating we were also able to watch kitchen, which was really fun.

My only negative point is that they only accept card

ordered the silk handkerchiefs with walnut butter, the agnolotti, and the artichoke. The pasta was excellent — perfectly al dente and full of flavor. The silk handkerchiefs were my favorite; rich, creamy, and absolutely delicious. The service was a bit slow, but nothing that took away from the overall great experience. Highly recommend!

We were seated on the counter and enjoyed the artichoke, sourdough, signature carbonara and gnocchi. To be honest we really found everything very tasty, the price a bit high. Pasta were all dente and tasty, and all sauces were very interesting. It wasnt just a classic sauce but there was a specific spin to it. The service was nice but quite slow. Decoration wise, it wasnt anything fancy, it is quite small and narrow. Though it is nice to see the staff cooking in front of you.

venues.image_alt: Bancone Covent Garden — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Osteria romana
venues.description: Intimate, elegant setting with a Roman theme for upscale Italian dishes made with imported produce.
venues.vicinity: Albert Gate Court, 3-4 Park Cl, London

reviews.text:
Very nice and cozy Italian restaurant in the heart of Knightsbridge.

The food is great and the service was excellent. Jesus was really nice and friendly. He came to our table all the time to check on us.

The ambiance is really charming and hearing all the different accents all around was very pleasant. It felt like Rome!

Thank you, Jesus.

A top rated place located close to Hyde park. We tried the cacio e pepe with truffles. The pasta is actually further cheesed up in a wheel for some extra indulgence. And the basic spaghetti pomodoro.
The star of the meal was the tiramisu. The best tiramisu I have had anywhere in my life. Had I known this before entering the restaurant, I'd have had 3 mugs for starters, mains and dessert. Absolutely sublime. Rich, luxurious, perfect amount of sweetness, every single thing was spot on for me. There was a father-daughter duo having a meal next to us. The daughter spilled her juice. The staff was kind enough to replace her drink. Terrific experience overall.

Best Gnocchi ever 🤤

This family-run Italian restaurant is an absolute treasure. From the moment you walk in, you're welcomed like part of the family. The atmosphere is warm, intimate, and perfect for a romantic night out or celebrating something special.

The food? Outstanding. Every dish is made with care, using original family recipes that you can truly taste in every bite. Fresh ingredients, rich flavors, and beautifully presented plates make for an unforgettable dining experience.

The staff are incredibly attentive, friendly, and genuinely passionate about what they do. You can tell they take pride in creating not just a meal, but a memorable evening.

Highly recommended — a place you’ll want to come back to again and again.

venues.name: Artusi
venues.description: Chalkboard menu of unfussy seasonal Mediterranean dishes and Italian wines in a pared-back setting.

reviews.text: A truly excellent food experience. Dishes are lovingly and expertly prepared. There's a home cooked feel to the dishes yet there's also sophistication. Me is change frequently, The ingredients were seasonal. Definitely worth coming back many times over
We had a delicious dinner on Saturday evening in lovely ambient setting. Service was excellent. We'll definitely be back !!

Artusi combines wonderful food with a casual atmosphere which makes it a perfect homely place to celebrate with friends.  After celebrating my 30th on the chef’s table a decade ago I recently celebrated my 40th there and it was just as good the second time around.  The chef’s table provides incredible value and allows you to try everything on the menu.

venues.name: Cento Alla Torre
venues.description: Cento Alla Torre is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Cento Alla Torre provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: My team and I went here for a team dinner and we had an amazing time. The host was very accommodating and greeted us with a smile. Pranil served us during our visit and he was very attentive in filling our water and polite. I had pork and it was the one of the best porks I’ve ever had. It was so tender and melts in your mouth. The tiramisu was one of the best I’ve had as well. We were very pleased with overall experience. Will highly recommend!

One of the best meals on our 16 day, five city holiday. We did not have a reservation on a Friday night, but they accommodated us anyway and seated us quickly. Outstanding service, delicious food, and friendly staff. Great wine selection. Reasonable prices. Our servers, Adi and Adi N., were both attentive and helpful. We started with the tasty Insalata allá Parmigiana and a garlic focaccia, with the exceptionally good Bauletti al Stracotto e Barolo - braised beef ravioli! Adi recommended the Panna Cotta al Pistachio, and he was not wrong. It was heavenly!

I came here for my birthday. The service was amazing and the food was great. Our waiter, Craig N, was amazing and pleasant. He gave great suggestions as well. We had branzino, broccoli and lasagne. I will certainly return.

venues.name: manteca
venues.description: Fire-cooked nose-to-tail cuts of meat meet hand-rolled pasta in this simple, Italian-inspired diner.

reviews.text: - Incredible. Definitely coming back. Pasta was absolutely perfectly cooked to an al dente that was so satisfying. The kale sauce was the best (and cheapest). It paired so well with the white wine the lovely waitress suggested. Crab bucatini was also banging but wouldn’t get beef nduja again. The focaccia was so fluffy and great evoo. Ricotta was super lemony-so interesting. Lovely staff, lovely ambience, amazing pasta. Even tho pricey & smallish portions I’d say quality is so good it’s good value

Manteca is a real gem of London showcasing refined Italian cuisine and extensive wine list. The menu is meant to be shared, so bring your friends, grab some wine and enjoy. The flavors are excellent and you will walk away from the meal feeling fulfilled. There are subtle technique changes that could be made to the dishes that would further elevate their offerings, but the flavor is what matters and Manteca does not disappoint in that department.

Lovely restaurant. We ordered coppa, beef shin fritti, and focaccia as entrees. Ewe chop and fazzoletti as main dish, finished with a chocolate tart. Everything was well cooked and taste great. Highly recommended!

venues.image_alt: manteca — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: La Mia Mamma King's Road
venues.description: Quaint Italian restaurant plating regional fare & fresh pasta offering cookery classes & party hire.

reviews.text:
Veramente autentico! There is so much to be said about this delightfully cosy little Italian spot on King's Road, very much in the heart of the Italian Quarter, and a real treat for anyone looking for food and service becoming of Il Bel Paese.

The food, service, warmth and feel of La Mia Mamma was exactly what we were looking for, and I can't recommend anymore in words just how pleasant an experience it was, simply visit and enjoy!

Response to your reply:

I’m giving you straightforward feedback  not looking for drama or attacking your restaurant. I’ve eaten at top places around the world, and what you served didn’t meet the mark. Instead of getting sassy or defensive, take it as a chance to improve. That’s how standards get better.

I went to the kings road one on Saturday, the staff were extremely kind and welcoming, atmosphere was also nice. I ordered the pasta with truffle and honestly it was extremely salty and i couldn’t eat that. I thought maybe be it was the truffle so didn’t think too much of it. Then on Monday my pasta craving was still here as I was left very unsatisfied after Saturday’s experience. Decided to try the one on Hollywood road. It was Monday, less hectic on the kitchen staff so I assumed food will also be better!! Again super warm welcome from staff, we sat outside and it was really lovely. They served us a welcome bruschetta which was delicious. We then ordered Arancini, potato croquettes, potato al forno then the same pasta but this time without the truffle as I thought may be thats what made it too salty. Anyway my honest opinion about their Italian food is. Arancini was tasteless, potato al forno was very good, the pasta was extremely salty and the cheese they made the sauce with was most likely of very commercial quality. One of the worst Italian food experience i have ever encountered. They say “run by real italian mamas” like seriously if i had a real mama cooking italian food like this for me everyday, i would ask her to better rest and don’t cook at all.  Left the restaurant extremely disappointed, may be i didn’t choose the right dish, ill never know as we aren’t going back there ever.

There's nothing quite like going to a restaurant where you feel at home. The chefs are in fact mothers, who cook traditional Italian food for their families at home. Food was exceptional, atmosphere and vibes to match. They were very accommodating with the tasting menu, as I have a few dietary restrictions. Overall very happy tummys, I highly recommend the visit!

venues.name: Ciao Bella Restaurant
venues.description: Classic Italian dishes in airy basement with aqua-blue furniture, framed photos and hanging guitars.
venues.address: 86-90 Lamb's Conduit St, London WC1N 3LZ, UK
venues.vicinity: Rokeby House, 86-90 Lamb's Conduit St, London

reviews.text:
A little piece of Italy in the centre of London.
This evening we visited ciao Bella for a family meal. The food is the most authentic Italian food I’ve had outside of Italy.

I had the special lamb ragu with freshly made pasta , genuinely the best pasta dish I’ve had outside of Italy. I also tried the ravioli , lasagne and arribatta . All incredible dishes. As a fellow italian it takes a lot for me to be blown away by the food whilst eating Italian out… but wow! Incredible.

The portions are super generous almost as if your Nonna was serving you. The atmosphere is vibrant and a busy Italian setting which adds to the whole experience. The staff were great and the fiery, scary, polish nonna was so lovely once we got talking to her!

Highly recommend! Will be back

Very well maintained and ambient Italian restaurant which appears to be run by Italians and feels very much like a family run business.

Vast menu selection and lots of seating options. Indoor and outdoor.

The food portions were good and decent in taste. I have had better Italian food but it was still good, no complaints.

The ambience and atmosphere is lovely and the staff are attentive and whizzing around. We went there as a couple with two yound kids and they have a separate allergen menu which is very easy to use.

What a lovely authentic Italian restaurant! Service was prompt and friendly. The restaurant has lots of atmosphere. I had a special and a salad. My friend had the veal romano. The house wine was pleasant but not very punchy. The espresso was very good and a great way to finish the dinner.

venues.name: PaStation London
venues.description: Casual Italian eatery in a snug space offering create-your-own pasta dishes, plus salads & desserts.
venues.address: 76 Tottenham Ct Rd, London W1T 2HG, UK

reviews.text: This place is incredible. After the first time, I was utterly compelled to come back and I’ve been back almost every week since. The food is UNREAL there’s no doubt about that. Everything just slaps. THE CUSTOMER SERVICE. Guys it’s incredible. Specifically Salva, we see him every time and he’s always so happy to help us out and provides the best care. Highly recommend coming if you need a pasta spot cos trust me this will become THE spot.!

Excellent service received at the tables from Salva, and at the counter. Really friendly team.

They have fresh pasta here, as well as the dried options. Halal beef and chicken, but also serve pork and alcohol. So everyone is catered for. Plenty of soft drinks are available as well as wines.

The meatballs were good. The spaghetti bolognese was avarge, definitely needed more sauce as it was dry. My sister had the gnocchi and she wasn't a fan. The service was ok and it was a decently priced meal for london. I had to ask for a Ferrero Rocher as they missed our table.

venues.name: Zuma London
venues.description: Informal, high-end Modern Japanese with sushi counter, robata grill and natural designer interior.

reviews.text:
I have such wonderful memories of this restaurant. Even though I didn’t have a reservation, they seated me at the chef’s table, which turned out to be a really fun and fascinating experience. I was dining alone, but the food portions were so generous that I left absolutely full and happy.

The first dish was sliced yellowtail sea bass — beautifully fresh, with a delicate pink color. A solid 10/10.

Next came the fried soft-shell crab with wasabi mayonnaise. The flavor was so unique and delicious that I’d definitely come back just for this. Another 10/10.

The jumbo tiger prawn followed — juicy, perfectly cooked, and simply amazing. 10/10 again.

For dessert, I had ice cream with pecan pie and sliced banana — the perfect sweet ending. 10/10.

Overall, I’ll absolutely be returning here on my next trip to London, and I’ll be recommending this place to all my friends.

Service was very good (8/10). The waiter brought out the crab but forgot the cutlery — apart from that, everything was excellent.

This has to be one of my favourite restaurants. From when you enter the restaurant you are made to feel special and welcomed. Our food was delicious and drinks…. Wow. Our waiter was very attentive, helpful and polite.

There is a great chilled vibe and you don’t feel rushed or as if you’re being hounded.

Did I mention the food is amazing.

You have to try the soft shell crab!!!! 10/10

Despite we came early for dinner and had no reservation, the staff gratefully offered
a table and accommodated us. (However make a reservation because there was a large queue by the time we left)
All the drinks we ordered were quite impeccable, really balanced flavors and  mixing top notch ingredients.
Zuma is renowned for its excellent modern Japanese cuisine and did not disappoint at all. Well umami on the dishes, fresh seafood and detailed cooking (also plenty of vegetarian options)

venues.image_alt: Zuma London — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Machiya
