venues.description: Traditional Japanese cuisine — with decor to match — accompanied by cocktails, whiskeys and sakes.

reviews.text: Our server was so sweet and attentive; we loved chatting with her. She recommended a delicious sake. We had the beef udon, pork donburi, grilled chicken skewers, karagae, and miso aubergine. The aubergine was a bit sweet for my taste but everything else was 10/10.

A sweet little restaurant with wonderfully cheerful staff who took care of us the whole time! We were early for our reservation which wasn't a problem - and despite a few other people already present, food was served piping hot and surprisingly quickly, especially as we ordered a mix of one main and lots of small plates together. The tonkatsu and agedashi tofu were highlights in particular - but the desserts and coffee we had were also fantastic, espwcially the matcha mille crepe. We'll be back next time we're in London! 😊

An amazing Japanese restaurant in the heart of London. The location was perfect. Just a few minutes away from Leicester square. My local friends took me there. The place is small and cozy. The chicken katsu was delicious, and the same goes for the meatballs. The service was quick and excellent, the price was great for the value.

venues.name: Kanpai Classic Soho
venues.description: Kanpai Classic Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Kanpai Classic Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Great restaurant in the heart of Soho with amazing food and experienced servers who are ready to educate you on all things Wagyu!

So many different cuts and a good selection of dishes and wines, the only thing that would have made this place more ‘fine dining’ is the decor (which looks a little cheap with low quality materials and scratched dark floors etc) and the atmosphere was rather lacking.

Otherwise a great experience and a hot spot for those with expense accounts and paid-for lunch meetings due to the price point and meat-heavy menu.

Overall a bit skeptical on this place. Is it fine dining? Is it fast casual dining? I went there and they seated us right on front of restaurant. Air-conditioning blaring on us. Asked to change direction and that helped, but the manager found this request challenging I had to ask twice. The beef tongue was good, and the rib eye fingers were good. Just not 5 star overall. Sorry can't be overly excited. The staff were pleasant - but did not have the details required on each dish to live up to the marketing of this place.

Honestly, this was the best meal I’ve had in London! We went for the full set menu and enjoyed fresh sushi, oysters, sea urchin, caviar, and an incredible meat selection. The wagyu was outstanding—tender, flavorful, and simply melted in my mouth. Each dish was prepared right in front of us by the staff and paired with unique sauces and sides that elevated the flavors even more. Highly recommended!

venues.name: SUSHISAMBA London
venues.description: Creative Japanese & Latin American sushi in contemporary surroundings, plus cocktails.

reviews.text:
This was my second visit, and it was just as amazing as the first! Located on the 38th floor, the views are incredible, and the whole atmosphere feels special. The service is top-notch — the staff are always so friendly and helpful, really making you feel looked after.

The food is outstanding — the sea bass, the sushi, everything was absolutely on point. It’s one of those places where every dish tastes fresh and full of flavour. Definitely one of my favourite spots for a treat meal!

We went for an early dinner, the food was amazing. We ordered tiger makki samba roll, pork rib robata and kobe gyoza. Amazing drinks collection and our service was very welcoming!!! We reserved samba room, and seated facing the window! It was an experience next time we would probably choose the restaurant! Loved it! Definitely would visit again!!

From the moment we stepped in, the ambience, the views were absolutely spectacular…the kind that make you stop and just take it all in. The whole vibe of the restaurant felt so vibrant and elevated, yet cozy and welcoming at the same time.

The staff were so friendly, attentive, and made sure we were well taken care of all night. The food? Incredible. I had the ribs, and they were so good — tender, flavorful, just perfect. I also tried this sweet potato baked dish and some sweet corn on the side, and everything was delicious. You can tell a lot of care goes into every single plate. It’s one of those spots that leaves you smiling long after you’ve left. Definitely a must-visit when in London!

venues.image_alt: SUSHISAMBA London — japanese restaurant in Central London

venues.name: OITA Soho
venues.description: OITA Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, OITA Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: This is a popular place and best to make a booking. Came on a Friday evening and it is packed with several sittings. For starters, the Takoyaki was great. We shared the salmon lovers roll. Also had the Salmon Sashimi don and Ikura don. All the seafood was fresh and large portions. Service was prompt.

We popped into OITA for lunch and left seriously impressed. The food was fresh, bold, and full of flavour — and the service was super quick too

The takoyaki was a total standout — crispy on the outside, soft and gooey inside, topped with a rich umami sauce and dancing bonito flakes. Comforting, savoury, and genuinely some of the best we’ve had.

The Fire Dragon Roll was just as good — warm, spicy, and perfectly crisp with a great balance of texture and flavour. Definitely something we’d order again.

We also had the kakuni ramen — the broth was rich and satisfying, though the pork belly was a bit firmer than expected. Still a solid, hearty bowl.

To drink, we tried a piña colada and a raspberry mojito — both super refreshing and well-made, the perfect finishing touch to a really enjoyable lunch.

@brownsugaaaa

This place is perfect. Very nice interior design and helpful staff (especially Mrs. Joanna, who has made our visit a wonderful experience, thank you!).
We ordered some sushi and fried chicken, it was really tasty. The waiting time was short and the quality of the dishes high.
We highly recommend and surely come back during next trip to London.

venues.image_alt: OITA Soho — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Eat Tokyo (Soho)
venues.description: Small Japanese eatery with no-frills decor serving sushi and bento boxes, plus sharing platters.
venues.address: 16 Old Compton St, London W1D 4TL, UK

reviews.text:
INCREDIBLE food experience!
Great value for money - good portions (it is hard now day to find a sushi restaurant with his prices!!) 100% worth the wait.
It is very popular within locals, might suggest to prepare yourselves for a queue (even tho, depending on the days, it is quite fast).

Food 12 out of 10! (Sushi speaking 🤓)

There was a queue outside and I thought it was just another gimmick BUT the food was really nice, sushi to be exact. Nice place to dine as a group, date or on your own. There was a group of 8 and the bill came to £37 (alcohol included). I recommend booking a reservation to avoid the long line.

Perfect spot to come with friends! The sushi is lovely and the portions for the Chicken Katsu Curry were very big for the price (regular on the left, large on the right). We are always welcomed by the lovely manager who is so friendly and accommodating 💖 It can get a little busy at times but so far I have been lucky, will definitely be back again soon! 🫶🏼

venues.name: Sanjugo Victoria
venues.description: Sanjugo Victoria is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Sanjugo Victoria provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 44 Hugh St, Pimlico, London SW1V 4EP, UK

reviews.text:
You are absolutely brilliant!

I’ve been trying Japanese restaurant in this country and many others and you are one of the greatest no doubt. We tried many dishes and they were all outstanding.

From the reservation (I book 1hr in advance), to the service, the INCREDIBLE FOOD, the ambience, etc… NEVER CHANGE!

I will be back, over and over and over again as this amazing place is local and just discovered now! Thank you for everything and please keep up the good work 🙏🏻
What a hidden gem! I walked in on a Friday evening and was pleasantly surprised to find a seat available. The food was delicious and reasonably priced. Highly recommend!
We visited for the first time tonight and we had a great time. The food was excellent and Carla, our waitress was very kind and made our dinner perfect. Thank you and we will be definitely back !

venues.name: Maru London
venues.description: Maru London is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Maru London provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Wonderful dining experience with outstanding hospitality and delicious food. The staff are so friendly and personable whilst maintaining a professional level of service and the style of food really emphasises the qualities of each ingredient. Watching the preparation is also a fascinating and makes this a really fun evening. We also enjoyed having a tea pairing option (must be ordered in advance) which complemented the food really well.

We had an amazing Omakase experience here! The ingredients were super fresh and everything tasted delicious. There were 20 courses in total, so we were really full by the end. The chef was not only skilled but also very friendly (and good-looking!). Highly recommended!

Incredible omakase experience! The best in London for us and it took us right back to some great places we experienced in Japan. The chefs were so amazing and so was the rest of the staff and the courses were fantastic. It felt very intimate and special.

venues.image_alt: Maru London — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: High Yaki
venues.description: High Yaki is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, High Yaki provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: High Yaki, UNIT 13, 10 Newport Pl, London WC2H 7PR, UK
venues.vicinity: UNIT 13, High Yaki, 10 Newport Pl, London

reviews.text:
Had a mix of the bbq meats and sushi  - the scallop tataki and sea bass with black truffle rolls were standout, some of the best scallops were had.

Great stop for some quality food, quick service, well presented, gorgeous interior.

Only con: some of the bbq meats were a little chewy but may have just been a bad cut, and the salmon was a little over cooked.

They also have some great lunch deals where you can get massive portions for around £20 each.

High Yaki was amazing! It’s the best Japanese BBQ we’ve tried in London so far. It’s a lot of fun to cook your own food on the grill and everything we ordered was so tasty. We ordered the 12 kinds of beef, you get so much variety in one order and the meat is so tender - and they also include chicken, seafood and pork too! We also got the sushi variety, it was excellent quality. 10/10 would recommend

I had such a great experience at this Japanese restaurant in Chinatown. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, with a nice mix of traditional Japanese style and modern design. The staff were friendly and attentive, always ready to recommend dishes and explain the menu.

The food was the real highlight—fresh sashimi that melted in the mouth, creative sushi rolls with balanced flavors, and a bowl of ramen that was rich, flavorful, and comforting. Every dish was carefully prepared and beautifully presented, showing the chefs’ attention to detail.

Considering the quality and location, the prices were very reasonable. Overall, it’s a fantastic spot for anyone who loves authentic Japanese food. I’ll definitely be coming back!

venues.name: Shack-Fuyu Soho
venues.description: Izakaya-style dining for Japanese comfort food in a relaxed, bi-level setting with a counter bar.
venues.address: 14A Old Compton St, London W1D 4TJ, UK

reviews.text: Went for lunch on a Saturday....the Express menu is good value for money. You can't substitute items on there and pay the difference. (I wanted to try their prawn toast). The tuna taco was a great shout. The salmon was also really good. Dessert outdid my expectations. Would recommend a visit!

We were excited to finally try Shack-Fuyu after hearing great things. We booked in advance, and it was packed when we arrived.

Between us, we shared:
Izakaya - tenderstem broccoli, edamame, wagyu beef tataki, crispy fried squid, Okonomiyaki prawn toast
Raw - seared salmon sashimi
Hot Stone - sukiyaki wagyu beef, pulled lamb
Robata - grilled salmon fillet
Dessert - kinako French toast

The salmon dishes were the standouts - perfectly cooked and full of flavour. I’m more of a savoury person, but even I loved the French toast. The broccoli and lamb were also really solid picks. Overall, the food was good.

Unfortunately, the experience let it down. We were seated next to a loud table who arrived after us but were served first, and they spent the evening shouting across the table. Our drinks took 25 minutes to arrive, and we had to ask multiple times - even though we could see them sitting at the bar. We were also served the wrong dishes more than once and had to chase missing items. At the end, we were even given the wrong bill.

I get that it was busy, but the service felt chaotic throughout, with no apology or effort to make up for it.

Glad we tried it, but I probably wouldn’t go back. For the price, we expected a better overall experience.

—

Edit: despite a comment on this review asking me to get directly in touch i’ve since emailed the provided address and received no response

Great selection of menu items, we were pleasantly surprised by the serving sizes and flavour profile. The French toast and matcha ice cream is a must have for dessert. The Shack’s spritz was a very nice Japanese take on a classic cocktail. Perfect for a nice warm Summer’s day. The quality of the service was superb, the staff were very friendly.

venues.name: Hot Stone London
venues.description: Relaxed Japanese meat outfit where diners can cook their own high-end steak on a hot volcanic stone.

reviews.text:
We had a wonderful dining experience at Hot Stone in London. The menu offered a great selection — we ordered mocktails, salmon sushi to start, followed by grilled sea bass with sesame spinach and steamed rice, and grilled teriyaki salmon with rice and miso soup. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavour. Cherry on top was everything was halal.

The service was attentive and the ambiance was refined yet welcoming, making it an ideal spot for a relaxed evening. The only minor drawback was that the portion sizes were quite small, but the overall quality of the food and dining experience more than compensated for it. Highly recommended for anyone looking for elegant Japanese cuisine in London.

The sushi here was good but the hot stone experience not so much. They often have discount offers like 80% off summer Wagyu deal for 29.95£/ person but in my opinion it is only worth that much really and definitely not worth full price.
Olive fed British wagyu isn’t good.

Portions here are very small and service is unfortunately although friendly enough not very efficient.

The ventilation system of the restaurant is also insufficient therefore the alarm can go off frequently.

I would say if you have a discount voucher yes why not give hotstone a try but if you are planning to visit for full price I would stay away from it.

Food was amazing. The plates of sushi might have been one of the best things I have tasted. We did the 5 course sushi tasting menu for £30pp was very much worth the money. We upgraded to have drinks alongside it which was worth it for the experience. The staff were very nice and friendly. The sushi bar is right by the door and in the form of a counter. We got the 450 degree hot plate included which was a really fun experience. Would definitely come back!!

venues.name: SUSHINOEN
venues.description: Stylish modern dining room with kimono-clad staff, serving classic and modern fusion dishes.
venues.address: 2 White Church Ln, London E1 7QR, UK

reviews.text: As a Japanese, I was impressed by the quality of the food as well as the interior design! Really beautiful restaurant with so many staple Japanese food options😍 all the servers are so lovely, especially Haruki-san! We got some tempura, karaage for starters and makis for the main. The volcano maki and aldgate roll were their highest recommendation and did not disappoint! Their matcha crepe cake was insane! Best I’ve had outside Japan! Also get the Kirin beer on tap, it’s so good! Highly recommend this place 😍
Really amazing food and service! The atmosphere was gorgeous and overall 10/10 experience. It felt very authentic as well! Would definitely come back 🍱🍣 really good cocktails as well

The restaurant was filled with Japanese vibe and the food was perfect! I ordered a sea bass and it was perfectly cooked and the presentation was amazing! We also had the grilled aubergine with miso paste, which was unique and satisfying. Highly recommend!

venues.image_alt: SUSHINOEN — japanese restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Abeno
venues.description: Simple Japanese restaurant specialising in savoury pancakes, where tables have embedded hotplates.
venues.vicinity: The Atlantis Bookshop, 47 Museum St, London

reviews.text: I've not had okonomiyaki since I went to Japan years ago when I was vegetarian. I was so excited when I found this place that does vegan okonomiyaki! And it did not disappoint! They have a vegan set with some sides, the okonomiyaki and miso soup; all great. They also had plenty of vegetarian options. Everyone (including meat eaters) thoroughly enjoyed their food. All staff were really friendly and helpful. They even had vegan dessert. Fab it's all cooked in front of you like in Japan, staff were very cautious to keep everything separate so my vegan one didn't touch the meat/veggie ones etc.  Lovely experience. I would recommend and return.

From the moment you enter, Abeno feels like stepping into a cozy, intimate corner of Japan,tucked just off Museum Street near the British Museum. Each table has a built-in teppan (hot plate) on which your okonomiyaki (Japanese savoury pancake) is cooked right before your eyes. Watching the batter, ingredients, and sauces meld on the grill is part of the fun, it turns your meal into a mini performance. The staff are warm, friendly, and helpful,they take time to explain the menu and grilling process, especially if it’s your first time. You’ll likely spend around £25 per head (excluding drinks)

Absolutely delicious okonomiyaki! The flavours instantly took us back to our trip to Japan. We tried two — the tofu kimchi and one recommended by our server — along with omsoba, and everything was fantastic. The staff were so warm and welcoming, and our host made the evening extra special by chatting with us and explaining the dishes. We had high expectations when we sought this place out, and it truly delivered. A perfect spot to celebrate our anniversary — we left so happy and content with the amazing food!

venues.name: Sanjugo Shoreditch
venues.description: Classic & contemporary sushi in a cozy space with sushi bar seating & a skylight-inspired ceiling.
venues.address: 13-15 Great Eastern St, London EC2A 3EJ, UK

reviews.text: A week day first time visit to Sanjugo, we arrived slightly earlier and were were seated down. The Menus where presented and very much like coffee table books, clear and well presented. We decided and ordered our dishes and drinks. They came out quickly and the food was fine. The only comment was that my dish Chicken Katsu Curry with Rice wasnt hot as I had wished, but it was fine. Everything else was well presented and tasty and met our expectations. I would say the food was fine, but again, London has multiple eateries that offer very much the same dishes at a similar price point. If you are in the area, them drop on in and give it a try. It is close to City of London and does a lot of the City folks as well as well as the Shoreditch Tech crowd. Enjoy, a nice eating experience.

From start to finish this was an outstanding meal. The wagyu was incredibly tender and flavorful, melt in your mouth, while the Hiramasa salad was fresh and vibrant. We sampled many items from the tasting menu and every course was beautifully presented and utterly delicious. Highly recommended.

It was a good experience dining at Sanjugo. Customer service was great. Staff were attentive and they kept refilling our tea cups without us needing to ask. A special mention to the slim Chinese lady who brought us to our table and the young Japanese Guy from Mie! They even Brought out a complimentary dessert knowing it was my birthday. It was much appreciated 🍰😊. Food was needlessly to say very good also. Flavourful, presented well and value for money. We will be back!!

venues.name: Koya Japanese Restaurant Soho
venues.description: Simple, cafe-style Japanese for udon noodles and small plates served at communal tables.
venues.vicinity: Arts Theatre Club, 50 Frith St, London

reviews.text:
I think there was only counter seating inside and two tables outside. I was trying to rest my tired stomach after a recent disordered diet (pre-trip binge eating) and needed some real Japanese food, so I think I was right to come here.
I ordered mini udon soup.
The soup was light in color and flavorful.It was very tasty and warmed my body and soul.

Koya is a small Japanese spot tucked away in the heart of Soho, offering chef/ kitchen counter seating for around 20 people.

The atmosphere is casual, and they open early, though the menu before 12pm is quite limited—mainly breakfast items and a small selection of udon dishes.Three chefs were working behind the counter during my visit.

I ordered the curry udon with grilled vegetables. Unfortunately, the dish was underwhelming. The vegetables—okra, fennel, aubergine, spring onion shoots—were fibrous, sparse, and didn’t add much to the plate. The curry sauce was overly thick and starchy, lacking balance. The portion of noodles was Over-generous almost turning it into a dish filler, but it felt mismatched with the meagre amount of vegetables.

Service left a lot to be desired. Food was handed over the counter without much interaction, and one of the waiters repeatedly brushed against me without a single apology. I eventually had to ask for the service charge to be removed.

Overall, it was a disappointing visit. The food was below average, and its was overpriced and poor value. The lack of basic ingredients—especially vegetables, which are inexpensive—felt careless. I won’t be returning or recommending Koya.

Very popular. Some of the udon noodles were a little bland, but I think that’s authentic.
Belly pork was fantastic.
Service was excellent.
Worth another try n

venues.name: Hanasaki Japanese Restaurant
venues.description: Hanasaki Japanese Restaurant is a japanese restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Hanasaki Japanese Restaurant provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine japanese flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: We really love the food here. I think I would rate grilled wagyu beef and king prawn, seared toro signature sushi, soft shell crab signature sushi, truffle beef tataki are the top in London. Sooooooo good. yellow tail, grilled chicken and wagyu beef tongue also nice

An absolute gem! Having spent a lot of time in Japan, I'm always on the hunt for truly authentic Japanese food in London, and Hanasaki completely blew me away. The sushi and sashimi are incredibly fresh, a testament to their high standards. Every dish is crafted with impeccable attention to detail, from the perfect slice of fish to the beautiful presentation. If you're a purist who appreciates genuine Japanese cuisine, do yourself a favor and visit Hanasaki. It's the real deal.

This sushi restaurant offers incredibly fresh, high-quality ingredients. The atmosphere is pleasant and inviting, making for a relaxing dining experience. The service was also excellent; attentive and friendly. I would highly recommend this place for anyone looking for delicious sushi. It's definitely worth a visit.

venues.name: Sanjugo Angel
venues.description: Sushi, sashimi, bao buns, donburi & grilled fish offered in an unassuming Japanese restaurant.

reviews.text: The food was delicious here, every item we ordered had a distinct taste. I was fortunate that they allowed me to make some changes to the sets, so I'm very happy with the food. The staff were also really kind and explained the menu or recommendations well. I was a little disappointed in the restaurant decor itself. It seemed like a place that needs a decor revamp, a bit of love and excitement to go into it. I would still recommend, but I think it could be more high end. Great for casual dining.

Visited on 13 September and had a very disappointing experience.

Food was average, but the oyster tempura was terrible. Overly salty, soggy, and clearly fried from frozen.

Service was even worse. We arrived shortly after opening with only one other table occupied but were seated beside the stairs to the toilets at an awkward two-person table. When we asked to move, the male staff refused, claiming all other tables were reserved, even though most stayed empty throughout our meal. He was also unnecessarily rude when I briefly took a phone call.

Thankfully, a female staff member later served us and was polite, but the overall experience remained unpleasant. After placing our order, closer to half past, we noticed that most tables were still empty and asked again to move to a better table, but she also refused, saying they were reserved. It was extremely distracting to have staff constantly walking up and down the nearby stairs during our meal. Several “reserved” tables were later given to walk-ins or remained empty.

All this happened within just 45 minutes of our stay. This was my companion’s first meal after arriving in the UK, and it left a very poor impression. We were very mad at the poor service, and this was no way to treat customers. Our first and last visit to Sanjugo.

Overall:

Food: Japanese Sushi

What I liked:

• Delicious food overall
• Great presentation
• Lovely service

What I didn’t like:

• Price point is simply too high and not ‘reasonable’
• Decor was quite tired and not commensurate to what you’re spending
• Tempura batter was too heavy

Do I recommend going? YES
Will I go again? YES
Was it good value? NO
Price Point: $$

venues.name: NIJŪ
venues.description: NIJŪ is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.5-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, NIJŪ provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
I’ve had many opportunities to try different styles of Japanese cuisine, from traditional to modern, and dining at NIJŪ was definitely an interesting experience. The customer service was excellent, and the course menu we tried had some good dishes. However, there didn’t seem to be any real connection between each course — it felt as though each dish was created by a different chef who hadn’t spoken to the others.

The dessert was phenomenal, but again, it didn’t match or flow naturally with the rest of the meal. Overall, it was worth trying once, but I wouldn’t return.

Unfortunately, this time the experience really fell short of my expectations. The waiter was overly enthusiastic and kept hovering around my table, which made me feel uncomfortable, as if I were being watched the whole time. The restaurant was also quite noisy.

To make matters worse, I even found hair in my food — which is unacceptable. Because of this, I don’t think I’ll ever come back.

I brought my friend here to celebrate her birthday, and it was my first visit after hearing so many great things. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly greeted by the reception team who kindly showed us to our table. The atmosphere was relaxed, welcoming, and had a lovely friendly vibe.

My friend is from Japan and has really missed authentic Japanese food, I was hoping to bring her a taste of home, and this place absolutely delivered. We both thoroughly enjoyed the food and the attentive service. The quality was outstanding, some of the best Japanese cuisine we’ve had in a long time.

We went for the 3-course meal and also tried a few dishes from the à la carte menu. Everything was beautifully presented and tasted incredible. I’d definitely come back and highly recommend it, especially if you’re a fan of sashimi!

Growing up in Japan, I’ve had a lot of opportunities to try different types of Japanese from authentic to modern - it was definitely a nice experience at NIJŪ. Customer service was excellent. Each menu was good (we did a course menu). However there is no connections between each menus as if they had different chefs for each menu and didn’t talk with each other.
Dessert was phenomenal but again, not matching with the other menus that led to the dessert menu.
Once is enough and won’t return again.

venues.name: ROKA Charlotte Street
venues.description: Premium sushi & grilled Japanese offerings in a refined, warmly furnished dining destination.

reviews.text: Had dinner twice this week. The first visit was almost perfect. The service was optimal from start to end. The second visit no to special. The food quality was good as always. I do remember back before the pandemic my husband and I loved it because the food was very creative and delicious. The food now days is good but no amazing. The second day the service felt rush and rude. One waiter kept pouring wine like a crazy mad man. I had to ask one the waiter to keep the rude one away from us. Another negative comment is that the noise level is overwhelming. Good luck and I hope they change the menu and soften their environment as it’s too harsh.

What a gem. We sat at the counter which gave us great views of their open kitchen so we could watch the chefs grilling. The service was prompt, and attentive. We ordered the £38 theater menu and everything was delicious and filling. The lemon chicken was some of the most tender and juiciest chickens I’ve ever had, and their dark chocolate and green tea pudding with crunchy jivara, pear ice cream for dessert was incredible.

We would 100% recommend to anyone traveling to London for a great meal and fun and lively area in the city

Simply beautiful and exquisite.
We had the premium tasting menu for four people, plus additional dishes for a vegetarian guest — and every single plate was a work of art. The presentation was stunning, and the flavours were perfectly balanced throughout. From the sushi and hot dishes to the desserts, everything was truly exceptional. We couldn’t find a single fault. There was also plenty of food, leaving us more than satisfied. A memorable dining experience from start to finish!

venues.name: Bone Daddies Soho
venues.description: Ramen bar with an old-school rock soundtrack, serving creative twists on Japanese fare, plus drinks.

reviews.text: We had SUCH a great time at Bone Daddies in Soho, definitely one of our favorite stops for a bite during my family’s trip to London. The food was amazing, but Ryan really made the experience a memorable one. We were a party of 8 and were not able to be seated right away, so he served us drinks while we waited outside and looked over the menu, checked on us often, and we really enjoyed chatting with him. All of the bao buns were delicious (and huge) but the crispy duck ones were the family fave. The Ramen was superb! The spicier ones definitely have a kick, but the flavor was so good even someone like myself who can’t do much spice finished every last drop. We did not have room for dessert, but the hot sake was the perfect way to end the meal. Would love to return whenever we make it back for a visit!

I got the crab tonkatsu ramen. It was tasty.
I liked the delicious broth and crispy-ish crab.
Service was fine.
The restaurant was clean and a bit quiet as I went on a week night.
Will visit again
One of the best Thai places I've eaten at in ages. Would 100% recomend to anyone. They also play great music

venues.name: YiQi
venues.description: YiQi is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, YiQi provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: The food was amazing. The flavour and the portion are good and value for money. The signature wing taste amazing with honey glaze and charcoal on the wings. The crab curry with steam rice was top notch. Would always recommend this place to have a good and flavour Asian cuisine. BOBY service was attentive and caring. Keep up guys. Top class

Chill yuzi Crab: SO good! The sauce is this amazing tangy, micro-spicy, refreshing masterpiece. AND it came with little buns to mop it up (genius!)The crab was massive – my friend and I were huffing and puffing for ages!
Sambal Seafood Fried Rice: Huge portion with whole prawns and squid rings.
Nyonya Lemongrass Grilled Chicken: Every piece was crackling crispy outside and then – BAM – super juicy inside. The green chili sauce made it even fresher.
King Oyster Mushroom Salad: Grilled mushrooms, a zesty sweet-and-sour dressing, and pomelo bits.
Thai Iced Tea: It wasn't sickly sweet! Friends, for a Thai tea born in the UK, not being sweet means it was born to be a good milk tea! The Tamarind Plum drink is for all my sour-loving friends.
Service: Impeccable. It felt just like the thoughtful service back home – bibs for the crab, frequent plate changes, hot towels. The manager says they roll out new dishes almost every month. I need to come back weekly to keep up!

I can’t find one bad thing to say about the quality or taste of the food. We randomly walked into this place, and we’re so glad we did—everything was excellent. The only miss for us was the drinks (we tried the tamarind mojitos and the flavor just wasn’t great). Other than that, a solid 10/10. Highly recommend if you’re in Chinatown, London.

venues.image_alt: YiQi — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Tattu London
venues.description: Chic, spacious restaurant turning out sophisticated, contemporary takes on Cantonese classics.
venues.address: The Now Building Rooftop, Outernet, Denmark St, London WC2H 0LA, UK
venues.vicinity: The Now Building Rooftop, Outernet, Denmark St, London

reviews.text: We have been to Tattu Manchester and we couldn’t pass the opportunity to visit Tattu London. The food is simply extraordinary! Mouthwatering and exceptional. Every dish better than the previous. We especially liked the starters like wagyu beef dumplings, mushroom rolls or pork bao buns. Caramel soy beef was exquisite. So tender and juicy. Our server, Alex, was really friendly and he made our night even better. The restaurant is very good at adjusting for allergies which we appreciate. The decor is beautiful and stylish. We will definitely come back!

Celebrated my husband’s birthday at Tattu. They booked us an amazing table with window to ceiling views. The ambiance and aesthetics were beautiful and cozy and the food was absolutely delicious. Funny enough we were actually advised we ordered too much food but we polished our plates nonetheless lol. Our waiter Peter was so lovely and gracious (he snapped some amazing photos of us!). They also surprised my husband with a complimentary birthday treat.

Overall a fantastic experience and would definitely recommend!

To make our overseas friend’s Birthday celebration memorable, particularly as this was their second visit to London, we selected the Tattu restaurant, which exceeded our expectations from the moment we entered through the eliminated tunnel and ascended the lift. We were warmly greeted at the lift with exceptional hospitality while proceeding  to our table.

The restaurant’s ambiance is equally impressive, featuring exquisite decor. And The live DJ playing great music in the background.

The culinary offerings were equally impressive, with each delectable dish presented artistically and bursting with incredible flavours. The service was smooth, friendly, and never rushed, the attentive waiter further contributed to the exceptional ambience of the evening.
They even brought out a surprise birthday treat for our friend. it was a lovely touch that made the evening more special.

I highly recommend dining at Tattu, a renowned restaurant celebrated for its exceptional cuisine, impeccable service, and memorable dining experience.

venues.name: Yauatcha Soho
venues.description: Top-of-the-range, contemporary Chinese dining with expertly-crafted dim-sum and handmade sweets.

reviews.text: I came here with a friend on a Friday evening and we had a great experience. The food was really tasty and well prepared. The staff let us know in advance that some dishes might take a bit longer since it was busy, which we really appreciated. In the end, the waiting time was actually very reasonable. The service was friendly, the atmosphere was welcoming, and everything came out very good. We’ll definitely be coming back!

Food quality is very high and tasty. I love their pickles and chill sauce very much. They offer cold press juice as well. Table staff was very friendly and attentive. I am sure I will visit again with friends. Highly recommend.

The food was absolutely delicious. Pricey for sure, but the portion sizes were generous enough and the quality of the food was outstanding. The staff were very professional and the venue itself was modern and clean, overall really great vibes as well!

venues.name: The Duck and Rice
venues.description: Stylish British pub with copper beer tanks and upstairs dining room serving elevated Chinese dishes.

reviews.text:
My girlfriend and I visited The Duck and Rice ahead of my birthday and it honestly couldn’t have been better. The food was absolutely delicious, we shared sweet and sour chicken, chicken chow mein, bao buns and venison pastries, and every single dish was so tasty.  You could really tell the quality of the ingredients and the care that went into the cooking.

A big shoutout has to go to our server, Hannah. She was so friendly, attentive without ever being overbearing, and genuinely made the whole evening feel special. It’s rare to come across service that feels that personal, and it honestly made all the difference.

I have a peanut allergy, so I have to be careful eating out particularly with Chinese food, but Hannah handled it brilliantly. She was knowledgeable, reassuring, and made me feel completely at ease, which meant I could just relax and enjoy the meal.

The place itself is lovely and inviting, and seems like a great place for a casual lunch or a more formal dinner.

The combination of amazing food, a lovely atmosphere, and such thoughtful service made this the perfect place to celebrate. We left already talking about what we’ll order next time.

Came here for dinner before a West End show. We were a bit early for our reservation, so grabbed a few drinks at the bar before our table was ready. For 3 people we ordered prawn chips , shumai, and XLB to start; then assam chilli king prawn (it is extremely spicy- fair warning!), crispy aromatic duck (quarter), pak choi with garlic, and Singapore fried noodle as mains.

Food arrived fairly quickly and everything was fantastic. They swapped our initial appetizer plates for clean plates when the mains came out. They present the crispy duck to you whole, then return with it shredded (with the bone on the plate) so you dive right into it more easily.

If I was local I'd probably make it a habit to do pre-show dinner here regularly. Everything was great!

I went on vacation with my family to London this summer, and this was a great place to dine at considering the numerous amount of restaurants nearby. The seating itself was a little tight, and I did see some customers struggle to get into them so as to not make contact with separate parties. Otherwise, the customer service was good, and the food arrived at a good time as well. My family and I enjoyed the duck the most, but everything else was delicious.

venues.name: Din Tai Fung Covent Garden
venues.description: Din Tai Fung Covent Garden is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.3-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Din Tai Fung Covent Garden provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: As always, fabulous food! I’ll highlight the green beans and the incomparable xiao long bao are just sublime. This place had the signature spicy sauce as well that was a huge hit with our table. The service was delightful, and I’ll give particular gratitude to our excellent waiter Eddy who was so attentive and patient with us! The only thing to note was that it was a bit loud and bustling and overly lit which wasn’t super conducive to the atmosphere of the place. That said, I’d listen to heavy metal music under the heat of the blazing sun just to have more of those dumplings so Din Tai Fung will always be a go-to for that heavenly food!

WE CAME HERE THREE TIMES IN 3 DAYS. Amber was our waitress and was phenomenal. The food was amazing and the atmosphere was even better. Had multiple dishes from the classic pork xiao long bao, to the noodles in spicy sauce and the prawn pork dumplings.

The food was great! Everything came out very fast and tasted really good. The noodles and dumplings were excellent. The Mai tai is delish. Our server Jenny was amazing! My mother kept saying how amazing she was (and she can be hard to please)!! Jenny was the perfect waitress - if i come back,
I will be asking for her! If

venues.name: Shanghai Family
venues.description: Soup dumplings & other Chinese specialties served in an informal locale with banquet space.
venues.address: 40 New Oxford St, London WC1A 1EP, UK

reviews.text: Authentic Shanghainese flavors right here in London! We tried crab roe soup dumplings, salted egg yolk shumai, sweet osmanthus lotus root, pork ribs with rice cakes, shepherd’s purse wontons, rice wine glutinous rice balls, and braised eggplant with minced pork. Every dish was comforting and packed with carbs in the best way possible. A must-visit if you crave real Shanghai comfort food.

If you're looking for the best xiaolongbao and pan-fried buns in London, this is the place to be!
The dumplings are perfectly juicy and flavorful, and the pan-fried buns are simply unforgettable.
On top of the amazing food, the service is outstanding - the staff are warm, attentive, and make you feel truly welcome. This is definitely a restaurant worth coming back to again and again!

Today in London I came across an amazing Chinese restaurant, and it was such a pleasant surprise! 😍
The braised pork belly had the perfect balance of fat and lean, melting in the mouth, and the sauce was absolutely divine with rice. The pineapple chicken was sweet and tangy, super appetizing, with perfectly tender chicken. The sweet osmanthus lotus root was both beautiful and delicious — soft, sweet slices of lotus root with the delicate fragrance of osmanthus, a refreshing treat. And the scallion oil noodles, though simple in appearance, were incredibly springy with a rich onion aroma — every bite was so satisfying! The four dishes complemented each other perfectly, with rich flavors, refreshing touches, and even a dessert-like finish. Such a delightful meal! 🥢

venues.name: Hutong
venues.description: Upscale spot with lanterns, silk curtains and city views, serving dim sum and northern Chinese fare.
venues.address: lvl 33, 31 St Thomas St, London SE1 9RY, UK

reviews.text:
It was a last minute booking as my other half couldn’t decide where he wanted to have dinner but since we’ve been at Hutong before, it was an excellent go to for any occasion.
Maybe I’m just getting too old but my boyfriend and I wasn’t impressed with the volume and choice of music.
Food and service were otherwise excellent as always. Also, always leave room for dessert!
Many thanks for making my boyfriend’s birthday a special one!

Celebrated our anniversary dinner here and it was worth it, 5 star on all categories. We were well assisted by Alan who’s not just a great staff but also a very good photographer, very attentive to our needs and details on all his service, the foods was great especially the duck, all I can say is wow, all the foods we got was amazing & freshly cooked, and the dessert was excellent, the best mango dessert I had so far in the UK, really tasted like sweet mango from Asia. And we were surprised with the free dessert to greet us for our special day, and they were also able to accommodate our request regarding the seating arrangement. Thank you to all the staffs! Really enjoyed our dinner from start to finish 😁

From getting to the shard to reaching the restaurant upstairs every single member of staff were so friendly. When we got to the restaurant our table was ready despite us being 10-15 minutes early, we were taken to our table and we had booked the skyline experience so was seated next to the window with a great view. The meal we had was amazing and the portion sizes were very fair, not too small and not too much. The duck was the best thing as they bring it out and cut it in front of your table for you to see. We was here celebrating a birthday and the staff even prepared a little happy birthday treat for my partner which was ever so kind. Well worth the money and I would come back here for sure

venues.image_alt: Hutong — international restaurant in Central London
