venues.description: Peacock London is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.5-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Peacock London provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, The Queen's Walk, London SE1 7PB, UK
venues.vicinity: County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, The Queen's Walk, London

reviews.text: We booked this Chinese restaurant for lunch which was located at the very prime tourist location.  Initially we thought it was a place mainly for tourists.  Upon arrival, we were led to a window table that had a great view of the Bog Ben.  They were having a summer special that a whole Peking Duck was at a reduced price from £118 to £68.  With no second thought, we ordered the duck right the way.  Along with the duck, we also ordered a few dim sum which were very nicely presented.  It's a pity they didn't cut up the duck in front of us.  Price wise, it was higher than those in Chinatown by 20-30% but it was still reasonable for this location.  Their wait staff were very friendly and helpful.  The two hours of dining went by quickly.  I  would love to try their abalone on my next visit.

Tasty dishes in pleasant atmosphere. Some of the tables have great view to Big Ben. Friendly and polite staff.
But; we were a group of 25 guests. The staff should take time to present the set menus and how to eat the dishes because not all the guests were familiar with Cantonese food. With such big group, they should have a lead staff to coordinate the tables. Pity!

Excellent authentic Chinese food, beautifully presented.   The location on the river opposite Westminster is great, from our table we looked out the window across the tanes and Westminster Bridge  and Big Ben and Parliament House. Price wise very reasonable, I have paid more for Pub Meals no where the quality of the food we ate here.Our favourite dish was the lamb with cumin.

venues.image_alt: Peacock London — international restaurant in Westminster

venues.name: Fatt Pundit
venues.description: Compact restaurant offering Indo-Chinese cuisine & drinks amid an informal atmosphere.

reviews.text:
I went to Fatt Pundit after seeing so many great reviews and was looking forward to it. The food was tasty and the wine went really well. Service was friendly and helpful too.

For me though, the whole experience felt more average than amazing. The atmosphere was fine but nothing special, and the toilets really need updating – they let the place down.

Overall, I’d say it was good but not quite what I was expecting. I’d probably go again, but with lower expectations next time.

As a fan of asian fusion cuisine I was surprised by how exquisitely good every dish looked and tasted while at a fairly adequate price. The ambience was relaxing and both Geet and Alex were very attentive towards our needs for refills, checking if we were pleased with the food and although it was a busy Friday, service was as fast as it was of top quality. Highly recommend for everyone that loves asian food and wishes to try Kolkata cuisine.

Fantastic service by the staff - Raj and Rutul, friendly and answered any questions we had. It was my birthday and I was surprised with a lovely candle and decoration on my desert. Food was 10/10
Will definitely be visiting again and recommending to others!!

venues.name: Shan Shui Social
venues.description: Shan Shui Social is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Shan Shui Social provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 14 Buckingham Palace Rd, London SW1W 0QP, UK

reviews.text:
I found this restaurant when searching for restaurants that are good for big groups. We were celebrating my dad’s 70th. When we went we learnt that it was newly opened, a few months old. We got a table downstairs and were the only ones there. Perfect.

The server was friendly and helpful. She recommended dishes to us and the food came quickly. Portion sizes are small which would have been perfect for sharing in smaller groups. (I say that because we usually dine with 3-4 people and some dishes are so large that trying food is difficult because of the large amount.) This time there were 12 of us so we just doubled up. Everything was delicious! I didn’t manage to photo everything because the children were hungry. The roast duck was so good. This is definitely kid-friendly food.

I really hope this restaurant stays. It’s a great addition to the neighborhood.

Incredible experience. One of the best meals I had in London! I cannot recommend this restaurant more.

Wonderful lunch selections and very helpful staff with questions and suggestions.

The pepper salted squid reminded me of my favorite childhood spot in Portland, Oregon. Brought back many good memories.

Every dish was flavorful and bright. I missed a couple dishes in photos because I couldn’t wait!!

Can’t wait to be back and visit again!

The serving speed is impressively fast—if you eat slowly, you might almost feel disrespectful to the food. Overall, this is one of the best Cantonese meals I’ve had in London recently.

💡 Drinks

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lion Eye: A lychee & longan mocktail, refreshing and lightly sweet without being overwhelming.

⭐⭐⭐ Elderflower Zest: Tastes like elderflower soda, non-alcoholic but with a hint of “boozy” character.

🍴 Dishes

⭐⭐⭐⭐ ¼ Roast Duck: Distinct from Beijing or Nanjing styles—Hong Kong–style roast with rich, slightly sweet soy-based flavor. Would be perfect with a plum sauce.

⭐⭐⭐ Salt & Pepper Squid: Tasty, but too much batter; the crunch overpowered the squid itself.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Salted Egg Yolk Prawns: Bold, savory flavor with plump prawns. Not too heavy—perfect for those who love salted egg dishes.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Chongqing Chili Chicken: More numbing (málà) than spicy, dry-fried style, very suitable for Cantonese palates while still keeping Sichuan flavor.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Fried Wontons: Absolute favorite. Thin, crispy skin with big, juicy shrimp inside. Paired with a sweet-spicy sauce—unmissable.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Custard Lava Buns: Sadly, the filling wasn’t runny since we didn’t eat them immediately, but still tasty with a more savory salted egg yolk filling (not the sweet custard type).

⭐⭐⭐ “Mouthwatering Chicken”: Decent, but not the highlight compared to other dishes. Still solid, but overshadowed.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Braised Wheat Gluten: First time having this in the UK—closer to frozen tofu in texture, pleasantly flavorful.

venues.name: Gold Mine
venues.description: No frills Chinese restaurant for signature roast duck and Cantonese specialities from classic menu.

reviews.text: Serves authentic chinese cuisines including Malaysian styled curry.  I heard about the Malaysian fried fish curry which is not on the menu.  I loved it.  The fried meat tofu is average. Great service for a very popular and busy restaurant. Very attentive staff.  Highly recommended for good quality food and excellent service.

Authentic Chinese restaurant ✨ — it really feels like a proper yum cha spot with the round tables 🪑 and traditional décor 🏮

🔸Service:
The waitress was very welcoming 😊 and even arranged the best seat for us. As usual in Chinese dining, we started with hot tea 🍵 (you can choose your own — we went with chamomile 🌼 this time).

🔸Food:

🍜 Fried Beef Noodles 🍜 – My favorite! The black bean sauce 🫘 mixed perfectly with the beef 🥩 and noodles, with onion 🧅 and sweet peppers 🫑 balancing it out.

🍤 Crystal Prawn Dumplings (Har Gow) 🍤– 4 pieces, fresh and delicious 🦐.

🥟 Scallop & Prawn Siu Mai 🥟 – 4 pieces, juicy and flavorful.

🥬 Steamed Veg & Meat Dumplings 🥬 – 3 pieces, loved the crystal wrapper with the veggie mix inside.

🍲 Beef Cheong Fun (Rice Roll) 🍲 – Soft rice roll drizzled with soy sauce, very tasty.

🍡 Dessert: Black Sesame Glutinous Rice Balls 🍡 – Soft, slightly chewy, with rich sesame filling 🖤. (Fun fact: black sesame is great for hair & skin ✨).

🔸Overall: A truly authentic Chinese dining experience 🥢, not the usual localized “British-Chinese.” Food, service, and atmosphere were all spot on 🌟. Definitely coming back, and highly recommend it to anyone who wants the real deal ✅.

I had passed by Gold Mine many times and noticed there always seemed to be a queue of people waiting outside during the day.  I checked online and found they are popular for their dim sum but also their roast meat.  I decided to pay them a visit as I love duck and pork dishes.

My first impression was good as they were happy for me to make a reservation for one person and were very responsive to my requests.

I had a three-course meal of Deep Fried Crispy Aromatic Duck, Roast Meat Rice (BBQ Pork and Crispy Pork) and Banana Fritters.  I had also planned to have the House Special Bean Curd but had no room after my main course.

All the dishes I had were delicious.  The duck was probably the best I have ever had.  It was crispy on the outside and the meat was not at all dry but succulent.  I had no problem finishing all the pancakes.  I asked for egg fried rice and it was well cooked, along with the two types of pork.  The pork meats were full of flavour but not overpowering.  The banana fritters were a great end to the meal.  Crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside.

The service was also very good.  The servers were attentive but not at all intrusive and I did not have to wait very long at all between courses.

One thing to note is that the restaurant was rather noisy and not the best place for a quiet or intimate meal.  I was glad that I had my noise cancelling headphones with me.  I would also recommend making a reservation, as it was very busy.

I definitely recommend Gold Mine if you fancy having Chinese cuisine, especially their roast meat dishes.  I hope to make another visit soon to try their dim sum, as it looks very good.

venues.name: Fatt Pundit
venues.description: Tapas-style Indo-Chinese specialties, fruit coolers & wine in a snug, industrial-chic space.

reviews.text: Had an excellent dinner here. Had to wait 20 min without reservation on a weekday night. Manisha provided top notch service once we were seated. Nice take on Indo Chinese cuisine, done with care. Food and service great, just one star removed on atmosphere as it is quite loud.

Arrived in London absolutely hangry, and Mervin was kind enough to squeeze us in. He truly saved the night! Their 4.9 rating is well deserved. The food was spectacular, the service just as impressive. My wife and I couldn’t get enough of the crispy spinach. And the lamb chops? Some of the best I’ve ever had, anywhere. Fatt Pundit absolutely lived up to the hype. Can’t wait to come back next time we’re in London!

Food was 10/10 and such great value for money.
If you need halal only then ask for the halal menu just so the experience is easier and clearly differentiated.

We tried the goat, beef and chicken momos they literally exploded in our mouths with flavour and juiciness. Our favourite was the beef. The sauces that went with them were delicious too.

The lamb chops were also amazing, they were thick and cooked and marinated to perfection.

We also got the ribeye dry red chilli, which was like a curry and stir fry and wow…probably some of the best saucy style beef I’ve tried. Cooked to perfection. Juicy, tender and melt in the mouth.

The Bombay chilli prawns were also amazing we ate that with the egg Szechuan fried rice. Everything was spiced to perfection, if you can’t hack chilli then maybe asked for a milder flavour. If you’re used to chillier food then it’s perfect. Probably a Nando’s level hot - extra hot as a comparison.

We also got a bing bread I think this was like a laccha paratha. This was so delicious you could taste the ghee and the crispy layers. I would happily eat this with some desi tea.

The most underwhelming item was the lollipop chicken and the sauce was just OK but it was still very fresh and delicious.

We also got the sizzling brownie and wow this was sooo delicious, with it being on a skillet the bottom of the brownie gets slightly chewy. It was just a perfect dessert simple but 10/10.

The service was also 10/10 alongside
the ambience and experience. The place had a calm and chill vibe. Even though it was extremely busy. The waiters and the managers carefully tended to all tables smoothly it was literally jammed from 5pm. You can tell the staff enjoy working there as they just vibe together.

I would definitely go again very soon to try the items I didn’t get to try.

Thank you!

BTW it’s like a 40 minute walk  from KGX.

venues.name: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine
venues.description: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine is a chinese restaurant located in London. With a 4.3-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine chinese flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Dined at this restaurant twice. First time was lunch dim sum which was amazing. Would easily say it's the best dim sum in London and that inspired me to go back for dinner, which was very good but not amazing.  Definitely recommend going there for dim sum.  Excellent service, something you would expect in a Michelin star restaurant. The atmosphere feels like a very luxury fine dining restaurant, very relaxed and calm but very attentive.
I've also had dim sum in their Guangzhou restaurant (Tianhui) and I would say the dim sum is better at London restaurant.

This is the best fine dining Chinese restaurant I've ever experienced. We tried the Peking duck, which we'd reserved in advance, accompanied by Burgundy red wine. The dumplings that came with it were also very good. I can't wait to come back.

We had the Imperial Treasure tasting menu and the food was exceptional! All of the dishes were outstanding! Our top three were the peking duck, black truffle lobster and the steak with garlic chips!
Our waiter Stephen was soo attentive and gave us some good tips on how to enhance our soup! We had such a wonderful time and we will be coming back

venues.image_alt: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine — chinese restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Pot and Rice
venues.description: Pot and Rice is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Pot and Rice provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
We had such a great experience at Pot and Rice! The service was excellent, especially from a waitress named Li. She speaks Cantonese and English, and was incredibly attentive—helping us choose dishes based on our group (me, my sister, and my aunt), our budget, and our preference for lighter flavors. She gave thoughtful recommendations, discouraged us from over-ordering, and patiently answered all our questions throughout the meal. Honestly, this is the kind of service that makes the service charge worth it.

🥤 Drinks
They offer an unlimited bubble tea deal for about £8 per person. The three of us ordered 8 drinks in total—every single one was delicious, no misses at all.

🍴 Food Highlights

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Claypot Rice with Chinese Sausage & Chicken: Classic Cantonese flavor with tender chicken and sweet, fragrant sausage. The crispy rice at the bottom was amazing once mixed with sauce (make sure not to leave the lid on too long, or it’ll get soggy). My aunt even said she wants to bring more relatives here just for this dish!

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Beef Udon: Fragrant XO sauce flavor, tender beef, and chewy udon noodles. Comforting and satisfying.

⭐⭐⭐ Braised Platter: Soy-braised chicken wings and tofu. Tasty and authentically Cantonese, but not a standout unless you’re specifically craving braised dishes.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Soft-Shell Crab Spring Roll: Wrapped in Vietnamese rice paper with fresh herbs and a touch of pomegranate. The crab roe was especially delicious—rich and flavorful.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Crab Roe Cheung Fun (Rice Noodle Rolls): Absolutely outstanding. Thin, silky rice rolls filled with popping crab roe, served with light soy sauce. The texture was perfect—tender yet bouncy, just like the ones I remember from childhood in Canton.

🫖 Extra note from my aunt: She usually avoids tea because of the strong flavor and sugar, but here every tea was balanced, not too sweet, and easy to enjoy—even for someone with high blood sugar.

Very good place! Service is polite and informative, and the food is some of the best I've had in London. Everything was brimming with flavour -- the smashed cucumber salad had such depth, the softshell crab summer rolls were delicious and light, and the prawn noodles were moreish.

It was far too hot outside for me to brave the hot rice dishes (currently 34c in London) but I will return on my next visit to London to give them a try. Splendid restaurant, highly recommended.

I recently had lunch at Pot and Rice, and it was an exceptional experience. The service was prompt and attentive, with friendly staff who ensured our needs were met throughout the meal. The food was delicious, with each dish showcasing great flavor and quality. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a midday meal. Overall, the combination of good service and excellent taste makes this place a must-visit for lunch or dinner. Yummy ^^  Bubble milk tea is my favourite.

venues.name: Min Jiang
venues.description: Swish, 10th-floor Chinese restaurant in a high-end hotel, with lofty views of Kensington Gardens.
venues.address: 2, 24 Kensington High St, London W8 4PT, UK
venues.vicinity: 2, Royal Garden Hotel, 24 Kensington High St, London

reviews.text:
Excellent fine Chinese dining.

Wide range of very tastey Chinese food. They're moderately priced and the service from entry to exit to tops.

There are some superb canopy type views of the city at night, which makes for a charming view of the city.

I've eaten there several times in recent years and the service is consistent and Excellent.

Try out their duck specialty, you'll enjoy it.

‼️book your Peking duck ‼️ Wonderful view and the food was really great.  We would have appreciated if the fact that we needed to make a reservation for Peking duck was advertised when we booked.  But the dishes we ordered in lieu were beautiful executed nonetheless.  The staff were lovely also - will come back again still!

More than average food for fair price, great location with amazing view.
The duck was better than average you can get in europe, the execution of the chef not so much. Doesnt say hello, doesnt explain anything, rushes to the table and starts cutting, leaves a lot of meat behind, which is then used to make 6 tiny bites. I wished he would just let ne debone the duck myself, thats how poor the execution was.

venues.image_alt: Min Jiang — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: House of Ming
venues.description: House of Ming is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.5-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, House of Ming provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Serving 2 difference halve and refried pecking duck, it was dry and no favouring even the duck skin isn’t crispy. The waiter said they make their own pecking duck pancake, we received factory made pancake .

I can taste the Honey roast pork char siu was frozen and reheat by microwave, It was dry and chewy.

£75 for a Lobster tails laid in giant lobster shell with the almost 70% butter I could not taste any lobster meat at all.

For Dim sum we have scallop and prawn har gao, it might be handmade but it usually comes with big pieces of scallop i guess I got a newborn. Har gao should be at least few pieces, we got some in finely chop.

It was a treat from my friend so I have to be polite and not to complaint . For the same price we paying in central london you can get much better quality and services.

Fried rice with xo sauce was nice not greasy but xo sauce should have dry scallop and spiciness.

Noodles with mushroom is slightly salty but it is the most decent food of that meal.

The waiters aren’t seem to know what are they serving and the ingredients. Foods aren’t serve as what we being told.

I was with a group of friends for a special event so I have to be polite and nice on that day.

My husband and I were staying at the Taj and as it was or 45th wedding anniversary thought we would have a nice meal. We chose House of Ming as we had heard good things about it, on arrival we were greeted warmly and showed to a lovely booth with curtains. Staff were attentive and the food was really nice, especially as we were vegetarian for that period, it was Navratri and we don't go vegetarian for the nine days. My husband (who isn't vegetarian normally) was also very impressed and as he's also a very good chef it's a huge relief when he finds the food excellent. We were given complimentary cocktails and a beautiful dessert in honour of our anniversary. Thank you to B. Prasad and everyone who works for House of Ming for making our evening extra special.

The service was lovely, the manager and all staff members were really kind. Celebrated a birthday and they bought out a mini cake and sang which was incredibly sweet. The staff went above and beyond to ensure we were taken care of and the food was delicious. Would recommend others try.

venues.image_alt: House of Ming — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Ye Ye Noodle & Dumpling
venues.description: Ye Ye Noodle & Dumpling is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Ye Ye Noodle & Dumpling provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: It’s a smaller place, which I really like. It feels cosy and welcoming, especially in winter. We ordered the juicy pork dumplings and the spicy beef dry noodles, and both were absolutely delicious. The flavours were spot on, good size portions, and we left completely full and happy. Such a lovely little spot. Highly recommend!

Came here for dinner on Tuesday night as we were craving for some grilled dumplings. The grilled dumplings were served piping-hot and we absolutely loved the soup inside the dumplings, which was really flavorful. The Fried Lotus Roots with Pork was amazing and definitely worth trying. Crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. £5.8 for 4 pieces was surely a deal.

The place was extremely busy during dinner time even on a random weekday, and we were only given 1-hr dining time which was a bit tight for the amount of food we ordered. But guess it was understandable as there were simply so many people queuing outside for a table.

We were in the area and wanted to.try somewhere new. I hadn't heard about YeYe before, but the reviews were extremely good considering there's over 1.8k!

All the food was cooked so well with a lot of flavours. The pork dumplings were the star - absolutely incredible. The beef is grass fed from Germany and you can really taste the difference.

Staff were helpful and friendly. The restaurant was packed, but not chaotic. It reminded me of the noodle houses you get in Asia.

Overall, I will be back over and over. If you like fresh dumplings and noodles, this is your place 🙌

venues.name: Gouqi
venues.description: Gouqi is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Gouqi provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Had lunch dim sum at Gouqi and it was amazing! The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully made – every dumpling was spot on. You can really taste the quality in each dish, and the variety was perfect for sharing. The restaurant itself has a nice vibe, elegant but still comfortable, so it doesn’t feel too formal. Service was super friendly and attentive, which made the experience even better. Honestly one of the best dim sum lunches I’ve had in a long time. Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for top-quality Chinese food in a great setting.

The best experience! The staff are amazing  so friendly and attentive and the cozy environment makes you feel right at home. The food is absolutely delicious! Their dishes  are packed with flavor, and if you love chicken, this is definitely the place to be  every chicken dish is cooked to perfection, juicy, and full of taste. Highly recommend it! And the most important part of the meal was dessert ❤️absolutely loving it

This restaurant was beyond expectations! The food was very well presented, good variety of dim sum, and exceptional service. The portions were bigger than we expected and we couldn't finish everything. We had the 3- course noodle set lunch (28£) and was well worth the price. We'll certainly be back to try the other menus!

venues.name: Meeting Noodles
venues.description: Meeting Noodles is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Meeting Noodles provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 35 Grays Inn Rd, London WC1X 8PG, UK

reviews.text:
This place doesn’t just serve authentic and delicious Cantonese food — the portions are huge! They’ve got everything: late-night snacks, BBQ, noodle soups, and dim sum 🍲🍢

The highlight? A super luxurious KTV private room that can fit up to 22 people! Even with a group of 10, there’s plenty of space — and the sound system is amazing 🎤

🔥 The KTV stays open until 6 AM, making it a true paradise for night owls!
The value for money is absolutely insane — you even get free KTV time when you dine here. It’s the perfect spot for London’s hardworking folks and students to hang out 🥂

👯‍♀️ Whether it’s a birthday party, friends’ gathering, or company event, this place is just perfect!

Wonderful and friendly service in a very clean cheerful restaurant. The food was wonderful and we enjoyed ourselves immensely. The noodles shredded chicken took us back to a fav dish we had when we first started dating 15 years ago! Thanks for a lovely meal.

Had such a fun dinner experience at Mian Mian Ju Dao!
The place serves a wide range of Cantonese, Sichuan, seafood and BBQ dishes, and honestly everything we tried was delicious.
The Seven Spice Spring Onion Beef Cubes were my absolute favourite — super tender and flavourful (I asked what the seven spices were, and the owner just smiled and said it’s their “secret recipe” 😂).

venues.name: Xi'an Impression London
venues.description: Simple Chinese restaurant specialising in Shan Xi street food like pork/beef burgers and noodles.

reviews.text: Food was nice but both the signature noodles and the tomato and egg dishes tasted pretty similar.

Small busy restaurant with tasty food, we ordered three plates and paid 50 pounds, not huge portions but enough to satisfy, the price was reasonable for Londoners but us Canadians get shafted, the noise level is very high with many people stuffed in a small space. Staff are friendly and quick and polite.

I tried the dumplings and their signature noodle dish with beef chunks. Whilst the dishes were good, I didn’t find the flavour particularly different from the standard dumplings and I found the noodle dish to be missing some punch - either the spiciness or umami flavour. The service is fast and it does satisfy dumpling and noodle craving and is a good place to visit if you are craving for these in the neighborhood.

venues.name: Speedboat Bar
venues.description: Speedboat Bar is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Speedboat Bar provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Oh my word. My husband and I came here with high expectations for our anniversary. Firstly, a sincere shoutout to the friendly and highly attentive waitstaff. We reserved in advance (which I recommend doing as it gets busy!) and they had actually read my booking notes. In the notes I mentioned I was pregnant and so they double checked I was happy with the preparation and ingredients of certain dishes. The menu leans towards the spicy and salty side, but at the same time is very fragrant and aromatic. Quite addictive really! I’ve seen viral videos of that Tom Yam deluxe noodle dish so obviously we had to get it. It was delicious, but to my surprise, my favourite dish was their Naem fried rice. It’s been about a week since our visit and I’m still licking my lips thinking about it. To top everything off, we got a surprise scoop of taro ice cream. How adorable is that? Lots of love to Speedboat. We’ll be back, and definitely before our next anniversary!

hyped up place for sure and while the interior lives up to the hype and certainly some of the dishes do they are unfortunately inconsistent and I don’t think pay attention to detail… possibly because it gets so busy. Don’t get me wrong it was nice and tasty but just a little inconsistent and not insane value. The rice was overcooked and actually clumped together which I wouldn’t expect from a Thai restaurant- especially when paying £4 extra.. the purple aubergines were really nice, tender and flavourful. However for £12.50 I got one long purple aubergine- eight pieces. Would’ve said id happily pay £9, as it wasn’t mind blowing but very very nice. Would’ve been nicer with better rice. Good spice level, even though we received warning it was actually perfect. Channah got crispy egg noodles with gravy pork and squid and was pleasantly surprised with two different types of squid and she said good value for the amount of squid, as she’d expect more pork and less squid but it was the other way round. The spice also could’ve been higher and she wanted more greens in the mix and garnish. She really enjoyed though and felt it was good value for central London £17. Staff are possibly a bit overworked and overwhelmed but they are all so lovely. Happy to have come but wouldn’t rush to come back.

Food and drinks were great!! I am obsessed with Tom yum mama noodles and regularly have the instant version at home so this boujee version was fantastic!! The fried rice was very flavoursome and even better with the sauces! Pour the beef tongue curry sauce on it and it’s even better! The pineapple pie was a nice way to end the meal

venues.image_alt: Speedboat Bar — international restaurant in Central London

venues.description: Platapian Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Platapian Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: 1st time to this Branch of Restaurant located in Greek Street. Came with friends for a get-together. Bowled over by the variety of dishes; perfect balance of seasoning delivering tantalising taste and all beautifully presented! Special mention for their unique Scallops starter! Loved their fantastic Cocktails, too! Do not hesitate to come try for yourselves! ThankYou too to Paul for his friendly and attentive service throughout the evening! Ps. Will be coming back but please fix the draughty front door!

What a wonderful place! Very zen and elegant place with lots of details! Food is incredible good! The scallop, papaya salad, and the clay pot rice are all amazing. Very fresh! You can really taste the food! Ploy is also helpful and super patient with us!! Definitely recommended!!!

Last night we had one of the most delicious meals we’ve ever had—not just in a Thai restaurant, but in any restaurant. The flavors were rich and authentic, the portions were generous, and the quality of the produce was outstanding.
Perfect for a romantic date night or a special celebration. We’ll definitely be back!

venues.name: Plaza Khao Gaeng
venues.description: Plaza Khao Gaeng is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Plaza Khao Gaeng provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 103-105 New Oxford St, London WC1A 1DB, UK

reviews.text:
My fave Thai restaurant in London!
I’ve been going here for the past three years and I love the fact that they always have a special menu that changes. It keeps the food exciting and different.

The flavours always burst in your mouth and I love spicy food too!

Truly authentic and amazing food!

The service was really good with helpful staff in making your decisions.

Truly a gem!

Was really impressed by the flavours of the dishes here. The roti bread and Morning Glory had a divine, delicate in flavour. The crust quails egg was good, but the accompanying sauce made it an excellent dish. The Massaman curry had rich flavours, and even though I didn’t sample the fried chicken dish, the other diner said that it was amazing. Many of the dishes do have a kick to them, so be mindful of that if you’re not good with hot food.

The staff were nice and attentive, they also treated us to some coconut pudding due to it being one of our parties birthday.

The only qualm I had was the fact that we were a party of three, sat at a table for two and it was quite cramped. I had to sit with my legs to the side and we couldn’t easily fit all our dishes on the table.

The food tastes really good and very authentic 🍽️ Portions are okay for the price. Service wasn’t the best, which does affect the overall experience, but would I return? Yes haha, I believe one fish can’t make the whole sea rotten ka!

venues.image_alt: Plaza Khao Gaeng — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Smoking Goat Shoreditch
venues.description: Cool, laid-back restaurant serving quirky dishes & drinks inspired by Bangkok’s late-night canteens.
venues.address: 64 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ, UK
venues.vicinity: Tea Building, 64 Shoreditch High St, London

reviews.text: Couldn’t leave a better review! The food and cocktails were absolutely delicious, everything we had was a must try - especially the wings, beef massaman and the mackerel. We sat at the bar in front of the kitchen, was so lovely to see all the staff getting along so well and the kiwi chef was so friendly and helpful. Special thanks to Jack who gave us great recommendations and looked after us! Can’t wait to come back soon

The fish sauce wings here are great, super sticky and crispy. They're quite expensive(~4£ each) and only sold as single wings but it is a whole wing; I would say these are a must try. They are pretty big. The crispy chicken skins were nice, but I think a dipping sauce with them would go a long way. Cocktails were good. Service was pretty slow, but overall would come back for the wings, they're very unique and some of the best in this style I've had.

I've heard for a long time about the quality of Smoking Goat, I finally had it yesterday and I already cant wait to go back! Food was absolutely delicious like 10/10 and the vibe was a nice cosy environment. It was very busy and a full restaurant throughout but not too busy to the point it affected our meal.

Special shoutout to Yasmin she made our time 12/10 due to her customer service and know how of the menu and recommendations. I asked her about what drinks she'd recommend and picked the perfect drink and she basically ended up curating our whole meal. The chill wing was one of the best chicken wings I've had all year down to the exquisite sauce. And the massaman beef cheek was to die for!! Also had a daikon salad which added another dimension and the squid was divine also.

She encouraged to try the grilled cockles which i was skeptical at first but as i love seafood and her assurance I wouldn't be disappointed and explained where in Wales they come from and how to enjoy them with the lovely sauce and im so glad we trusted her judgement, i can't wait to go back to try them again!!

5 star dining experience! Wish i could give them 6! Thanks again for everything Yasmin you are a superstar!!

venues.name: Kolae
venues.description: Kolae is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Kolae provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
I really enjoyed my visit over the weekend. I was very keen to try Kolae as it had been recommended by a friend and on the whole I was not disappointed.

We didn’t order a lot of the food on this occasion so I’d definitely like to go back and try some other dishes what we did have was incredibly flavourful and in some instances, very spicy,  the pepper chicken made me lose my voice. It was so spicy but so delicious. Luckily, our server recommended a cooling drink to soothe my throat.

I really liked the building and the place had a really nice vibe, although as is often the case, the toilets were a bit messy.

We were on the top floor and I don’t think there was a lift. I think we went up three flights of stairs to a smaller, lovely space, so do you bear that in mind when booking.

We felt rushed at the end but we did have a two hour booking limit. Another 15 mins would have been good.

Stand out was the kale, surprisingly, and the pork.

Recommended.

One of the best meals we've ever eaten. The lunchtime set menu is a brilliant deal, the prawns, butternut squash, fish curry and rice pudding dessert are all total world class.The guy from Alsace who looked after us was brilliant, friendly  helpful and kind. He did a brilliant job.One of the worlds best restaurants in my book, it was amazing, thanks for a lovely and memorable afternoon Kolae.

We had reservations for this very popular place near borough market. We ordered two curries and one salad for our meal. We ordered a wine and a beer. The prawn curry was super spicy which is fine as I like spicy but the curry was too thin and it was okay. We ordered a fish curry which was very good. The mango and cucumber salad was very good and so was the coconut sorbet. It was a good refreshing finish after the meal.

venues.image_alt: Kolae — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: AngloThai
venues.description: AngloThai is a thai restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, AngloThai provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine thai flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: They did something truly great with this restaurant. Incredibly gorgeous, delicious and balanced food. It’s definitively British food with Thai influence, not vice versa - very original and creative. Don’t think there was a bad dish here, I’d definitely recommend to NOT skip the supplement as that was one of the best bites. The curry as well as the oysters and sausage starter were additional standouts. I was literally cleaning off the plate with their homemade brioche. Even the cucumber broth amuse bouche was delectable. Only two dishes that didn’t wow me were the Thai tea dessert and the side of greens that was very very salty. Other than that this restaurant is exactly the type of cooking I’d love to see more of in London. Unfussy interior and service, very friendly and felt cozy but not rugged. Will definitely be returning!

This was one of the best tastings I have done in London. And at a very competitive price point. A couple highlights were the crab and caviar course and the bbq octopus. It may have been the best octopus I have ever had. The Thai spices were unique and fantastic across all the courses. They also had excellent ice cream in both of the dessert courses. The ambiance could be a bit more elevated, as it was quite tightly packed but the food makes it more than worth the visit!

Took my wife for her birthday dinner and we really enjoyed our meal. Every dish had a unique Asian spin that was flavorful and delicious. I usually don't like fish but all the fish dishes were spectacular. Can definitely see why they got their Michelin star! Staff were all very friendly and they gave us a great seta by the window as well as a beautiful dessert to celebrate the birthday. Thank you for such a memorable meal

venues.image_alt: AngloThai — thai restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Kiln
venues.description: Casual open kitchen cooking noodles & Thai-inspired dishes using wood-burning ovens and grills.

reviews.text:
Gonna go out on a limb here and say this place is just not worth the likely 45min+ wait and elevated price level. Both for the food and the experience. Food wasn’t terrible, but just not what I expected after such a long wait and the amount of hype around it. All starters were fine, but even for someone who loves and eats a lot of spice, the (presumably) Thai chilies overpowered many dishes. Skewers had nice flavor but quite fatty. Unfortunately all meats were similar, including the rump- flavor itself was nice. The one great dish that I’d happily eat again is the clay pot noodles - truly delicious. 140£~ for two people.

I think there’s a larger conversation to be had about the “reservation system” (non existent). While I can appreciate the no resi policy in a city where great restaurants are booked out in advance for months, I feel some adjustments are necessary. Not only are people waiting outside in droves, but they continue the “line” inside- the restaurant is incredibly cramped/small without people waiting for tables, but they cram people in behind the diners to keep the queue “shorter”. This makes the already loud environment even more hectic. That being said all staff was friendly, albeit understandably overwhelmed. If you can walk in without having to wait I think this is a fun place to try - just not if you have to stand around in the rain.

Kiln is amazing! The flavours are bold, the ingredients fresh, and every dish was delicious.

The service is excellent. Staff is very friendly and attentive. We even got there early on Saturday to queue before opening, so we didn’t have to wait, which made the experience even better. The atmosphere is cozy and lively, and the smoky charcoal cooking adds a really unique depth to the dishes. I’ll definitely come back when I miss the taste of home.

This was incredible - the highlight of our London food spots. We went on a Thursday at 7:30pm and it took about an hour to be seated (you can leave your name and number). The vibe of the upstairs is great with the open kitchen and bar - we were offered to sit downstairs but waited for the upstairs because of the ambience. All of the upstairs seating is at a bar so it’s best for parties of 2.

The dishes were strong. Very pork heavy menu. The highlights were the pork loin (the best pork dish I’ve ever had), jowl (the first bites were better than the last, which were chewy), sticky rice, and crab glass noodles. I didn’t know pork could be so good and the loin completely blew me away with how tender and tasty it was. They say it can take up to 45 minutes to cook so I’d recommend ordering it as soon as you’re seated.

Service was great with all the staff being friendly and attentive. They just get the ambience right - you feel like you’re at a trendy restaurant when eating here.

venues.name: Nua
venues.description: Nua is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Nua provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
A relatively new and nice modern Thai option in the area. The staff are really lovely from the moment you arrive and remain attentive throughout. The main menu is large and varied with photos to help aid any selection, but there’s also a reasonably priced lunch menu, offering either one or two courses from a concise range of options. From this menu, both the staters and main are served together on a single plate, presented well, and although not a massive portion is good for a lunch.

The pork skewers were delicious and a shame they only serve two, and the green curry was very tasty with a nice level of spice. The draught beer was a little slow to arrive but served ice cold which was great.

The decor and background music doesn’t give the most traditional or authentic atmosphere but fortunately everywhere is clean. I’ll certainly be returning and would recommend for a more unique independent offering.

Our group of four had a fantastic experience at Nua, enjoying a night of excellent Thai food. We started with the Nua Platter, which included Duck Spring Rolls, Chicken Satay, Steamed Thai Dim Sum, and Chargrilled Pork Skewers. A major positive is that they provide one of each item per person, avoiding the awkwardness of splitting dishes, something many other places don't get right. The accompanying sauces (satay, chilli and a hoisin-like sauce) were also spot on, adding extra depth to the starters.

For mains, we ordered a variety including the Pad Kra-Pao and Massaman Curry. Every dish was full of flavour: the pork was rich and juicy, the chicken was perfectly tender, and the boned-meat easily pulling away from the bone. The Sticky Rice and Jasmine Rice we had alongside complemented the mains beautifully.

Service throughout the meal was polite and courteous, though we did find it difficult to get attention when asking for the bill, waiting around 10 minutes.

Pricing is slightly on the higher end, but given the central London location and quality of the food, it felt reasonable enough.

Overall, Nua delivers delicious Thai food in a relaxed setting. A great choice for a treat or a special night out!

Overall the place was good. The food was tasty but not exceptional. The starters were tasty - the skewers, the tempura shrimp and the spring rolls were all good. The grilled chicken was fine but the portion size was small and the salad was not to my taste. Overall I’d love a rich sauce there instead of just a hot one. The service was extremely slow and it took them a lot of time to cook our order. What stands out is the wide selection on the menu.

venues.image_alt: Nua — international restaurant in Central London

venues.vicinity: at The Globe tavern, 8 Bedale Street Upstairs, London

reviews.text: An underrated spot tucked above a pub and delivering amazing and strong flavours! Outstanding food with a lot of zing, creativity, and consideration. Every dish balanced textures, spices, and citrus so perfectly. My partner and I shared 2 small plates and the whole sea bass special, which was a perfect amount of food for us. The corn ribs are a must-try! The sea bass was- by far- the best sea bass I’ve had. The fry was perfect and light, the garnishes fresh and balanced, and the green coriander sauce was so bright and punchy!

Unique & Delicious
KHAO BIRD packs a punch with a creative, flavor-bursting menu of Northern Thai cuisine.
The bbq chicken is beyond amazing!
Great vibe, great staff and an overall great experience.
We went for brunch which was unexpected and still delivered on inventive offerings washed down beautifully with a Som Tam Bloody Mary or two!!

Food was very nice and came out hot. There is a 3 course meal menu which 3 of our group of 6 wanted but you can only have it if everyone at the table wants it which was disappointing but this meant we actually spent less money so that’s their choice to make. The whole Bridget jones apartment thing feels a bit mis-sold. She lived in the loft and the restaurant is on the first floor. I know the place is now a restaurant and would have changed a lot but I couldn’t even find a familiar window in the restaurant. You could see stairs going up from the restaurant which was all painted white like in the film but you couldn’t go up there. So if you’re going for the Bridget Jones experience don’t bother but if you like Thai food this was a nice place to visit. The young lady that served us was great. The cocktails were around £12 my one was so small it was like a shoot so didn’t order more. I don’t mean to sound negative we actually had a lovely time and the food was great. The Bridget blue cocktail went down well so some people in our group had 2. We also had to pay a £30 service charge which worked out £5 each. Just a warning in case you’re not expecting it.

reviews.text: Really tasty Thai food with fair but not overly sized portions and fresh ingredients. The flavors were authentic and well-balanced, and the service was friendly. The atmosphere is casual but welcoming, perfect for a relaxed meal. The only reason it’s not 5 stars is that it could’ve been a little spicier for my taste and the chicken satay was quite watery – but overall, a great spot I’d happily come back to!

I had a lovely meal at this Thai restaurant and was really impressed by the food quality and presentation. I ordered mango sticky rice, prawn cake, Pad Thai noodles, and curry with rice, and every dish was full of authentic flavour.

Tiny little place that doesn't have the capacity to seat more than 16 people, so you may have to wait for a table. But service was excellent. For a no frills place with just 2 people running front of house. They actually come check on you to make sure everything is okay. Their spicy noodles with thick rice noodles was 5/5. Generous portion and they don't use store bought dried noodles. It's proper chewy rice noodles, with a lot of minced meat and herbs in the soup base.  Better than the other Thai noodle place down the road. They also have a good dessert selection which I'll be back for.

reviews.text:
OVERVIEW
Exceptional high quality Thai food and the best set menu in London so far!

PLUS
+ Every dish on the ‘Sharing menu’ was at a 5* level  — bursting with flavours, balanced perfectly between sweet and savoury, with fresh vegetables and herbs adding depth.
+ The ‘Sharing menu’ is best enjoyed on an empty stomach — its range and portion sizes leaves even the greediest eater satisfied.
+ The ‘Sharing menu’ was value for money through its culinary depth and variety.
+ Staff were formally welcoming, genuinely friendly, and attentive throughout the service.
+ The restaurant had a fresh, modern feel with an earthy, garden-like vibe.

MINUS
- The restaurant could provide QR code self-payment option at each table for quicker, hassle-free service.

TABLE ORDER
Sharing menu:
* Prawn Miang Bites
* Gai Prik
* Cured Sea Trout
* Smoked Chicken Hot & Sour Soup
* Chilli Jam Mussels
* Whole Marinated Seabass
Sides:
* Sticky Jasmine Rice
* Roti
Drink:
* San Pellegrino Natural Sparkling Mineral Water

Got the set menu.
The fish was so good and flavorful! The fried chicken was so crunchy (yumz) and the starter with the betel leaves (who knew it went so well?). Wasn’t super impressed with the chicken soup soup. But definitely huge portions that we had enough takeaway for the next day. Lovely service as well.

I've been here four times and I cannot believe that I haven't reviewed this place yet.

First of, this is the only Thai restaurant I've been to four times (and I don't live close). Food is always amazing, and service is always fast, attentive, and welcoming.

It's not your typical Thai restaurant, but the flavors are there. Last time we went we ordered the turmeric roti, nice, flaky and full of flavor. We also got the salted turmeric flossed tiger prawns, and I recommend two each (by default the order comes with three, but you can add one more), the crispy pork belly, and the beer battered chicken.

We weren't that hungry last time, no none of the larger dishes. We've had their larger ones before, and we were always happy.

venues.name: Champor-Champor
venues.description: Thai-Malay restaurant with candlelit balcony, decorated with exotic artefacts, silks and statues.

reviews.text:
We booked a Friday evening table for a birthday dinner, and the place was buzzing! The ambience is absolutely beautiful — very warm and aesthetic.

I’m a vegetarian and ordered the tofu butternut squash green curry with jasmine rice. It was scrumptious, filling, and served hot with a lovely touch of basil oil. The portion size was generous too.

My friends had the king prawn pad thai and chicken massaman, and they really enjoyed both — the massaman was their favourite of the night.

For dessert, we shared the chocolate chilli cheesecake, which we completely devoured!

The only downside was that the service was quite slow. I understand it was a busy evening, but it did take away a bit from the overall experience.

Still, the food and atmosphere made it a lovely evening overall. I’d happily come back!

We brought our guests here for dinner and everyone left with a smile, truly happy. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious. One of our guests had never tried Thai cuisine before, yet they loved it! We were impressed as well. The team was genuinely friendly and the food was fantastic thank you!

Really enjoyed my chicken green curry, and my friend loved her vegan version too — both were delicious! It was a lovely evening overall. Just a heads-up: the restaurant gets very busy, and there’s a 2-hour dining limit, so worth keeping in mind when booking. We went on a Tuesday evening and the place was absolutely heaving.

venues.image_alt: Champor-Champor — international restaurant in Central London

venues.vicinity: Union House Shepherds Bush Green, 65 Shepherd's Bush Grn, London

reviews.text:
I visited for both breakfast and lunch. The restaurant is located toward the middle of the building on the ground, but it's filled with natural light and has a bright, welcoming atmosphere. There are various types of seating, and if it's not too crowded, the staff will kindly let you choose the kind of seat you prefer, which makes the experience even more pleasant.
Everyone from the reception to the servers was polite and warm, and I truly appreciated the thoughtful and graceful service. Every dish I tried was carefully crafted and absolutely delicious. This is definitely a place I'd love to visit again.

We had prawn toast, pineapple fried rice, pork ribs and coconut yellow curry hake fish clams - they were all absolutely banging! Wouldn’t miss out on coconut rice & mango and banana roti. Every bite felt like we’re instantly transported back to Asia. The ambiance was cozy & service was great! The staff and the chefs were quite friendly. We will definitely come back to try their other food!

I tried Chet’s BBQ pork belly and wagyu fried rice, and I was absolutely blown away! The fried rice was full of flavor due to having so many different components and seasoning, and every bite felt like an incredible, new experience. The pork belly was also very enjoyable and my only complaint was that there wasn’t more of it on the plate! I was also quite surprised by the serving size of the fried rice; it could have easily fed 3! The service was also perfect, my waitress was attentive and helpful throughout (as I had a few questions). Definitely a 5-star experience!

venues.image_alt: Chet's — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Patara Knightsbridge
venues.description: Upscale venue with chic, sleek decor offering an innovative contemporary take on Thai cooking.

reviews.text: Absolutely incredible Thai food. Highly recommend the lamb massaman curry and wok fried noodles with beef. The Patara passion cocktail is also fantastic if you want to enjoy a nice refreshing beverage with your meal! We will definitely be back!

Excellent service and food!
It’s my second time dining here I really like the fried sea bass! You can tell the chef did a great job with his knife skills.
Highly recommended! It’s close to Harrods so if you are craving some legit Asian cuisine, should definitely try them out!!

reviews.author_name: สุภัทรสร ขุนเเก้ว
reviews.text: I came here for my husband’s birthday and we both had a wonderful meal! The food was sooooo tasty and all of the staff were great. I highly recommend Patara if you are looking for a Thai restaurant in London.!

venues.image_alt: Patara Knightsbridge — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Thai Square Trafalgar Square
venues.description: Contemporary Thai chain restaurant with bronze Buddhist sculptures & traditional carvings.

reviews.text:
Lovely and elite experience! The staff were very welcoming and kind, plus they confirmed  for us that the chicken was halal 🙂‍↕️

The ambiance was beautiful with lovely decor, air conditioning, and a very peaceful environment 😌

And the food was very delicious! Everything on the starters platter and mains was bursting with flavour 🤤 The soup’s broth was very good but the shrimp felt tasteless 🥲

Overall we had a great time 👍

Beautiful setting but disappointing service and portions

The restaurant has a grand entrance and is in a perfect location. The décor is lovely and feels authentic – I’d give five stars for atmosphere.

Unfortunately, the service didn’t live up to expectations. We visited during a quiet Sunday lunchtime with only two other tables occupied. The waiter seemed disinterested and inattentive. We ordered a bottle of sparkling water but weren’t given any glasses. We also had to ask for knives with our starter and call the staff over whenever we needed anything. For a high-end restaurant during a quiet period, I would expect the service to be far more attentive. One staff member who came by later was friendlier and asked about our meal, which was appreciated, but overall the service fell short.

The food was good, but the portion sizes were underwhelming for the price. The most disappointing dish was the Padang Thai beef curry – the portion was so small it didn’t even cover a bowl of rice. It was also served on a small plate rather than in a bowl, which was surprising for a curry.

Overall, a beautiful place with potential, but service and value for money need improvement.

Just a short 5-minute walk from Charing Cross, Thai Square is a lovely little spot tucked away near Trafalgar Square. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the service was top-notch. The staff were really attentive, especially Tia, who went out of her way to make sure we were looked after.

The drinks menu was great—lots of options. We went for mocktails, which were refreshing and well made. Starters were a hit too; the corn cakes and dumplings were especially tasty.

The mains came out fairly quickly, and everything was nicely cooked. We had the red chicken curry, glass noodles with prawns, Penang curry (though I was meant to get prawns and ended up with chicken, they swapped it for me but I had to wait a little so double check your dish before diving in!), and duck in sauce. The coconut rice was a standout for me - really fragrant and creamy. Just a heads-up: rice has to be ordered separately.

It was a birthday dinner, and they surprised us with a complimentary little chocolate cake and ice cream, which was a lovely touch.

The only downsides were the duck dish, which didn’t look the most appetising (though it tasted okay), and the fact there are no male toilets - just urinals.

Also one thing to note – no one asked about allergies when we ordered, so it’s worth mentioning any dietary requirements upfront just to be safe.

Overall, it was a really enjoyable evening with good food and excellent service.

venues.name: The Great THAI Restaurant
venues.description: Simple but smart cafe serving array of Thai favourites, with express lunch menu and dinner options.
venues.address: 14 Riding House St, London W1W 7HR, UK

reviews.text:
Absolutely delicious Thai food!
I had an amazing experience at this Thai restaurant. The flavors were authentic and perfectly balanced—spicy, savory, and full of rich herbs. Every dish was cooked to perfection, especially the Pad Kra Pao and Fish salad. The staff were friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. Highly recommended for anyone craving real Thai cuisine!

This is the closest I can get to Thailand! (from London).
The price is very reasonable for the amount of servings you get.
The staff are so amazing, they will talk to you on how to enjoy every dish to the fullest.
My favourite is the steamed jumping fish balls!
Highly recommended 💯

I should have known better (a Thai mini-chain near Oxford St) but, I was hungry, had an urge for som tam and grilled meat, and was still about a mile from the reliable Lao Cafe. Plus it was 11.30 and this place was open already… I took my chances after seeing their Isaan menu.

On walking in, one of the staff immediately barked at me that I could only have the table for 1 hour.  Great start.

I then made the mistake of asking for “kor moo yang” rather than “moo yang” and was told to only order from the menu. I explained my error and then ordered the som tam pu (from the menu, ironically) and was told they couldn’t do that, as they didn’t have the the little field crabs available. (I agreed to have it without the crabs and just pl raa and got charged an extra pound anyway…)

I asked for Thai spice with the som tam and it had decent heat. It could have done with some more lime juice for balance in my view (and to make it less dry), but that’s a matter of taste. It was also pretty expensive at £10.95 given the size. The pork was tender and marinated fine but came topped with sesame seeds randomly. The sticky rice was quite hard and dry. Came to just over £30 with service. And the service remained prickly for the duration…

Overall, average at best. Given the service this falls into the “avoid” category for me.

venues.name: The Churchill Arms, Kensington
venues.description: Flower-bedecked real ale boozer, filled with Churchill memorabilia, serving Thai noodles and curry.
venues.address: 119 Kensington Church St, London W8 7LN, UK

reviews.text: Such an adorable spot. We grabbed 2 pints of some tasty raspberry cider just to try out the place and it was very busy on a midday Friday. Enjoyed our pints outside since it was a beautiful day lots of folks outside. The interior is packed with memorabilia and has some tables but limited seating if it is busy. Outside has some beautiful flowers along the building. Would definitely come back to enjoy the Thai spot out back.

Went here after seeing it featured in YouTube travel videos.

It truly is beautiful and interesting to look at inside and out, but like my friend said, "What is their theme? It's like they just did all of it!"

From the outside, it looks beautiful because it's covered in flowers.

When you walk inside, there's a bar and there's British flags hanging from the ceiling and Winston Churchill art on the walls.

I said, "Now this is a proper British pub!"

And my friend who is British said, "This is a British pub that's gone over the top!"

I read that this is actually one of the oldest pubs in London being established in 1750, and was frequented by Winston Churchill's grandparents who the pub is named after.

I had made a reservation for dinner, so we were led to the back where there were Thai flags hanging from the ceiling and plants as well, to the point it looked like a jungle.

The dishes were all Thai and I read that this is one of the first restaurants to serve Thai food in London in the 1990's, and it all started with a chef who was Thai.

I ordered vegetarian pad thai. It was good, but more noodles than vegetables.

The price and portions were reasonable.

Overall, this was a good experience that I'd recommend.
A traditional London pub with a twist - only serves Thai food. Good selection of cask and craft beers and lagers, wine and spirits. Usually busy so may have wait for a table but service is quick.

venues.name: Nipa Thai
venues.description: Upscale Thai dining in a hotel restaurant with a panelled teak interior and original furnishings.
venues.address: First Floor, of, Lancaster Terrace, London W2 2TY, UK
venues.vicinity: First Floor, of, Lancaster London, Lancaster Terrace, London

reviews.text: Booked through First Table and enjoyed a fantastic 50% off the bill. The food was absolutely delicious and tasted authentic, with prompt service and minimal wait times. Most of the staff were very friendly and attentive, creating a welcoming atmosphere. The only downside was one waitress who gave incorrect information about a menu item and rushed our order, but it didn’t take away from the overall experience. The restaurant is small and cozy, located within a lovely hotel, making it a great spot for a relaxed and enjoyable meal.

The restaurant is tucked away on the first floor of the Royal Lancaster London Hotel. You enter through the elegant marble foyer, head up the stairs, and turn right. It sets the tone beautifully.

We were greeted warmly by the manager and shown to a window table overlooking Hyde Park. Our 18:30 reservation meant the restaurant was still quiet, with only one other table occupied, a perfect start.

The menu is broad but not overwhelming. I chose the chicken and coconut soup, chicken stir-fry, and mango sorbet for dessert. Every dish was exceptional, the best Thai food I’ve had anywhere.

Service was attentive without being intrusive. The team clearly know what they’re doing and let the food speak for itself.

The whole experience reflects the setting, refined, calm, and just the right side of luxurious.

Excellent food, excellent staff. I’ll definitely be back, and would highly recommend you book a table too.

This restaurant is up there in my top 3 restaurants of all time. An absolute game changer!

I was treated to an early birthday dinner by a friend and I chose here as they were rated very highly on tripadvisor.

Had a little Google before hand on what to order and their website mentioned that chef’s favourite and known for dish was the Tom Kha soup and Prawn Pad Thai

I’d never had Tom Kha before but it’s probably one my favourite dishes of all time now - and actually I’ve had it elsewhere since and it didn’t compare! Had the prawn pad Thai too which was just delicious

My friend had the dumplings which I had a cheeky sample of too which were tasty.

Staff were friendly and attentive - probably the best service I’ve ever received.

Defo my new favourite spot! It’s located in the Royal Lancaster hotel and is a little spenny but worth it!

venues.name: Phakoon Thai Kitchen - Earlsfield
venues.description: Phakoon Thai Kitchen - Earlsfield is a thai restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Phakoon Thai Kitchen - Earlsfield provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine thai flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.vicinity: Palace Gate Estates, 346-348 Garratt Ln, London

reviews.text: Finally, a place that gets "hot" and "spicy" right. I specifically asked for spicy spicy and not British spicy (no offence intended here) for my takeaway order and they delivered beautifully. This place is run by a warm, friendly family. Good service, good food! I had the curry with rice and absolutely loved it! The other flavours aren't buried underneath all the heat from the chilies. Well balanced, would definitely recommend this place. The ambience looks good so hope to dine at the restaurant some day :)

A Triumphant Return to Thai Dining at Phakoon Thai

After a long hiatus from Thai restaurants, Phakoon Thai has completely rekindled my love for the cuisine. What a fantastic evening! Every dish we sampled boasted its own distinct and memorable flavor profile, a refreshing change from many unpleasant Thai restaurants out there.

The Crispy Golden Bags were a highlight—perfectly prepared and delightfully grease-free. The Chicken Satay was equally impressive, offering a wonderful smoky curry flavor and incredibly tender chicken.

We were also pleasantly surprised by the steamed sea bass fillet with ginger and the tamarind Silken tofu, both exceeding our initial expectations with their delicate yet impactful tastes.

Beyond the exquisite food, the overall experience was truly exceptional. The service was natural and perfectly attentive, never feeling intrusive. It was clear the staff were genuinely happy and eager to please, which added significantly to the welcoming atmosphere.

As a gluten-intolerant diner, I particularly appreciated Phakoon Thai's excellent accommodation. It's a huge relief to find a restaurant that caters so thoughtfully to dietary needs without compromising on flavor or experience.

Well done, Phakoon Thai, and thank you for a truly delightful evening!

Food was delicious and came out very fast. Although the food had great flavour there wasn’t all that much to it (I had the chicken massaman curry). Portions were quite decent as I was quite full after the rice and curry. I think it would have been better to make a reservation as they turned down a couple people with no reservations despite the restaurant being semi empty (there were definitely quite a few tables available). We got given a table on the basis we vacated within an hour and a half which was plenty of time. Overall, staff were nice, food was good and came out quite fast and pricing was decent as well.

venues.name: Kin + Deum
venues.description: Contemporary cooking of Bangkok with cocktails in a stylishly spare, dog-friendly dining room.

reviews.text: Kin + Deum offers a warm, cozy ambiance paired with genuinely friendly service. The Thai-inspired dishes are flavorful and thoughtfully presented. The noodles were cooked to perfection, with rich, balanced flavors that really stood out. Desserts were a delightful surprise—light, creative, and satisfying. It’s also dog-friendly, making it a perfect spot for pet owners. A great choice for casual dinners or catching up with friends. Highly recommend for anyone seeking comforting food with a modern twist.

Tried their special manual, pink lychee martini, pandan chicken. All so good. The stuff here are supper helpful, and friendly. We don’t know what to order. They provided so many good recommendation. Definitely will came back.

Really delicious Thai food and generous portions. Each dish had so much flavour and the meat dishes were so tender. Standout dish was the grilled honey tamarind spare ribs and the mango cheesecake. Service was friendly and the restaurant itself was spacious, would recommend booking ahead as it does fill up in the evening.

venues.image_alt: Kin + Deum — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Kibele Restaurant
venues.description: Vibrant eatery offering classic & modern Turkish cuisine plus cocktails, live music & belly dancing.
venues.address: 175-177 Great Portland St, London W1W 5PJ, UK
venues.vicinity: devon house, 175-177 Great Portland St, London

reviews.text: I would have written this review the same day,no words can truly capture the customer service. Although they charge £15.50, which feels a bit on the higher side and not entirely fair, the experience made up for it. The service was excellent and so warm, the toilets were clean (though the place itself felt a little dark), and the food,what can I say? Generous portions, authentic flavours, and absolutely delicious. A must-visit for anyone who loves real, tasty food!

the food was amazing!!! would totally come back here a second time. the staff are respectful and welcoming, the environment is the perfect mix of lively and colourful and a relaxing place; and the music is calm and chill. our waiter, Ayten was amazing! she was very kind and nice.
overall, a wonderful evening; highly recommend!

Surprisingly good. Very substantial portions, which weren’t a substitute for quality. Could have been a tiny bit more seasoned.

Live saxophone music which was not too loud and made for great ambience.

Murat was our waiter, very professional yet warm demeanour.

Will be coming back soon

venues.name: Gökyüzü Green Lanes
venues.description: Informal family-run Turkish spot serving classic dishes cooked in a traditional oven.
venues.address: 26-28 Grand Parade, Green Lanes, Harringay Ladder, London N4 1LG, UK

reviews.text: Visiting in the UK, this restaurant was recommended by family members living in the neighborhood. It was an excellent suggestion. The food was delicious, savory and flavorful. The portions were much larger than the menu suggested and we enjoyed it all. Your most difficult choice is narrowing your selections from their extensive menu. You won't regret this meal.

My friend who lives around Hampstead introduced me to this place last year and since then we’ve been regular here to enjoy some genuinely good Turkish food!! The service here is always nice and the mixed platter is very generous and serves delicious meats alongside salad and Turkish rice! A must have and definitely bring your friends along! Good value for money!

This time we were served by Havni & Yaren who were great hosts and we recommend them for their attention to detail and hospitality

A proper Turkish restaurant. It was such a nice experience. Nice food full of flavour and cooked properly, nice service and friendly. Really big portions. We tried a lot of dishes and apart from one dish we liked all the rest.

venues.image_alt: Gökyüzü Green Lanes — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Antalya
venues.description: Lavish, colourful frescoes adorn this vibrant restaurant for classic Turkish and Mediterranean fare.

reviews.text: Antalya Restaurant was a fantastic find in the heart of London. We sat outdoors on a warm summer evening, and the setting was perfect, relaxed and inviting. The food was full of authentic Turkish flavour, beautifully presented, and made with fresh ingredients. From the grilled meats to the baklava, everything was delicious. The staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole experience even better. Highly recommended for anyone looking for great Turkish food, especially in the summer. Thank you again for the amazing food and service! We will definitely come back again ☺️🙏

Stumbled above this restaurant on the way from the train station to our hotel and what a wonderful find it was!! Lunch was beyond a bargain. The chicken wrap was delicious and as for the Rosè… stunning. Our waiter Fatih was so friendly and welcoming. Such a gorgeous start to our holiday in London.

Tried the lunch deal and opted for the mezze meal option, definitely not worth almost £20 for the quantity given. Food was average, I was expecting a lot more considering the high reviews. The other dish in the picture is the lamb iskander, which was also alright, again not worth nearly £25. I'd probably skip this and get better value for money + better tasting food elsewhere.

venues.image_alt: Antalya — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Hala Restaurant
venues.description: Traditional Turkish plates offered in a wood- and brick-lined setting with wagon wheel chandeliers.
venues.address: 29-31 Grand Parade, Green Lanes, Harringay Ladder, London N4 1LG, UK

reviews.text: With no exaggeration, this is the best turk food in London. It is even better in some ways than that in Istanbul. Looking for authentic flavour and craving tender cooked to perfection Mediterranean food? I highly recommend this place!

As a Turk, we were very happy to find these dishes at a restaurant in London.
The homemade mantı, içli köfte, and liver were very good.
As in classic Turkish restaurants, yoghurt-based meze and spicy sauce were served with bread before the meal.
The lahmacun was a disappointment — we had high expectations.
But unfortunately, the dough was soft, the topping was sparse, and the taste was not what we hoped for.
The ayran was also quite tasteless.
We would have been much happier if the staff had been a bit more friendly.
They offered a turkish tea after meal
desserts were very nice we had kunafa and rice pudding.
We ordered the large portion of the cop shish, but it seemed small to us.
The prices were reasonable.
We paid £35 per person
