Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 12 Regent Street Saint James's, London SW1Y 4PE, UK

reviews.text:
This coffee shop is an absolute gem! The lattes are incredible—smooth, rich, and crafted with real care. Each one is perfectly balanced, and you can tell the baristas know their coffee inside out.

The cakes are just as impressive. Fresh, flavorful, and beautifully made—they strike the perfect balance between indulgent and comforting. It’s the kind of place where you can’t resist ordering a slice with your drink.

On top of that, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it a perfect spot to relax, catch up with friends, or enjoy a quiet moment.

Definitely a must-visit for anyone who loves great coffee and cake!
Beautiful art i ever witnessed on a cappuccino, it’s way more than a cup of coffee. Thank you and will see you next time!

Love this coffee shop, it's really friendly with a fantastic atmosphere. Absolutely love visiting here as the food and range of drinks is simply amazing and taste great too. Even love the difference in the coffee froth designs. Nice to have a coffee shop that's different from the usual chains.

venues.name: Monmouth Coffee Company
venues.description: Fair-trade coffee & gourmet treats in the cafe & whole or freshly ground beans bagged to take home.

reviews.text: Coffee is amazing here. It's busy but there are still places to sit and the staff here know their coffee and happy to suggest different beans. Variety of beans to choose from if you like filter coffee. They have oatly oat milk if you are particular with that as well! Love the atmosphere.

Amazing coffee definitely worth the hype and then some 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥. I will be returning for another caffeine hit. A must visit. For non dairy people like me they do oat milk. I would be great if they had other non dairy options like coconut. The quality of the coffee was amazing. You can also buy coffee beans to take home. ☕☕☕☕🫘

There’s many things to like here. Pastries are great, service is very good, the set up of the whole cafe is very enjoyable to be a part of. Unfortunately the standards have dropped in the coffee over the last few years, flavour of the beans has gone down in favour of stronger more bitter cups. The milkwork is still really good. I’d still recommend a visit if you’re around Borough Market but I wouldn’t go out of your way to come here.

venues.name: Arôme Bakery - Mercer Street
venues.description: Cosy bakery with a trendy vibe dishing up a fusion of French & Asian confections.

reviews.text: Great bakery and awsome pastries. Apple miso danish was wonderful, crispy dough and balanced taste. Also cappuccino and hojicha latte were very good. Honey toast wasn't to good as I expected, but not bad. It was too dry for me. Some cream with toast will be better. Nice, cozy atmosphere with asia influence. Very nice and helpful services. I am glad for recomendation and talk. Their another savoury and sweet pastries looks also interesting.

My favorite bakery in London by far. Everything I tried was amazing. The doughs are just perfect — whether it’s a brioche that makes the best toast, a croissant that’s laminated and shaped so beautifully (which is really hard to pull off), or a quiche that’s creamy in just the right way, not too eggy and not too heavy on the veggies. Everything felt super balanced and delicious. It’s one of those rare spots where every single thing you pick is a winner.

No doubt many people are aware of this bakery and its excellent reputation, so perhaps leaving a review is somewhat redundant. However, it’s been a couple of weeks since our very first visit and I’ve not stopped thinking about how much I enjoyed it! The Apple Miso Danish frankly deserves its own national holiday. That pesto mozzarella wonder was all but inhaled. And the fight over the last bite of pistachio and chocolate snail nearly ended in divorce with my husband. You know the drill though. Somewhere this good and this hyped gets queues. And we arrived first thing on a Saturday morning too! Be prepared to wait if you arrive later in the day - or just do as we did, which is grab and go as there’s plenty of seating dotted around where you can people watch while you scoff! Definitely one of those places which will beckon you to return to try out their other delectable looking items. In fact, it’s in my diary for this weekend! Oh and shoutout to the team at the counter who patiently dealt with my decision paralysis.

venues.image_alt: Arôme Bakery - Mercer Street — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Aux pains de papy
venues.description: Quaint French bakery offers baked goods, sweets and sandwiches in a nook with limited seating.
venues.address: 279 Grays Inn Rd, London WC1X 8QF, UK

reviews.text:
Stumbled upon this hidden gem near King's Cross station by chance and after trying couldn’t believe it wasn’t much busier than it is. The chocolate almond croissant was perfect - flaky, rich, and generously loaded with sliced almonds and had a gorgeously melted bar of good chocolate inside. The plain croissant? Deep golden layers, buttery aroma, crisp on the outside and soft within.

Coffee was spot-on. Strong, smooth, and made with care. Friendly service, no fuss, no rush. Just great pastries, great coffee, and a quiet spot to enjoy them. One of the best bakeries I've tried in London. Will return.

Croissants are one if my favorite things and so are boulangeries. I go to Paris quite often and I love trying different boulangeries. The croissant from this place is a croissant you could get in Paris and it's the best I've tried in London. Super crispy, flaky, a hint of butter, fluffy inside. I will come back for more!! We also tried the almond croissant and the chocolate eclair. These two were good, but for me the plain croissant was outstanding.

From the window, everything looked and smelled delicious, and it was! It was very difficult to choose what to eat because everything looked delicious. The chocolate bar and cappuccino were delicious! A special mention for the friendly and warm service I received.

venues.image_alt: Aux pains de papy — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: E5 Bakehouse
venues.description: Artisan bakery & cafe with a community focus serving sourdough bread, organic lunches & cakes.

reviews.text: Loved the feel of the place and how it has a mini market. Very spacious and clean bathrooms if i may add. Delicious coffee didn't like the cookie they braged about, was kinda dry for me. Will definitely try other things if I ever was in the area again

Holy cow this was good!! I had the fried egg & halloumi bun, as well as a corn madeline/scone thing. The bun was yummm — super tasty bread with just the right balance of sweet/savoury/umami.  I had the corn snack a little later and it really threw me off: moist inside but with a satisfying crust.  Would 100% return, this time with an empty stomach and some grocery bags.

I had an amazing time at the sourdough bread course at e5 Bakehouse last Saturday. It was a beautiful day, and the whole experience was inspiring from start to finish.
Alex, our teacher, was fantastic—so enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and clearly passionate about his craft. He made the learning process fun, clear, and really engaging. The rest of the team was just as warm and welcoming, creating a great atmosphere throughout the day.
I learned so much and left with new skills, more confidence, and, of course, lots of bread! Highly recommend this course to anyone curious about baking or just looking for a special and enjoyable experience in London.

venues.image_alt: E5 Bakehouse — international restaurant in Central London

reviews.text: Stopped here somewhat recently on a whim. Super busy! They have a really great selection available - We both had one of the beignets, which were very tasty but I think they could've been a bit more generous with the toppings for the price, service was quick and friendly, will definitely be back again if we're in the area.

The street it’s located on, along with the overall vibe and style of the place, was really charming. The coffee was excellent. The baked goods we tried were tasty, though the savory ones we chose were a bit too oily for our liking. As for the sweet option, it was nice, but we would have preferred it without the chocolate sauce. Overall, it’s a lovely spot with a cozy atmosphere, definitely worth a visit.

It’s definitely an “Instagram” spot - everything was oversized and well made. The proportions of the pastries were a bit off, aka not enough pastry to sausage roll or croissant to chocolate ratio.
Plenty of options means there is something for everyone, but I do believe this is one of those over hyped places

venues.name: Chestnut Bakery, Covent Garden
venues.description: Chestnut Bakery, Covent Garden is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Chestnut Bakery, Covent Garden provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Wonderful assortment of pastries but the ones we ordered were just alright, nothing mindblowing. A little too sweet for our liking. Soft serve with honey toast was an interesting offer that we don’t see many in other cafes/bakeries so it was lovely. Wanted the vanilla flavour soft serve but it was sold out so I had the chocolate one which was decent. The honey toast that came with it was a little too sweet and dry though. It’s a lovely place with great vibes for a coffee with a friend, to rest your legs after some shopping in central London but not specifically be there for the baked goods. Menu offers breakfast/brunch type of food I have yet to try but I’ll probably skip that. Staff were extremely helpful and kind though. Made us feel really welcomed despite being so busy.

We sat upstairs right by the window with the scenic view of the street. The pastries were each made to be a perfect image of itself. The labneh cherry tomato toasty was the best savory breakfast sandwich you can ask for to be balanced with the sweetness of the blueberry tart - which is easy to miss, but not in Chestnut - every bite you get fresh blueberries and never a jammy sticking to your teeth goo, but a wonderful creamy filling encased by the more exquisite laminated dough.
Not one miss!

Came in just before 6. There wasn’t any seating downstairs expect a small table near the entrance which we had to sit there was four of us. Even though the cafe was open we was told upstairs seating was closed. Wanted the Karak tea which wasn’t available, either was the brookie. Ordered two scoops of ice cream which I asked for choc. Then I see one of the guys giving vanilla asked the lady that was serving me that I asked for choc which she said there wasn’t any available even though she took my order. She wasn’t paying attention as she kept repeating my order. As we sat with our hot choc and the basic vanilla ice cream. We can see the bins getting taken out, everything getting cleared up. There was still people coming in. Considering we were in convent garden and you pay more than average I don’t expect to see huge bins going past me multiple times, aswell everything getting cleared up. The cafe is open and should accommodate accordingly during the opening hours. Won’t be coming in a hurry anytime soon.

venues.image_alt: Chestnut Bakery, Covent Garden — international restaurant in Central London

venues.description: COMMON BREADS is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. reviews.text:
The cheese manakish, musakhan, and spinach pies were absolutely incredible. The owner manages the restaurant himself, and the location is just perfect. I truly congratulate him and wish him even more success and new branches in the future.

You can actually ask them to make the pastries in a small size for takeaway — they were absolutely delicious, arrived hot and fresh, and perfectly clean. Truly amazing!

We recently hosted a work event and chose Common Breads for the catering. From start to finish, the experience was exceptional. They tailored our order perfectly, offering a wide variety of options to suit everyone’s preferences. The food was outstanding — fresh, delicious, and of the highest quality — and the service was just as impressive.

Our team and guests were genuinely impressed, and it made the event feel extra special. I would wholeheartedly recommend Common Breads to anyone looking for catering that combines quality, variety, and excellent service.

The chicken musakhan manouche was the best dish - highly recommended. The other dishes were alright. Worth a try but nothing to rave about.

Service is great and staff are friendly.

venues.image_alt: COMMON BREADS — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Bageriet
venues.description: Compact Nordic bakery & cafe with traditional Swedish cakes and pastries to eat in or take away.

reviews.text: As a Swedish Londoner this place will always have a warm place in my heart!! I also had the most wonderful few shifts working here just before Covid started, and got to learn about how everything’s made on the premisses! Can’t recommend enough if you want some authentic Swedish cinnamon buns 💕

They are comparable to any bakery in Stockholm👌 they even make the princess cake. It is pretty small, but the atmosphere is cosy. The pastries were delicious, but the pistachio one was a little too sweet for me. The coffee can be improved.

Wow!! What a selection, what a bakers, what customer service!! I ordered a special cake and 48hrs it was ready to collect and the engraving I asked for, perfectly done, just as I asked for! Would recommend any day, even just for a visit to see (or sample) the cakes!

venues.name: Miel Bakery
venues.description: Cosy, classic French bakery offering housemade breads, pastries & seasonal tarts, plus hot drinks.

reviews.text: I wanted to love this bakery but I felt my almond croissant was a little too sweet. It was well filled and the pastry was extra buttery. The cinnamon buns looked amazing here so I would come back to try. Only two outdoor seats for seating. Pastries range from £3.5-£6 so some are definitely on the premium priced side. My almond croissant was £4.50.

As we were eating our croissants outside an older lady walked past and blared out “I can’t just walk past, I have to get one”. And it makes sense once you try one. Delicious heavenly croissants. This is an exceptional bakery offering a range of both sweet and savory croissants.
A truly lovely local bakery with amazing pastries. Out of the oven fresh, all absolutely delicious made with fresh and quality ingredients. Their coffee is also phenomenal.

venues.image_alt: Miel Bakery — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: TOAD Bakery
venues.description: TOAD Bakery is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, TOAD Bakery provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
The line is long but it moves relatively
quickly! The pastries are delicious and fresh - get the kalamansi and coconut iced bun, this was cheap but delicious, cornbread croissant was savoury but could’ve done with more jalepeno, plum danish was ok, and the everything bagel croissant was delicious! Tastes just like a bagel, but in croissant form so it’s super buttery and flakey.

The least favourite was the Jaffa cake, texture was a bit too dense.

Would queue again!

This was a very nice pastry, and to be honest they seemed to have tonnes of great options. It was delicious! My only gripe with this place is that the queue was mental - I was in it for 45 minutes. I have no issue with a place being popular but the queue was barely moving which was slightly frustrating.

The line was sooooo long and you look at it, and think is it worth it for a bakery??

And let me tell you… it is SO worth it. I truly believe this is the best bakery in London and is worth every single person in line waiting for pastries. We ordered so much and enjoyed every last bite. They had a collab at the time and we had a beef curry pastry which was fab. The pastry just tasted incredible, the different savoury and sweet options were an added bonus.

venues.image_alt: TOAD Bakery — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: The Dusty Knuckle Bakery
venues.description: Light cafe fare such as creative sandwiches & salads with coffee drinks & fresh breads to-go.

reviews.text:
so yum! ive had this bakery on my radar for a while now, and it was so worth the wait to come along.
whilst £11 is obviously a lot for a sandwich, you 100% get what you pay for. The homemade bread was absolutely lovely and the sandwich was packed full of flavourful filling.
the atmosphere was lovely, and sitting outside was great. service was brilliant and hardly a wait for my food either. i came at about 12 o’clock and didn’t have to queue, however when i left at 12:40 there was a large queue, so definitely get there a bit earlier if you want a sandwich! they deserve the popularity though, i absolutely loved this bakery.

After being recommended this bakery I was eager to visit and it didn't disappoint.

Maybe one of the largest bakeries you'll ever visit, hidden down the end of a back lane with extensive outdoor seating it's a great spot for brunch or lunch on the weekend just be prepared to que.

I visited on a Saturday and waited no more than a couple of minutes and tried two of my favourite UK stallwards the Morning Roll (chai spiced sugar dusted cruffin) and the go-to Honey and Feta swirl which was laden with sesame and poppy seeds and was absolutely banging!

All their pastries and bread looked top tier. Flaky lamination and a deep caramel crust on all their sourdough (just the way I like it!)

The breakfast sando looked unreal, and is clearly a top seller for good reason.

I look forward to my next visit to try the rest!

Keep up the good work team! 🤘

Unbeatable breads, amazing sandwiches, and really creative options! The queue this past July 6th weekend was wild, but worth it! We waited in the queue about 20 minutes until we ordered, but there were plenty of tables and we were able to sit 4 of us at a table inside. Despite the crowds, service was so fast! Our sandwiches + drinks arrived within 8-10 minutes of ordering and were of course, the best in London.

It’s the first time I’ve seen it this busy, but even with the queue, these baked goods are always worth it.

venues.name: Chestnut Bakery, Belgravia
venues.description: International breads, pastries & sandwiches featured in a high-end bakery & cafe setup.

reviews.text:
Wonderful place to kick start the day. My favorite Chestnut Bakery branch in a very beautiful and aesthetic area of the city (posh 😅). Big selection of sweet and savory pastries plus the breakfast dishes, you can’t go wrong here. Service was very good and staff were welcoming and helpful. Don’t miss their crispy cinnamon roll.
Highly recommended 👍🏼

Stopped by Chestnut Bakery and was pleasantly surprised! I had an Americano and their Chicken Club Sandwich – and both were spot on. The sandwich was especially impressive – packed with flavour, and the melted cheese took it to another level. Fresh ingredients, warm and satisfying – honestly one of the best chicken clubs I’ve had in a while.

The coffee was smooth and well-balanced, perfect with the meal. Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff made the experience even better. Definitely recommend if you’re in the area – a great spot for a quick bite or relaxed coffee break.

The flatbreads are to die for. Haven’t tried the pastry yet but I imagine they’re good as they sell out quickly! Service is so kind. I will say, probably not the place to go if you’re in a rush as the workers will give you plenty of space.

venues.name: Beigel Bake
venues.description: 24-hour bakery known for traditional Jewish-style filled bagels such as salt beef and smoked salmon.

reviews.text: Honestly the best place for beigels!!! The salt beef-gherkin-mustard combo is always my favourite, but even a plain cream cheese beigel here is amazing. The texture of the beigel is just simply the best. Never fail to pop in here whenever I’m back in London!

I happened to pass by and saw that there was a long line of people, and because it was a Sunday I chose to come two days later when there were fewer people and at a more convenient time. On the one hand, the saleswoman didn't understand that I asked for the 'house dish', on the other hand, the bib sandwich was full of tender meat and was delicious. I enjoyed it very much and will go back there again.

Decent bagel at this bakery that is an institution in London. I had a salt beef beigel with extra of pickles. There is a good amount of meat in the beigel per serving . Meat is not dry and it’s flavoursome. Service was fast (I was not stuck in a queue). I would say if you are in the area looking for something to eat /after a night out this is your best bet. Good value for money.

venues.description: Arôme Bakery - Duke Street is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.5-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Arôme Bakery - Duke Street provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
I got two strawberry tarts with vanilla cream as I was told it was their last day and a chocolate and pear tarte.

Strawberry tarte is very delicate and crumbly, the strawberries were nice and ripe, cream was more like a vanilla flavoured whipped cream than custard and the tarte base was very buttery. Very delicious for first two bites but then it gets boring and dull. I’d split it with 2/3 people as it get sickly after some time.

I had high hopes for chocolate and pear tarte as autumn is a season of the pear and the apple. It was disappointing. Pear layer is thinner or the same as chocolate but the chocolate ganache is so thick that it’s overpowering every flavour. If you want to taste any pear you need to separate cause it’s too delicate too fight the strong and thick layer of ganache. Flavours don’t balance each other out. The chocolate layer is a thick overkill that becomes a blip of chocolate in the mouth.

Matcha was nice but quite small.

The team working didn’t care about being there and if asked any questions about the pastries they couldn’t be more uninterested. It seems the popularity of the place makes them confident in not caring about people coming there. Which is a shame considering the prices and that in this climate it would be a treat for most to go to a place like this.

I bought two strawberry tarts and one chocolate and pear one + matcha.

In total I spent £26.20. I would not come back tbh.

On an extremely hot day, the Iced Citrus Black was absolutely perfect super refreshing! I also tried two desserts: the first was the café’s signature Honey Toast, and the other was a Coffee Cheesecake. I didn’t expect much from the cheesecake, but it turned out to be really delicious highly recommended! As for the Honey Toast, it was okay, but not amazing for me. The sweetness level was fine, but the toast itself was a bit on the dry side.

Possibly better than their other bakery in Covent Garden. Different options available here and all taste incredible. The chocolate and banana croissant is one of the best things I’ve ever put in my mouth - will keep
coming back just for this. Their coffee isn’t bad either.

venues.name: Maison Bertaux
venues.description: 19th-century, French patisserie and tea rooms with marble-topped tables, plus art gallery spaces.

reviews.text: Yummy pastries and busy workers!! Recommend rosehip tea 🌹and the mixed fruit 🍓cheesecake and the raspberry tart. Both were light and creamy. ✨🤍SO good!! We got 6 pastries and two pots of tea. 🫖That FILLED the four of us up and filled the table as well!! 100% recommend if you want a cheaper afternoon tea with more bang for your buck. 💷💥

4.5/5.
I cannot get over the scones and the collated cream and the fresh berry tart. Especially the latter. The creme inside was divine. The outer whipped cream is so light and airy. The dessert itself is perfectly sweet. Not cloying, not un-satisfying. Just perfect. With the freshest assortment of berries. Their hot chocolate is comforting, especially on a cold day. The service is good, there is seating. Would definitely visit this place many, many times to try everything they have on their menu. Outstanding stuff!

Scones were very good. Very big piece and very generous with the jam and clotted cream. At first we were hesitant as the scone was not heated up but it was still very very good, especially with the tea! We also had the berry tart which was very refreshing. Price was reasonable, 40 pounds for 3 scones, 1 tart, and 2 teas. Would come back again!

venues.name: Maya’s Bakehouse
venues.description: Maya’s Bakehouse is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Maya’s Bakehouse provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Amazing little bakery, we tried the cinnamon+cardamon bun, the chimichurri bun and the basque cheesecake! All were immense and will definitely be returning!! Lovely staff as well who even cut our pastries in half so we could try them all in the store 🫶🏻
I’m so glad that finally right time walking by and get the coffee and bun from Maya’s ! Bun is very delicious, favorite so far in Lambeth area !

This is hands down the best bakery in London. Baked goods are out of this world. Flavour combinations are chic, original and absolutely delicious. I wish they didn’t run out of things so quickly. I guess that is just a testament to their craft and quality over quantity approach.

venues.name: Dunn's Bakery
venues.description: Long-running local bakery offering bread, sandwiches, traditional pastries and celebration cakes.

reviews.text: We frequent Dunn’s so it was only fitting to order a Dunn’s cake for our wedding. We were not disappointed! Turned out exactly as we imagined and tasted delicious. We barely got to eat any, as guests loved it so much they had finished it off entirely by the end of the reception (photos by our lovely photographer @elvira_azimova)

Australian’s love their sausage rolls served hot, often with ketchup, so it was very exciting to not only see these beauties in the hot oven BUT ALSO for the ketchup to be put INSIDE THE SAUSAGE ROLL when we asked for sauce. What is this SORCERY (saucery🤭)? I don’t know but I didn’t mess about to find out. Acquired and devoured in minutes. Pure magic! 😋🤤👏 Vegan sausage rolls also available.

Dunn's Bakery is a reliable spot for a quick bite or fresh loaf of bread when you're in the neighborhood. While they might not be the most extraordinary bakery in town, they consistently deliver decent quality. We've never had a bad experience, so they're always a safe bet for a satisfying treat.

reviews.text: Love this bakery… sweetest people and the best cinnamon and cardamom buns. The cardamom bun is like a soft hug, reminds me of Iraqi kleicha 🥹♥️

The place is known for there cinnamon bun - and they deserve the reputation.

I tried there famous cinnamon bun. It is slightly chewy, feels glazed with some crispy sugar crystals on the top. Perfect way to start a Sunday.  Only downside: could’ve have been slightly more moist, but likely personal preference here.

Likely one of the best cinnamon buns in the city.
I loved the ambiance of eating right in the working area/kitchen, so lovely and lively. The 2 nut pastries we had were fantastic, plus the flaky croissant was delicious. I can’t wait to go back.

Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Amazing food. We had baked eggs with streaky bacon with toast soldiers. It was so good. No lactose free milk though. Oat or soy only.

What an excellent little cafe. The drinks and pastries are fantastic and the service is very warm and friendly. The cafe in itself is small but cosy and I will certainly be purchasing from other branches too.

I went out of my way to visit as id seen some good reviews.
They were a bit limited and what they did have wasn't exciting me in terms of cake.
I did get what looked like a cinnamon bun in a mushroom shape and with chocolate in.
It was dry . Barely any chocolate.
It was a disappointment.
Some of the savoury food looked lovely.
No steps to get in.
Some seating available.
Near Oxford street.
I don't think I'd try again

reviews.text: Very nice coffee shop, the coffee and food are great, really enjoyed the time sitting at the window seat, the people are great and welcoming the customers, everyone is friendly !

Come here pretty much every Sunday and always a great experience! Tried so many different cakes, pastries and bread, always so fresh and delicious (their coffee is wonderful too!). Staff are always friendly and give a great service. Our favourite bakery in London ❤️

A little bakery with good indoor seating. The pastries and hot cross buns were lovely and all the other products looked delicious too.
Was slightly disappointed with the disposable cups, plates and cutlery even when eating in.
Would go back but would probably take away next time.

venues.name: Patisserie Sainte Anne
venues.description: Cosy, colourful French bakery with classic breads and pastries, cakes, macarons and chocolates.

reviews.text: Absolutely divine baked goods and drinks here! I’ve had the pain au chocolat- the chocolate is rich and the pastry is so buttery you can literally taste every flake and fold. It’s addictive. I’ve come back every day since my first one. Their mille-feuille? Unreal. The filling is creamy, custardy perfection- honestly, if I had a bucket and spoon, I’d live off it. Everything here just feels so decadent. The coffee is smooth and silky too — none of that bitter aftertaste you get at the big chains. And the staff are genuinely lovely — one of them even took the time to tell me how they make the croissants, which made me appreciate it even more. The place itself is adorable, cozy, and aesthetic — and being right across from work is dangerously convenient.

Everything I have had from here has been excellent and the kouign-amann aux pommes is always superb, I have had many 😋

I'd go so far as to say their kouign-amann aux pommes is the best pastry in London! Right up there with Habanos cigars and Scotch whiskey for pure pleasure of consumption 😃

Really disappointed with the apricot tart I bought recently — the base was undercooked and not up to the standard we’ve come to expect. This used to be our favourite spot, and we truly hope the new owners can live up to the high standards set before…

venues.name: Scarlett Green
venues.description: Buzzy, bi-level cafe & restaurant drawing on elevated Antipodean-inspired cuisine & drinks.
venues.address: soho@daisygreenfood.com, 4 Noel St, London W1F 8GB, UK

reviews.text:
This place is amazing with tasty food!
Everything we order was so delicious!! The perfect place for brunch and more.
Coffee is excellent!
Stephane made our experience the best! Such a great person, we felt welcomed.

Nice decor.. didn't have a reservation but they allowed walkins. It wasn't busy yet too. Stopped in for a quick drink and bite. We had bites from the menu and it was out of this world filled of flavour with really high quality ingredients used. I had their own old fashioned drink and there were small coconut bits in the ice. The shrimp was absolutely tasty as well as the chicken and the choux bun filled with cheese and Vegemite.

My Daughter & I came here for breakfast last year twice & this year twice. We wouldn’t go anywhere else. The food is just amazing! Our favourite are Pancakes, banana bread & sweetcorn fritters. We wish there was one in Cheshire & Manchester!

venues.name: The Buttery
venues.description: Lime Tree Hotel’s charming cafe with elevated breakfast & lunch, plus cocktails & garden seating.
venues.vicinity: Lime Tree Hotel, 135-137 Ebury St, London

reviews.text:
Such a nice back yard to have a brunch. The staff was lovely.
The food was really tasty, however the service was not so quick, we waited a really long time for our food to be served. Moreover both of us ordered something with poached eggs and one egg on each plate was hard boiled.

Absolutely loved my experience at the buttery ! The atmosphere is relaxing and beautifully designed, but what really stood out was the exceptional service. The manager Artan was incredibly welcoming, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect from start to finish. You can tell they truly care about customer satisfaction. Highly recommended!
Beautiful and cozy. If you want to be seated in the garden, you should reserve a table ahead of time! Coffee is excellent, the food itself is just normal, not too amazing.

The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Paradise Green provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Really great food, options for more healthy or vegan options if required, but they have proper hearty mains too. The chicken parmigiana was delicious. We were seated around the front which to start with was a bit cold and breezy every time the front door was opened but it eventually was ok.

The first waiter that we saw was very abrupt when talking to my sister, and taking the order from her. He was fine with me but seemed to have a different attitude with my sister.
I think equality and diversity needs to be taught to this particular waiter.
Other than that the food was great, and the second waiter was very friendly.

Gorgeous space, service was lovely. Enjoyed  my last meal of my trip to London here and it was beautiful, however it felt a bit pricey for what we got. Overall - lovely experience in gorgeous setting.

venues.name: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Notting Hill
venues.description: Creative takes on burgers in a greenery-trimmed space serving brunch & dinner.

reviews.text:
Finally tried this much-talked-about spot! Lots of hype around it, and it does deliver a cozy modern brunch vibe.

The scrambled eggs were perfectly creamy and tasty.
The granola was fresh and balanced, definitely a good choice if you want something lighter.
🥞 The famous pancakes… honestly a bit overrated in my opinion. They’re decent, but maybe not as life changing as the reviews suggest.

Overall, it’s a good brunch stop if you’re around Notting Hill — stylish, buzzy, and worth checking out at least once.

Had the most delightful Saturday brunch with my sister. The selection is a good mix between different breakfasts cuisines and the staples all have their own twist that really works. Gosh the pancake is divine, wish they also had a smaller portion for solo diners.

Just beyond my expectations!
We ordered their pancakes and it was really good topped with hazelnut syrup I guess, but I would recommend to share it! 9/10.
The egg sandwich is 10/10 fluffy egg and delicious sauce in a spongy brioche bun.
Steak & egg was also good! 10/10

Thanks to the chef and the staff👍🏻

venues.description: Drunch Oxford Circus is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Drunch Oxford Circus provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 71 Great Titchfield St., London W1W 6RB, UK

reviews.text: A lovely little brunch cafe near Oxford Circus with indoor and outdoor seating options. It's a bit of a walk from the main road so a good distance away from all the noise. The service was friendly and the food was tasty, plus a bonus that they have gluten free a bread option.

Exceptional service from start to finish the moment we arrived at Drunch. Every member of the team delivered with genuine care, warmth, and a true passion for hospitality. Special thanks to Khadija and Pujan—your attention to detail and commitment to excellence did not go unnoticed.

The omelette was absolutely delicious and made just to my expectations! My sister’s burger and my mum’s grilled chicken salad were just as impressive. Hats off to the chef—every dish was spot on!

You both went above and beyond to ensure we felt welcomed and well taken care of. We’ll definitely be back!

The veggie full english and the mexican benedict eggs, which were very nice and good portions too. We also got the fashion coffees, good and nice to take pics of. the buttermilk fried chicken was small (only 5 pieces) and very bland, wouldn’t recommend.

venues.name: Duck & Waffle
venues.description: British & European cuisine 24/7 in a modern 40th-floor space that has floor-to-ceiling windows.

reviews.text:
Great food and service!  Maitre’d was very kind and accommodated our schedule change with grace and service.

Wonderful food, service, ambiance was scenic.

English breakfast was amazing, duck and waffles signature dish is like butter melting in your mouth.

An absolute amazing experience! Took myself on a solo date there and had a great time. The food was delicious, the service was impeccable. The waffle was light and fluffy and the sweet sauce complemented the duck just perfectly.  Strongly recommend!

I had a lovely experience at Waffle and Duck. The food was really tasty and beautifully presented, and the staff were very friendly and attentive, making us feel well looked after. Our order arrived quickly, which was a nice surprise. They also have a great selection of wines to complement the meal. On top of all that, the view is absolutely amazing – it really adds to the whole dining experience. Highly recommended!

venues.image_alt: Duck & Waffle — international restaurant in Central London

reviews.text: Came a few weeks back for an anniversary dinner. Absolutely outstanding food and service, thoroughly looked after. We sat outside and it's perfect for a cool evening in the late summer. Drinks menu was extensive and we'll definitely be back. Also thought it was incredible value for money we were totally stuffed for £50pp and had 2 drinks each.

After walking one round in Borough with not many places to sit for a meal, we headed towards Brother Marcus that is also pet friendly.

Alfresco dining was beautiful and the food is delicately made. They use very fresh ingredients and you get a taste of Mediterranean.

The pita and hummus dip was a delight to begin the meal with the pan fried bream and prawn pasta.  The pasta was well
Made. Maybe even hand made.

We had two lovely desserts

Amazing food and service. This is my second visit to Brother Marcus. The chicken was cooked to perfection, moist, flavourful and not dry. The fluffy pita bread is incredible. It was a summer evening so everyone sat outside and it was a vibe. The service was great and they know the food menu well. Phil who served our table was a super star, polite, caring and attentive. I will come back.

venues.image_alt: Brother Marcus Borough — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: The Wolseley
venues.description: Elegant restaurant serving Modern European food & afternoon tea with grand, art deco glamour.

reviews.text:
The Wolseley has an amazing location and a very elegant atmosphere, which makes it a great place for a special outing.

The environment was lovely, but I found the food to be just okay overall—nothing particularly memorable. Most of the dishes were on the salty side, especially the soup, which was far too salty for my taste.

Unfortunately, I also noticed a small fly in my wine, which was disappointing. While the setting is impressive, I felt the dining experience could have been much better.

Forget the plain old eggs on toast, we’re here for the rare gems!

✅ Kedgeree with poached egg
✅ Fishcake with Poached Egg & Hollandaise

Nowhere does those old-school British breakfast quite like this place. Next on my list are Devilled Lamb Kidneys and Fried Haggis & Duck Eggs with Whisky Sauce, only at The Wolseley could breakfast be this iconic.

Despite their rare find specialities, the morning service is very busy and short staffed. If u r just looking for a walk-in peaceful spot for a full English, there r better options out there.

The food was nice but I feel like the staff need to brush up a bit with some more training. One waitress was setting down everything so brutally and not a smile once. I understand people have bad days but there’s no need to take it out on customers. Also, I thought this was a high end restaurant with a dress code but I think they’d let you in even if you turned up in your pyjamas considering how some customers were dressed. The interior is gorgeous but I don’t think I’d visit again.

venues.vicinity: The Boat, Bridge Boat House, Riverside, Richmond

reviews.text:
I had a brunch there it was AMAZING!! Atmosphere is so cozy and they curated every single detail. I loved the setting! Food is simply delicious: I had their banana bread, best banana bread ever!
People working there is really nice. I saw this restaurant on TikTok but definitely not a tourist trap. It’s worth every penny and actually really affordable compared to London city center.
Next time I will come to London I will absolutely come back!! It has to be beautiful at sunset. However I enjoyed it also with the rain, they have heaters in the outside area.

I had such a wonderful time here! The riverside view is absolutely impeccable, the perfect backdrop for a relaxing afternoon. The food and the cocktails were spot on (the Dirty Daisy and the Mars cheesecake were especially delicious). A big thank you to Angela, who looked after me so well, she was incredible, attentive, and made me feel really welcome. I’ll definitely be coming back soon!

The restaurant was fully booked for Saturday morning but we went along at 9am and were able to get a table as a group of 2. They were accepting walk ups until around 9:45am. A big barge with a beautiful setting on the river. There are heat lamps if it is cold and a smaller indoor eating area. The exact same menu as other locations which are Aussie classics which have something for everyone. I ordered the corn fritters, they could have had a bit more spice but otherwise super tasty and my husband really enjoyed his bacon wrap. Great coffee which has a light roast. Our bill was £50 for two people to have breakfast, a coffee and a bottle of water.

venues.name: The Breakfast Club London Bridge
venues.description: The Breakfast Club London Bridge is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.3-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, The Breakfast Club London Bridge provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Really nice spot to get breakfast. Staff very welcoming. Had the chicken and waffles and it was amazing. Highly recommend the Hash browns on the side with the chipotle ketchup. Yorkshire tea was great and would advise on a cheeky Paloma to chase it all down. Busy on a Sunday morning so you should definitely book ahead of time.
I loved their variety of English breakfasts and toast, everything was delicious. Even though it was crowded, I didn’t have to wait long to get a table. Highly recommended. Very good coffee.

Lovely food and service.
A great place to have a a nice breakfast whether it be pancakes 🥞, a fry up or a healthy egg 🥚 and avocado on toast
The service was prompt and friendly however the only negative is that it gets rather busy and we were only allowed to sit down and eat for an hour before being told to hurry along. Hard to do when kids are in tow and want a leisurely breakfast. This was despite booking at 8.30 am on a Sunday morning !

venues.name: The Breakfast Club Soho
venues.description: English and American breakfasts, plus comfort foods and burgers in cheerful, quirky surrounds.

reviews.text: Cozy breakfast spot located right in the heart of Soho serving delicious savory dishes. An absolute refreshing change from the usual sweet heavy brunch menus. We visited as a group of six and were seated impressively quickly, which is rare for central London. The staff were warm, attentive and made us feel welcome right away. I was especially impressed by their Strawberry Matcha. High quality, vibrant and just sweet enough. The Iced Latte with an extra shot of caramel was also excellent. As for food, I recommend the Smashed Avocado Toast topped with crispy bacon, and hash browns. Generous portions and packed with flavor. If you’re after a savory brunch spot with great service, central location and fair pricing, this place is well worth a visit.🥑🍳

Overall a good experience, the staff were really friendly but the service was a little slow. We pre booked but were only allowed the table for 1 hour, so it felt a little rushed because we were celebrating a birthday. The food itself was really good but I would really recommend pre-booking as there was a long queue if you hadn't. For vegans there is a lot of choice.

This place is great. We waited around 15 minutes for a table but understandably so. It’s so good. Well worth the wait. I went with my mum and she got scrambled eggs on an absolute door stop piece of sourdough. Both were cooked to perfection. I got the Big Stack and my god it was good. It had the best of both worlds: pancakes and bacon/egg etc etc. so full I didn’t finish it. Also had a delish vanilla matcha.
They have a few locations in the city so if the one you want to go to has a queue then there will be another not too far away!

venues.image_alt: The Breakfast Club Soho — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Milk Beach Soho
venues.description: Milk Beach Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Milk Beach Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 14 Greek St, James Court, London W1D 4AL, UK

reviews.text:
We had an incredible experience at Milk Beach Soho for my friend’s birthday lunch. I called ahead due to train delays, and Kimberly kindly reassured me they would hold our table, a huge relief on such a special day.
From start to finish, everything was perfect. The ambience is relaxed yet vibrant, even the restrooms are beautifully designed, with calming ocean sounds. The food was delicious, thoughtfully presented, and portions were just right. We didn’t even finish everything, which surprised us!
A heartfelt thank you to Swiz, who truly made our experience exceptional. She was warm, attentive, and explained the menu with care, suggesting drinks tailored to our preferences and they were exactly what we loved. Her service struck the perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness without ever rushing us.
The birthday surprise was the cherry on top: a small dessert brought out with a lit candle, a handwritten “Happy Birthday” card, and a tiny gift box tied with a bow containing a bite-sized sweet. My friend described it as “a little piece of heaven.” That thoughtful gesture made her day.
It was our first time at Milk Beach Soho and certainly won’t be the last. Absolutely memorable in every way.

We visited Milk Beach in SoHo and had such a wonderful experience. The atmosphere was welcoming and stylish, and from the moment we arrived the service was friendly, attentive, and professional. The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish we tried felt thoughtfully prepared and exceeded our expectations.

Overall, Milk Beach is a fantastic spot that combines great service with outstanding food. We’ll definitely be back and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting SoHo.

An absolutely amazing experience. From the moment we arrived, the service stood out - the host who checked our reservation was warm and welcoming, and our waitress was lovely throughout.

We sat out on the patio, which truly gave off beach day vibes - the atmosphere felt like a little summer escape in the middle of Soho. We were a group of six, and everything was handled smoothly and efficiently.

We tried a good number of cocktails (all fantastic), and honestly worked our way through most of the menu ; which, while not huge, is well-curated. The portions were generous, the food was excellent, and the setting just elevated the whole afternoon.
Highly recommend for a relaxed, sun-soaked outing with great food, drinks, and service.

venues.image_alt: Milk Beach Soho — international restaurant in Central London

reviews.text:
I finally got to try the famous Sunday in Brooklyn pancakes, and they were absolutely lovely. Perfectly fluffy, rich in flavour, and not overly sweet, just the right balance that makes them so easy to enjoy. I can completely see why they’re so popular.

On top of the food, the service was excellent. Our server, Marcus, was incredibly attentive and made sure everything was just right throughout the meal. His thoughtful service really added to the experience.

All in all, it was a fantastic visit, and I’ll definitely be coming back again soon!

Well… I came 3 times to this brunch spot to try different dishes.
Breakfast egg sandwich 10/10. Fluffy and well cooked eggs and a spongy bun!
Steak&eggs 9/10 both egg and steak were good and perfectly cooked but the potatoes on the side were a bit dry and tasted like left over potatoes.
Their famous pancakes 10000/10000 really yummy!

Great spot for breakfast! The vibe is really nice and the place is pretty big with lots of seating. Overall, the food was tasty, but I tried their signature pancakes ‘Sunday Pancakes - single' (which is quite big for me and my friend) and felt they were a bit too sweet for me 😅 not really my thing

venues.image_alt: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Eggbreak
venues.description: Hip cafe focused on egg dishes, from omelets to eggy pastas, in casual digs with juices and liquor.

reviews.text: We had to download an app in order to book a table. The menu had a great selection of egg dishes, all very tasty and different. It also had sweet dishes and salads. The food was tasty and flavours were great but it is quite pricey for eggs. Service was great. The atmosphere was nothing special.

I stopped by Eggbreak around 9:30 AM without a reservation and was pleasantly surprised to be seated after just a short 10-minute wait, not bad at all for such a popular spot.

The place itself is lovely. The interior has a warm, inviting charm that instantly makes you feel relaxed, and the atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between buzzing and cozy. What stood out just as much was the team, genuinely friendly, always smiling, and attentive without being overbearing. That kind of service goes a long way.

Food and drinks came out quickly, which was impressive given how busy it was. I was tempted to order the whole menu (seriously, everything looked amazing), but I went with the Turkish eggs, and they were absolutely excellent. Rich, flavorful, and satisfying enough to carry me through the day.

All in all, Eggbreak delivered on every level, great vibe, kind service, and food that truly hits the spot. I’ll definitely be back, and maybe next time, I will try everything on the menu

One of my favorite meals and best breakfast while visiting London! Portions were filling, juices were so good and the staff was busy but kind- would definitely come back here for breakfast! Inside is very cute and cozy as well

venues.image_alt: Eggbreak — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Caravan London Bridge Restaurant
venues.description: Industrial chic decor, an upbeat vibe & eclectic global cooking served all day in a hip hub.
venues.address: 30 Great Guildford St, London SE1 0HS, UK
venues.vicinity: Great Guildford Business Square, 30 Great Guildford St, London

reviews.text:
Convenient central location for a bank holiday brunch. Booking online was straightforward, and they had a high chair ready for us, which was great for families. We ordered the baked eggs, Korean fried chicken with pancake, avocado toast, and the English breakfast. Filter coffee came with a thoughtful note about the coffee’s origin, which was a lovely touch.

The food took a little while to arrive, and while everything tasted fine, nothing stood out as exceptional. Still, it’s a decent option for a relaxed brunch in a lively setting.

Went here to meet family. Had decent vegan options, but felt the food was quite oily.
I did love my tofu red curry!

Great ambiance and a warm welcome at reception, but that’s where the positives ended.

The food was consistently mediocre. The fried chicken pancakes were especially disappointing: dry, oddly sweet, sour, and spicy, not to our taste.

But the real issue was the service.

I understand things get hectic when it’s busy, but what stood out was the clear lack of care. We were served by Zoe, who made us feel like we were inconveniencing her. It took 25 minutes before we could even order, and only after I called her over. She forgot our water, never checked in on our meal, and when the food finally arrived, the waiter accidentally collapsed both our pancake towers.

We gave feedback on the food and asked for the bill. Ten minutes later, they offered free coffee, which never arrived. Instead, they removed just two drinks from the bill, even though we were a table of four.

We were planning a business lunch here next week, but we’ll be going elsewhere. Disappointing experience overall, never coming back.

venues.name: The Table Café
venues.description: Breakfast-to-dinner British fare served in a bright, modern space.

reviews.text:
We were really impressed by The Table! It’s a small, charming restaurant with a very cozy atmosphere and lots of plants that give it a lovely, rustic touch. The menus are colorful and nicely designed, and the staff were all super friendly and attentive.

We had The Table Full English — a classic English breakfast and everything was absolutely delicious and served hot. The quality of the food was excellent, and you could really taste that it was freshly prepared.

They also offer vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, which is fantastic. Debora was especially knowledgeable and gave me great advice on the gluten-free alternatives available.

A big thank you to Debora, who took such great care of us and gave wonderful service and recommendations. :)

We can definitely recommend this place — great food, warm atmosphere, and lovely people!

We visited The Table again today, and once more we were absolutely delighted. The dishes were freshly prepared in the open kitchen, which we really love — it’s such a great and inviting concept.

This time, we had the brunch classics: Smoked Ham Hock + Chorizo Hash with Halloumi and an Avocado + Feta Toast with bacon. Everything was delicious and beautifully presented.

Our server today was Daniel, who double-checked my gluten-free option and made sure everything was just right. He provided excellent service.

Very much enjoyed my meal out on Saturday, sheltering from the rain.
Waffles (with cinnamon pear and shortbread crumb) were gorgeous and they were happy to accept my substitutions. So many options, I was overwhelmed! Will just have to come back 😁😁
Our server was so nice and really made the experience extra special.

reviews.text: I usually give it 5 stars if a place really struck me, and The Black Penny did. The atmosphere inside is amazing, there are 4 little rooms with some tables each with a different style, but same vibe. The food was delicious - I would have loved having some cakes too, but it was great anyway. Service is just amazing. The place was not packed, so the guys had the chance to give us the best service - it would be interesting to see when the venue is full, if the level of service stays the same. I went there for the first time years ago and I had a positive memory, I was very happy to confirm that memory.

Especially books and where they belong and excellent food!
A real fabulous place to have breakfast. Sat outside in the street, but there is a lot of space inside as well! Bacon was just perfect! And eggs a la minute! 🤩🙏 really enjoyed our stay.

I arrived at the cafe with no reservation and alone but the person could manage to get me a table (I recommend to make a reservation just in case). The coffee is really good, their menu is pretty democratic to dietary restrictions people. The atmosphere and the staff is incredible.

venues.name: Victoria House Coffee & Food
venues.description: Quaint cafe featuring global brunch plates & Indian-inspired dinner dishes, plus outdoor tables.

reviews.text: We came here for a late afternoon brunch and had an outstanding experience. We ordered an iced dirty chai and a sparkling elderflower mocktail as drinks, and we got the country omelette and the rooty frooty fresh and fruity waffle as mains. Everything tasted great, and the waffle was notably one of the most aesthetically pleasing and delicious waffles I’ve ever had. The presentation was simply breathtakingly beautiful. The staff was very friendly and attentive, and we would definitely come back again when we’re in London!

Loved the food here, very flavorful and tasty. The place is popular for all the right reasons. The service was super warm. Even though there was a long queue for the restaurant, the staff was very polite in dealing with people waiting outside. The service was fast and swift. Knowing they could fit more people because of the rush, they still didnt push people to eat quickly or even order quickly. That was very nice and speak volumes about the values of the restaurant. Highly recommend going here, especially try shakshuka it was super good.

We arrived just as they were opening and without a reservation but they seated us right away and took our order, two traditional full English breakfasts. We were served within minutes and everything was absolutely delicious! The atmosphere is energetic but not chaotic. We will certainly visit again on any subsequent trips to London!

reviews.text:
Everything was so good. The service was amazing and the atmosphere was chill and fun.

For food I had the smacked cucumber the burrata and the spiced lamb pizza. I also ordered a carrot orange ginger juice which was super fresh. They even gave me a free edamame which was a nice surprise.

Great experience overall I’d definitely go back.

Beautiful place.   Stopped for breakfast and was told at entry they had no coffee ( it was ok but glad they let us know at 9:30 am lol) but we confirmed when we entered they had bloody Mary’s so excellent.  We ordered bloody Mary’s and a few toast plasters and grilled cheese only to be told they weren’t serving alcohol until 10am (yet I confirmed on their breakfast menu which stated it was 8am to 11:15am. After a bit we were told they would make them for us. Ok great. I really struggled between the vanilla pancakes and the avocado toast with egg and opted for the eggs.   Which were delicious.  But I’m craving the pancakes still especially after seeing them delivered to a neighboring table lol.  Food was delish. The spouts and crispy chickpeas on top of the smashed avocado was yum and the eggs are great.  The grill cheese was very well done.

I’ve been to many branches of Caravan but over time the portions appear to be shrinking. I ordered a side of halloumi to accompany the broccoli and black bean bowl. The beans portion is smaller than I recall from previous times I’ve had it. The biggest disappointment is half a slice of halloumi cheese for £3. It look forlorn and hardly is a reasonable portion. Gross margins on food of 55% is about standard. This is way off mark.
Lovely food but I’m getting disappointed with the experience with Caravan these days.

reviews.text:
\\ A Singaporean Girl Review 🇸🇬

What makes this place special?

I’ll give you three reasons.
1️⃣Generous servings of GOOD food.
2️⃣Excellent roasted beans for coffee.
3️⃣Great atmosphere and mood.

We came all the way from King’s Cross Station. There is also another outlet there but this outlet has a higher review point and we understand why. Throughout our meal, there was a queue outside. The half & half was generous! And the flat white was delicious 😋

Shoutout to the lady at the door (Analgar), she knew her stuff and the product offerings. Though the menu was generically written as beans, she could advise us not to take shashuka for those medically allergic to fava beans 🫘 as it was a core ingredient. She also reminded us again upon serving- what a conscientious gesture.

Highly recommended. Only thing to improve would be the door, that kinds of slams hard. Otherwise, all good.

Fantastic breakfast place although we made the mistake of not booking a table as it was very busy! Ended up waiting for 5-10 mins to be seated.

Otherwise the food was absolutely delightful – easily one of the best breakfast venues we’ve been to. Beautiful fluffy waffles, superb full English and great coffee.

Service was very good too, quick, friendly and professional. Well done to the Breakfast Club!

Expensive, but serves good quality food and is insanely popular (mostly with tourists). Expect to pay around 16 quid for each dish, and just over 3 quid for a small mug of tea. There are probably better (and cheaper) breakfasts to be found in London, but the large variety on the menu means there's something here for everyone, and the staff are extremely helpful. I will definitely be going back if I stay in the area again.

reviews.text:
Can definitely agree with all the great reviews.
Nice relaxing set up, although restaurant was full on a Sunday lunch time, we did not feel rushed and was served by a very pleasan Soniya.
Soniya carefully explained ehich are the Gluten free options and gave good recommendations.
Food is very tasty for wach of our dishes.
We had the Gluten free Fried chicken, Shasuka with oita and Soniya has kindly offered and extra piece of super fresh Pita on the house.
The Peach and Olive oil cake was divine. Its been a while I had good Gluten free cake.
Highly recommend this place .
Thanks Siniya for making this dining experience so pleasant.

Great brunch spot in a fantastic location!
Probably the best location you could ask for. The service is quite good — if they’re busy, you can leave your phone number, have a little wander, and they’ll call you when your table is ready, which is a brilliant idea. On the other hand, it sometimes feels like there aren’t quite enough staff inside; we were forgotten once and ended up paying at the bar after waiting a while for someone to bring the card machine.
Marcus tea looks lovely and tastes great if you’re a fan of chamomile, and the smoothies are excellent. Portion sizes are fairly standard. The Eggs Benedict wasn’t bad, though the mustardy flavour isn’t typical and not really to my taste — but that’s just a matter of preference. The shakshuka, however, was very nice.

Amazing food, so well seasoned and prepared. Mezza options with a tonne of options; the haloumi in particular is a must. The service was also excellent with the staff who were friendly, joyful and approachable, which elevated our time there.
Ayanthi was our primary waiter and she was delightful and made our experience even better!

reviews.text:
There are a few Breakfast Club locations in SoHo alone and after some research we found this one was most likely to be the best. I am delighted to say that the reviews were very well founded.

The Full Monty English breakfast and All American Classic Pancakes are both highly recommended and we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves in destroying both and licking the plates clean. The pancakes, even without butter, were fluffy and delicious just on their own.

I won’t lie - there’s a reason they don’t include the prices on the menu. It’s expensive! We paid over £55 for the above along with a cup of tea, an orange juice and a bowl of fruit but don’t let this put you off. It’s very much worth the experience of squeezing in, shoulder to shoulder almost with other customers, tiny tables and borderline squabbling over room for your chairs such is the cosy, space-challenged setting but that’s what makes the food even better.

Booking is essential but folk are happy to wait outside for a table if you fancy chancing your luck.

Staff were superb!!! Polite, courteous, efficient and somehow make it work with what little room they have.

A very enjoyable experience and we will be back next time we are in town.

Super easy to get a reservation so just do that. The potato's are great, pancakes were a bit flat in flavour and you don't get very much maple syrup. The drinks are great though and the service is fast and efficient! I don't get why people queue up so long for it

Cozy warm breakfast place with multiple locations in London.

Went for English breakfast and came out very satisfied. It was a very recommendable place.

Staff was nice and especially beans were delicious.

Definitely would go back.

reviews.text: I had a lovely experience at this English breakfast spot. The food was hearty and satisfying, but what really made my visit special was the service. Our server, NAV, was exceptionally friendly and attentive from start to finish. They made sure everything was perfect and added such a warm, welcoming touch to the meal. I would definitely recommend asking for Nav if you visit—great service makes the breakfast even better!

I really enjoyed the English breakfast here! The portions were generous and well-balanced, with every element cooked perfectly. The coffee was also a highlight smooth, rich, and exactly to my taste. On top of that, the staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. A wonderful start to the day, highly recommended!
Excellent breakfast and service. Lovely staff. Would recommend reserving ahead, as we were lucky to take their last available table. So much choice and will definitely return.

reviews.text: I definitely recommend this rooftop. It has a very modern and beautiful interior. Drinks are good and The alcohol is strong. Staff are extremely welcoming, friendly and kind. Our waiter recommended us what to drink based on our preferred flavours. One of our drinks came with a mini ice cream!

Not only the food choices are limited, the view is also limited compared to other roof bars in the world. There is only one corner of the outdoor area that can see St. Paul, the majority of the outdoor areas you are just facing ugly buildings. Food wise is so so, except for the potatoes with octopus which is quite good. Cocktails wise was a bit too sweet for our taste and just so so in general, although the presentation looks good. Service was friendly but slow. Price wise is quite pricey for its quality. Music was also so so in this place.

I had a blast in Florattica! My best friends have surprised me with a birthday brunch. Roberto, the manager was ever so kind to help us with our belongings. He welcomed us with a glass of bubbly and a big smile. The staff was ever so kind, we had fantastic waiters who served delicious food and bartenders were serving top-notch cocktails! The atmosphere in Florattica is amazing, you get that Dolce Vita vibes! I’m definitely coming back! - Well I did 😉 and got welcomed with a delicious glass of champagne 🥂🍾

Big thank you to Roberto, Michael, Juan and the lovely waitress from Nepal, you have made the end of my birthday weekend more memorable with your hospitality! 🎊🥰

reviews.text: This is a great place for a cocktail. They have a wide selection of really fun ones. Beautiful bar and vibrant atmosphere. The only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars was the snack selection was pretty poor. We opted for the “House crisp selection” at £4.75, which turned out to be a tiny bowl of regular crisps with a sour cream dip on the side!

Me and my friend went there for a short hangout during the afternoon. There wasn’t any wait around 3pm.  If you are finding a bar with a bit of uniqueness, good vibes and of course with some good pictures, this is the place. The interior is really unique and well thought out, it felt really welcoming as well.

I had an mocktail and my friend had a rum cocktail, both drinks taste really good. I would like to try more next time!!! Just a note you will have to ask for mocktail since they aren’t on the menu.

Taking local advice to explore Soho for a fun night out turned out to be the best decision—and The Little Scarlet Door completely lived up to the hype! We stumbled upon this place while searching for lively bars in the area and were lucky enough to be offered a table around 10 PM without a reservation—a win in itself.

From the moment we walked in, the vibe was fun, quirky, and full of energy. The theme of the bar is super creative, and the atmosphere was electric with great music and even better cocktails.

A huge shoutout to Cass, our server, who was absolutely phenomenal—genuinely friendly, attentive, and made our visit that much more memorable. He really embodied the welcoming spirit of the entire staff.

We loved it so much that we actually came back the next evening after checking out a few other spots in Soho that didn’t quite measure up. Not only did the staff remember us, but we were lucky enough to have Cass serve us again, which made us feel like regulars.

Final Thoughts

If you’re looking for a fun, vibrant bar with excellent service, creative cocktails, and an unforgettable atmosphere, look no further than The Little Scarlet Door. This spot is officially on our list of must-visit places in London—and we can’t wait to return!

reviews.text:
A Night to Remember at Amazing Grace, London Bridge

Tucked away near the heart of London Bridge, Amazing Grace is unlike any restaurant or bar we’ve visited before. Housed in a breathtaking Grade II-listed 19th-century church, the venue effortlessly blends historic charm with vibrant modern energy. Think stained glass windows and original stone architecture meeting thumping disco beats and soulful live performances, it’s a unique sensory experience that grabs your attention the moment you step through the doors.

We visited on a Friday night, when the vibe was electric. The night’s soundtrack was built around disco, funk, soul, old-school hip-hop, and even some Garage classics, which were performed live with impressive vocals that got everyone moving. As we soaked in the lively atmosphere, we couldn’t help but admire how perfectly the lighting and acoustics complemented the stunning church setting; it's truly a party in a place you’d least expect.

The food was as memorable as the music. We kicked things off with the Amazing Grace Sharer, a generous and flavour-packed platter featuring crispy Japanese Fried Chicken, sticky-sweet Korean Chicken Wings, smoky Padron Peppers, juicy Corn Ribs, and moreish Korean Potato Bites. Each bite offered something bold, spicy, or savoury, a masterclass in Asian-inspired comfort food.

We followed this with a couple of Fried Chicken Baos, which were soft, fluffy, and bursting with flavour thanks to the tangy pickles, creamy Gochujang mayo, sesame, and spring onions. But the standout dish for us was the Chicken Burger. A free-range chicken coated in crunchy panko and sesame, layered with Kewpie mayo, fresh lettuce, and pickles. It’s rich, crispy, juicy, and a definite must-try. On the side, I ordered the Amazing Rice, which lived up to its name: a fragrant mix of spring onion and ginger oil, tare sauce, crispy onion, and sesame. It’s the kind of side you could happily eat on its own.

For dessert, we shared the Salted Caramel Brownie, served warm and delicately dusted with icing sugar. It was rich, gooey, and exactly the indulgent finale you want after a night of dancing and feasting. We also had a trio of Japanese Mochi Ice Cream—Mango, Chocolate, and Vanilla—which added a refreshing, chewy, and cool contrast to the brownie.

All chicken served here is halal, which made our meal worry-free and even more enjoyable. The mocktails were just as thoughtfully crafted as everything else. My wife had the Espresso Martini (alcohol-free), made with Amazing Grace’s house coffee mix and vanilla syrup; she called it one of the best she’s ever had. I loved my Grenadine Bramble, a bright, citrusy blend of Lyre’s Original, lime juice, sugar, and grenadine . It was refreshing, not overly sweet, and paired well with the food.

A special mention goes to Dio, who looked after us throughout the evening. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely warm, he made us feel right at home, even in a venue buzzing with energy.

By the end of the night, we’d not only eaten incredibly well, but we’d danced, laughed, and soaked up one of the most unique dining experiences in London. If you’re looking for a place that hits all the right notes, food, vibes, and service , Amazing Grace London Bridge is the one. We can’t wait to return.

Feel like this place has so much potential… The food was good and the music was entertaining, however found the staff rude. I could understand if the restaurant was extremely busy and staff were under pressure, however it wasn’t. Food is ordered from the bar and when I went to order, the staff member wasn’t friendly and it seemed a chore for them to take my order. I feel like the atmosphere was let down by the customer service. Overall, I don’t think I would return unfortunately

We went through using first table and the food was delicious! Atmosphere were great and the staff were 10/10, I lost something in there and the staff went above and beyond to help me find it. They also had a live performer ANDD a photo booth! Nothing to fault

Delicious cocktails, very creative. When I was there in Sep 2025, there was an autumn menu.

I ordered something Tokyo, it was absolutely delicious and with strong flavour. My friends order something gimlet and they liked it too.

It’s not a quiet cocktail but people can still chat with higher volume.

£11-15 each. Good for a night out.

I was here last weekend & there’s a reason why it’s such a hotspot! It’s lively & full of energy in the heart of Soho, where the drinks are premium & the service is impeccable! The cocktails range from £9 to £16 & there are options for wine & light snacks too.

We tried a few of the different cocktails & some seasonal ones too… safe to say we weren’t let down!

Huge Shoutout to our server Theo. Dude just started out there & he already has it down for warm, personable service; Anyone would think he’s a veteran server.
He had a smile that could light up a room & was very knowledgable when it came to the menu (which is quite extensive!!). Theo made our visit to Swift that much greater & he will definitely be one of the reasons I will return there someday.

Warm, welcoming vibes with a great team that made us feel instantly at home - even though we arrived just before last call. The staff were friendly, chatty, and generous with both local tips and conversation.

The drinks we tried were well-balanced and flavourful, with some interesting combinations. We were especially impressed by the Irish Coffee, offered as a taster - a thoughtful touch that showed pride in their craft.

A solid spot with good energy and well-made drinks. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.text: Great vibe, food was amazing. Tried to extend our 2 hour booking but sadly were told no. Would come back next time we’re in London. A great time was had.

We got served by Alex who was awesome and then another Alex came and sang happy birthday to my friend which was also awesome and unexpected. This is the place to be if you are in London bridge. Excellent beer and wine selection. Amazing atmosphere and super nice staff..

It was okay, the atmosphere is what made the experience for me. It was busy and the music was good. Waiting times were good, I went around 6-7pm. The stairs weren’t that bad on the way up to the rooftop; but I can imagine it would be a lot harder coming down when you’re drunk. I liked the food, but this place isn’t something that you come to eat if you get me. The staff were friendly but as a small con; the seating area wasn’t good where I sat, it was quite cramped. Overall I would say 3.5

venues.description: Chic cocktail lounge with large rooftop terrace overlooking Tower Bridge and Tower of London.
