reviews.text: We had just flown into London and spent the walking, we were staying at the Doubletree and didn’t want to venture far for dinner.  They have a club/restaurant on the 12th floor.  It looks bougie but very nice, the food was delicious and we were happy with the Bou Beef and Pizza.   The view from here is awesome!

You never forget how people make you feel 🫶💖

I celebrated my birthday here and came back a week later for drinks. It was the most incredible evening - everything was perfect! The DJ banging out amazing tunes, unbeatable views over London and delicious drinks - but above all it’s the service from the staff!

They remembered me from my birthday, they were so lovely, kind and welcoming. I really can’t recommend Savage Garden enough!

It’s my favourite place in London. I can’t wait to come back! 🤩😍

Savage Garden is perched on the 12th floor of the DoubleTree Tower Hill, and from the moment you step out onto the rooftop, you understand why it is often described as London’s best-kept secret. The views stretch far and wide across the city, with a sweeping panorama that includes iconic landmarks such as The Shard, the Tower of London, and much of the historic skyline. It is one of those rare places where the setting feels just as memorable as the food and drinks.

The design of Savage Garden is striking and deliberate. Inside, the décor is bold, with a balance of raw urban edges and refined finishes. The reflective, scored, and textured surfaces contrast with plush velvet seating and marble-style floors, creating a space that feels sultry yet comfortable. It feels decadent without being overdone, and it sets the stage for an evening that is both stylish and relaxed. Whether you come for a casual meal, an after-work drink, or a special occasion, the atmosphere here makes it feel unique.

Our meal began with the Pizza Padellino, topped with truffle mushroom cream, pickled shallot onion, and stracciatella. This dish stood out for its rich flavour and perfectly balanced toppings. It was indulgent but not heavy, and easily a favourite at the table.

The Red One Burger followed, a pulled beef dirty burger with crispy shoestring fries and an egg. The beef was juicy and tender, and the combination worked beautifully. It was the kind of burger that leaves you satisfied without being overwhelming.

We then tried the crispy chicken wings served with a fermented pineapple and chilli sauce. These were excellent, with the wings cooked to the right level of crunch while the sauce added both heat and a tangy sweetness. They disappeared from the plate quickly, a clear sign of how enjoyable they were.

Another highlight was the Weeping Tiger Beef, a dish that paired tamarind dressing with spicy cucumber and fresh herbs. The flavours were bold and refreshing, with the tamarind giving a sharp note that cut through the richness of the beef. The cucumber and herbs added freshness, making it a well-balanced dish overall.

For something a little different, we tried the cheese selection board, which featured Stilton, Somerset Brie, and Godminster Cheddar. This was served with damson chutney, water crackers, and grapes. It was a simple yet very enjoyable course, with each cheese offering a distinct taste that worked well with the accompaniments.

The finale was a real standout: the warm Savage Doughnut filled with yuzu and peach custard and topped with coconut crumble. This dessert was nothing short of excellent. The doughnut itself was light and warm, the custard had a lovely balance of citrus and sweetness, and the coconut crumble gave it texture. It was a memorable way to finish the meal and one of the best desserts I have had in recent months.

Alongside the food, we ordered a selection of mocktails. Each was refreshing, carefully prepared, and nicely presented. My personal highlight was the Aroa Nui, which had a balance of tropical flavours without being overly sweet. It paired perfectly with the food and was something I would order again without hesitation.

The service throughout the evening was faultless. Maya and Iba looked after us from the beginning, making us feel welcome and comfortable. They provided helpful recommendations on both the food and drinks, and their attention to detail was clear. Their friendly and professional service elevated the entire experience, showing that Savage Garden is as much about people as it is about food and views.

Overall, Savage Garden is a destination worth visiting for anyone in London. The panoramic views are unmatched, the food is creative and delicious, the drinks are refreshing, and the service is excellent. Whether you are looking for a rooftop spot to enjoy with friends, a romantic evening with a view, or a place to celebrate a special occasion, Savage Garden delivers on every level.

reviews.text:
Excellent service. Our server was really friendly and helpful. Great food and drinks. Enjoyed the food options. Tasty yummy foods. Nice decor and atmosphere.  Had the crab and samphire dumplings, excellent. The pork and chicken were really tasty and tender. The special fried rice, may have been a bit too salty, but packed with a variety of ingredients. The salt and pepper tofu, nice serving size and also really yummy. Willing to try more dumplings. There's a platter of the best choices to try.
Went a second time. Had the afternoon tea. Service was not as excellent. It was okay. Don't expect milk or sugar as it wasn't available. No scones either.

I’d been meaning to visit Lucy Wong for years, and finally got the chance when a friend hosted their birthday party there and it didn’t disappoint. The food was genuinely fantastic. I fell in love with the aubergine dish; the flavours were rich and beautifully balanced. The prawn dumplings were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, absolutely delicious. The duck rice bowl stood out too, with just the right amount of sauce to keep it from being dry or bland. Portion sizes were generous, and while I didn’t see the prices myself (my friend kindly paid), it felt like great value. The decor was stylish and the venue even has a private terrace available to rent for events. The only downside? The drinks were a bit weak, especially for the price. Otherwise, a memorable experience and definitely worth a visit.

My sister and I booked this restaurant on a whim after a long day of shopping. The salad was absolutely to die for, the dim sum was bursting with flavour. Everything was fresh and delicious. The restaurant had a lovely relaxed upscale ambience, perfect for a low-key date night. I dont live in London, but if im in the area, I will be going back.

venues.name: Flight Club Shoreditch
venues.description: Cool darts bar with automatic score-keeping system, plus sharing boards, cocktails and shots menu.

reviews.text: It was my first time visiting this place with my work colleagues, and I was really impressed. The atmosphere was great, and the team was amazing—very welcoming and attentive. One of the waitstaff went out of her way to explain every dish that was brought to our table, which I truly appreciated. Her attention to detail made the experience even more enjoyable. We had a lot of fun, and the host was fantastic. Overall, a great experience!

This place is incredibly cool! I want to bring this back to Thailand 😎

The menu offered a wide variety of options and everything was delicious! The decoration and interior design added to the overall wonderful experience. I definitely plan to return here..

My first time here. A great idea. Using the darts machine was really easy and the games suggested were good fun.

The pizzas arrived on a paddle and were very tasty, hot and plenty. Good value. Which was surprising, considering where we were in London.

Downstairs looked like fun. We didn’t go. Maybe next time. Plus, the toilets were really clean.

venues.name: Aviary
venues.description: Elevated seasonal dishes served in a stylish rooftop restaurant that has sweeping city views.
venues.address: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London EC2A 1DX, UK
venues.vicinity: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London

reviews.text: We came here on a Saturday evening and can say im surprised this place doesnt have solid 5 stars. Absolutely lovely place. The venue is very nice, decor is stylish but subtle. Views are amazing outside too. Staff were all very friendly and service was great. But the food, that was the best part. Really impressed with the flavours of both the mains we had, lamb and the pork. Even the side dishes were amazing! Fries and the potatoes. Eton mess was nice although the chocolate dessert was nicer I think. Cocktails were great flavour too. Obviously price is higher than some places here but id say its worth it considering the quality.

The Aviary proved to be a great place to meet up with old school friends for Sunday lunch - this place is quite the little gem! Waiting for my friends, I enjoyed a frisky picant0 mocktail on the roof terrace, soaking up the sunshine and the fabulous view. The manageress was very welcoming and attentive, and helpful with the wine selection. We shared a selection of starters, all nicely presented, substantial and delicious - especially the tuna crevice. For my main course I chose the Asian Summer salad - adding the pork belly as I thought a salad wouldn't be enough.In fact it was enormous - and extremely tasty! The vibe was chilled and we were able to have a good catch up over a really nice lunch in a restaurant with a 'wow' factor! All credit to the staff and chef for a great experience.

Good selection of drinks
The Montcalm hotel’s rooftop bar, good atmosphere and panoramic views of the city skyline. The seating strikes the perfect balance between comfort and style. Good selection of drinks.
Ahmed provided exceptional service throughout our visit, maintaining just the right level of attentiveness without being intrusive.

venues.image_alt: Aviary — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: STEREO Covent Garden
venues.description: STEREO Covent Garden is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, STEREO Covent Garden provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.vicinity: Jubilee Market Hall, 35 The Piazza, London

reviews.text: A large, basement bar in Central London, right next to Covent Garden. I went there on a Saturday evening, all the tables were booked, but they let us in as there was still plenty of space around the bar. I had 2 cocktails, reasonably priced. There was live music, which added to the vibes of the place.

Loved the vibe here!! Great music, nice crowd, and an aesthetic atmosphere. The cocktails were solid, and the staff were lovely. Perfect spot for a fun night without it feeling too hectic! Definitely recommend going during the live performances regardless of the event🫶🏻

Truly an unforgettable experience. We’re here to have a meal before the theatre and what an absolutely treat and hidden gem. The space itself is dimlit and beautifully curated, the music not too loud so you can have a nice conversation without screaming at each other.

Then the food, wow what a surprise, I’d recommend the salmon fish and the tacos 🥹🥹 10/10!!

There’s happy hour until 8.30pm so that’s always a plus.

The best bit though would be the chef coming out and speaking with us - we felt so honoured for that. So thanks to chef James!

The service was also 10/10!

Anywho, would highly recommend, we’ll definitely be back!!

venues.image_alt: STEREO Covent Garden — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Bussey Rooftop Bar
venues.description: Cozy rooftop bar with 360-degree views of London serving cocktails & beers, plus burgers & chips.
venues.address: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London SE15 4ST, UK
venues.vicinity: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London

reviews.text:
After failing to get into another nearby rooftop bar, we ended up at Bussey Rooftop instead. It’s on the 5th floor of the building, but getting up there was a bit of a mission. The lift is this old industrial type that felt a bit sketchy, and you need a code to access the top floor, otherwise it only stops at the 4th. If the weather’s not too hot, I’d actually recommend just taking the stairs. There aren’t many stairs in between floors, and it’s probably quicker.

Once up there, the space itself is okay but a bit underwhelming. The menu is super limited, with only a handful of drink options. Ordering is easy with a QR code at the table, though.

The biggest letdown was the atmosphere. The whole place smelled a bit like rubbish and it was so warm and muggy. We came up hoping for a bit of a breeze and fresh air, but the space is mostly walled in and there are no fans, so it just traps the heat.

Definitely not the rooftop escape we were hoping for.
Great views, music and decor! Cocktails weren’t amazing but there were a range of spirits. Would probably return if in the area.

Can't go wrong with in made Pizzas and great beer selections. Roof top views and great temperature with easybup and down windows. Great, happy team and a DJ spinning some great beats!
Great for groups or nice intimate time too.
Hopefully the lift is working otherwise the stairs are a great way to earn that first beer!

Great selection of Alcohol free options available too.

venues.image_alt: Bussey Rooftop Bar — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Electric Shuffle London Bridge
venues.description: Retro-style, brick-walled venue offering shuffleboard games, plus a bar, pizza & small plates.

reviews.text:
A place of great fun! Interior design is top notch!

A tunnel-like interior with the arched brick ceiling and warm back-lighting. The neon highlights and glowing bottles giving a splash of modern flair.

Sliding the pucks was so much fun. We a gang of four had a great night playing the games. If you want to have a good time and good fun with friends and family, definitely gotta pop in. The music was so dancibly good we were dancing all the time while sliding the puck!

Went to Electric Shuffle for drinks recently and was pleasantly surprised. The decor is really eye catching, lots of color and visual appeal that makes it stand out from other bars in the area.

Cocktails were really good and arrived quickly which was great. You can tell they know what they're doing behind the bar and the drinks were well balanced and tasty.

It's tucked away a bit which gives it this hidden gem feel in London Bridge. The atmosphere was relaxed and welcoming, perfect for drinks with friends.

Would definitely recommend if you're looking for somewhere a bit different in the area. Nice change from the usual chain bars and the quality is definitely there.

Great experience. I visited for the first time midweek. It was about £15 each and we were in a very large group. I found the game very enjoyable and is a must visit even for a couple on a date, so suitable for everyone, even children.  A good selection of drinks and cocktails. Great decor and a cozy vibe within the railway arches.

venues.name: Spiritland
venues.description: Spiritland is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.3-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Spiritland provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Was a nice placed in a really nice area, the place was recommended by chat PGT as a listening bar but it wasn't like that. I think it's rather a whiskey bar. There's lots of DJ gear inside but and vinyls that you can't buy but they play an album at a certain time.

Was going to do one star but I have to admit the atmosphere would make that unfair. I would recommend this place for drinks but the food leaves much the be desired. I absolutely urge anyone who does order food to avoid the shrimp (photographed after already eating some) - it could still be eaten but really tasted like it came from the Aldi frozen aisle. Service was okay, very lovely front out house but beyond that could be improved once actually sat.

We visited Spiritland in the late afternoon, around 6pm, hoping to get a listen to the sound system. The hi-fi components look very impressive, but we noticed there is a bass boom which makes it less enjoyable to listen to, which if you’re hoping to attract an audiophile audience, is not great. The menu is limited and overly expensive, which I guess is pretty common for London bars, but the staff were very friendly and the service was good.

venues.name: The Coral Room
venues.description: Stylish, villa-style bar topped with chandeliers, offering cocktails, small plates & afternoon tea.
venues.address: 16-22 Great Russell St, London WC1B 3NN, UK

reviews.text: We booked a champagne tea on our final day of our trip and it was the perfect finish. Emma was an incredible host, very attentive and warm, and made us feel at home. The them was Devil Wears Prada which was done with amazing detail and finesse. Would highly recommend anyone go there, and if you can get a room too it’s a gorgeous hotel.

Went on a Saturday solo drinking afternoon.
It was pretty busy and staff were still attentive.

Love the dry martini there and seemed to be a popular pick 😊

Phone went dead last minute and wanted to borrow one power bank but haven’t got it there. Got a plug 🔌 and cable in the end..

😂Would love to take our free service to the hotel as it’ll be handy for guests to borrow it and return..

Thankfully we came at a quiet time which really helped us to feel relaxed (as a duo). The afternoon tea itself was really well thought out. Delicious tea, wide variety of sandwhiches and desserts and yummy tea and champagne. Quick service and wouldn't have been as nice without Emma serving us. She was really personable and lovely to talk to.

venues.name: A Bar with Shapes for a Name
venues.description: A Bar with Shapes for a Name is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, A Bar with Shapes for a Name provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 232 Kingsland Rd, Whitmore Estate, London E2 8AX, UK

reviews.text:
A must-visit for anyone serious about cocktails. This minimalist, Bauhaus-inspired bar takes craftsmanship to the next level - from precise temperature control with thermometers to custom ice and pre-batching techniques from their own production lab.

Despite their pre-batch focus, there's real creativity and passion behind each drink. The menu includes some truly inventive ideas, and when we asked for something off-menu, they delivered a thoughtful and well-balanced twist. Staff were professional yet warm, with lovely personal touches that elevated the experience.

Highly refined, technically impressive, and quietly playful - one of the best bar experiences we’ve had.

A great time at a super unique bar! My husband & I came here on our last night in London and I am so glad we did.

Firstly, the bar was super communicative— I emailed them to ask about updating our reservation last minute and they responded within 15 minutes.

The drinks were phenomenal. We started with the habanero and the osmanthus— both had striking flavor profiles and even more interesting creation processes. We got the kazimir and atlas for our second round — perfectly balanced and wholly unique.

The service was spectacular— Brian, Juan, and Juliette were so friendly and knowledgeable. They answered all of our questions and gave personalized recommendations to what we should try on the menu.

If we ever find ourselves back in London, this spot will definitely be on list to return to.

Lovely staff and really good cocktails. Not too sweet, perfectly balanced. All of them have really interesting inspirations, as sell, if you ask the staff. But even if not, it is a great place for some drinks.

venues.name: Opium Cocktail Bar - Soho
venues.description: Classic 'fancy drinks', large sharing brews and seasonal cocktails with dim sum in simple open bar.

reviews.text: We loved this bar!  The atmosphere was great, the drinks were tasty and the presentation was awesome!  The staff was totally top notch and really made us feel welcome.  Adam, Gordon, Papi OYP, Prince and Harold really worked well together and helped make it a special night.  As Americans on vacation, it was the perfect way to spend our last night in London!
Great cocktail bar with dim sum. The heavy on the door wasn't the warmest welcome but the team inside were great. Highly recommend the old fashioned and fish and fennel dimsum

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I can’t say enough great things about Harry, the security guard at Opium Cocktail Bar. From the moment you arrive, Harry makes you feel both welcome and safe. He has that perfect balance of professionalism and warmth — greeting guests with a smile while ensuring everything runs smoothly.

What really stands out is how attentive and respectful he is. He treats everyone with kindness and patience, handling situations calmly and confidently. You can tell he genuinely cares about people having a good time without any worries. His presence alone creates a comfortable atmosphere, and it’s clear he takes pride in his work.

Harry isn’t just “security” — he’s part of what makes the Opium experience so enjoyable. His approachability, professionalism, and reassuring demeanor go above and beyond. A true credit to the venue!

venues.name: Bar Soho
venues.description: Cocktail bar with mirrored walls and a fairground horse, or decadent 'boudoir' with baths for seats.
venues.address: 23-25 Old Compton St, London W1D 5JL, UK

reviews.text: Ryan (lead bartender) was so cordial and inviting and was just what we were looking for after a long day walking and touring the city.  Great service. Great recommendations and prob the best drinks (cocktails) we’ve had this trip.  Well done and cheers to him!

It’s a fat bar and open during the day when we popped in for drinks and light bites. Basically a club so we didn’t get the night time vibe. Service was good and the bar snacks we ordered tasty and well prepared. Next time we’ll come for the night life for sure!

Such a fun venue! Went in for drinks & pizza after work and had a fabulous evening. Staff are friendly, atmosphere is fun and bouncy - even during the more chill hours. Air con was a massive plus in the heat 🤙🏻 Will be back again soon!

venues.name: Nine Lives
venues.description: Modern house cocktails & craft beer poured in a stylish, greenery-lined space with a tropical vibe.

reviews.text:
I've been here a few times now for cocktails and have  loved each time. Friday and Saturday seem their busiest and loudest nights but I've been on a Wednesday and it's quieter but still a very great atmosphere.

Olivia was AMAZING. Very friendly and knowledgeable about menu items. My friend ordered tacos and really enjoyed but the cocktails and service keep me coming back!

Lovely cocktail bar with a fab atmosphere in a really cool spot underground and just outside London Bridge station.
I'm not a big drinker but I had heard about the food so that's primarily what we went for but I did also try the 'Mello' cocktail and it was really good, surprised by how well the cucumber flavour came through!
The mango ceviche was incredible, as was the pork, no-fish baja tacos, and beef tacos - I would 100% go back for the food alone!
The service was really good, the only negative was we were slightly rushed at the end of the meal because we were close to our 2 hour allocation, and they were super busy - but that bodes well for them if they're in constant demand so I can't really complain!

We were in last night for some food & drinks and from the get-go we loved it. Will and the guys at the front door were fantastic, so friendly and a great laugh! Downstairs decor was beautiful and created a great vibe too. Combine the delicious cocktails and food with the great service from Matin and our night was brill! Thank you for such a great evening🫶🏻

venues.name: SOMA Soho
venues.description: SOMA Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, SOMA Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
The TOMATO - possibly the best cocktail I’ve ever had. Starts savoury in the mouth- like the scent of a really crisp cherry tomato. Then it transitions thru the sweetness of a cherry tomato and ends in raspberry. Still an earthier fruit so follows the tomato well but goes from savoury sweet beautifully.
Cocktail bar is inspired by Indian flavours, sweet and savoury, done so well. Curry flavours with spirits, Indian salad flavours done in a light cocktail ect. Also rec the Cucucumber and Nimbu!! Super friendly and chatty staff too

Arrived just after 6 PM about a 15 minute wait to get in. Well worth the wait, the cocktails were fantastic and the bartender is definitely put pride into their work. The Kokum was the pride of the show. Most unique, slight pepper, but delicious all around.

This super cool speakeasy bar, located in the heart of London, offers an incredible cocktail experience. The attention to detail in crafting each drink is remarkable, and the design is equally impressive. While it may be a bit pricey, the experience is definitely worth it. If you’re a cocktail enthusiast, this place is a must-visit!

venues.image_alt: SOMA Soho — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Alcotraz London: Cell Block Two-One-Two
venues.description: Theatrical cocktail bar where guests wear orange jumpsuits, drink in jail cells & smuggle liquor.
venues.address: Unit 3B, 127 Hackney Rd, London E2 8GY, UK
venues.vicinity: Unit 3B, Nichols Court, 127 Hackney Rd, London

reviews.text:
I thought it would just be a prison themed bar, four of us went. It was honestly really good. Absolutely hilarious the whole time.  I'd say it's more of a story with actors involved. They keep you involved with the story the whole time. You bring in your own alcohol and they use that bottle for your cocktails.

The cocktails were all absolutely amazing, too.

We are planning to do Moonshine next door. It's the same company. I have high expectations.

The experience was amazing, the actors were so good at their roles and funny. They interact with you on side missions and you get a photo taken. Would definitely recommend to anyone was so worth it and you get quite alot of cocktails whilst in there.

This was a great experience. Have done the aurora immersive experience prior to this so thought we would give it a go. This one had a good mix of comedy and theatrics. However felt that you were left a long time in your cell compared to the aurora one that was continuous acting around you. Great thing to do though and cocktails were fun!

venues.name: The Rooftop
venues.description: Trafalgar Hotel's smart rooftop bar offers cocktails and Nelson's Column views, plus private hire.
venues.address: 7th Floor, 2 Spring Gardens, London SW1A 2TS, UK

reviews.text:
We stayed at the hotel and were told to just to upstairs to the rooftop at any time and we’d be accommodated as guests and Platinum Honors members. We were turned away by the young hostess. By some “miracle” just as we were about to get the elevator to go back to our room a table mysteriously appeared. I’d like to say that that’s never happened to us before but I know better.

Once we got up there, it was a decent enough experience. The food was passable and not terribly expensive by London standards.  The drinks were good. The service was a touch spotty. I almost gave three stars, but it’s more of a 2 1/2.  The best views are at the bar area and we were in a place where the view was okay, but not spectacular compared to other places we’ve been to.  We nevertheless had a good enough time.

We love the hotel, so I’m sure we’ll be back.  And perhaps we’ll have a better experience next time. This one was not awful, but it also wasn’t something to write home about. I’m only writing about it here. Hopefully we’ll be able to update this with a higher review come winter.

Myself and my friend got some small plates to share. The food tasted good, but considering how extortionate the price was and how absolutely minuscule the portion was, I was not impressed. It wasn’t the best thing I’ve ever had, and it would’ve had to have been to make up for the price and lack of it.
The same applies to the cocktails- they tasted fine but £18!!! And in fun size glasses!! I’ve had far better tasting cocktails in larger sizes and at much cheaper costs. Overall, I wasn’t too impressed.

To top it all off, we had to pay a £10+ service charge; our waiter didn’t even get us a single moment to deny doing so, which I thought was extremely cheeky.

The atmosphere was lovely nonetheless.

Disappointing Experience - Not Worth the Hype

I was hoping for a relaxed, enjoyable evening, but it didn’t deliver. The 21+ rule after 5:00 pm felt unnecessary and off-putting-like we’d somehow turn into troublemakers after 5:00pm.

The view was nice, but that was the only real highlight. Our table and glasses were sticky, and the food came out cold.

Staff were polite but overly pushy, and the whole thing felt rushed - like they just wanted us out as quickly as possible to seat the next group.

I had specifically noted in the booking that it was for a birthday surprise, but clearly no one had read it.

There was no mention or acknowledgment of the occasion, which was really disappointing given the context.

The cocktails tasted nothing like described on the menu more like a random mix of ingredients thrown together.

When we asked to have the optional service charge removed, we were questioned about it, which felt awkward especially considering the cold food and lack of attention to the booking details.

Overall, it felt more like a rushed production line than a place to enjoy a special night out. Nice view, but not much else. I wouldn’t go back or recommend it.

venues.name: Wagtail
venues.description: Upscale locale with terraces & panoramic views of London from the top of a 1920s building.
venues.address: 68 King William St, London EC4N 7HR, UK
venues.vicinity: HOUSE OF FRASER, Underground Ltd, 68 King William St, London

reviews.text:
Been here for drinks a couple times after work and on the weekends. The drinks are GOODDDD 10/10. Recommend a pina colada, it banged differently! All the cocktails look really nice.

The service was slightly slow when I last went, and we took the service charge off. The staff didn’t really seem too bothered about taking it off which made it seem a bit weird. It wasn’t busy and it took 15/20 mins for 4 drinks to come. Only disappointing thing about this place to be honest.

Also, sometimes they serve the drinks in glass and then other times they serve it in plastic cups!!!

Views are amazing! Worth a trip if you love cocktails and really want to some stunning views of the city.

Amazing views and decent prices. We visited on a Monday evening, so it wasn't crowded. The waiter was really helpful and had a good knowledge of wines. The fact that it wasn't busy made our visit really relaxing. Would definitely recommend.

We had a fantastic time starting our day with vermouth and cocktails followed by the chef’s incredible menu. Denise was absolutely fantastic in explaining (bit of a complicated) menu. The vibe is amazing and I must also praise the music list. Overall worth every penny!

venues.image_alt: Wagtail — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Madison
venues.description: Rooftop, 6th-floor bar and tapas restaurant, with hand-blown glass chandeliers and large terrace.
venues.address: Rooftop Terrace One, New Change, London EC4M 9AF, UK
venues.vicinity: Rooftop Terrace One, New Change, St Paul’s, London

reviews.text:
We had a wonderful dinner at the Madison. The views of Saint Paul’s and the London Eye can’t be beat on this rooftop restaurant. We particularly enjoyed the shrimp rigatoni, green goddess salad, and bread with Brie. Both the skillet cookie and chocolate sea salt brownie were chocolatey and delicious.

Overall we had a positive experience but a few minor remarks are that the service was a bit slower than we’d like, we had to ask for our bread, ask for the check, etc. Additionally while the salmon was flavorful we wished it came with hot sides rather than cold boiled eggs, lettuce and green beans. It seemed more like an afterthought.

Lovely rooftop bar and restaurant. It met our expectations but seating is limited near the bar so unless you are dining in you will be standing most of the time. The music is ok but I would say it's more catered for the older generation, not something you can dance or vibe to. The aesthetic and views on the other hand was beautiful and stunning but price of drinks definitely matched the clientele of the area.

Had a couple drinks here. It's got great views, very busy on a Thursday with loud DJ. Not much seating if just grabbing a drink at the bard but it's a bustling city vibe. Lovely view of St Paul's and the sunset is beautiful. The restaurant looked nice to chill and have a view without the crowd. Much quieter inside. Seating outside with the view but can't take your drinks with you!

venues.name: Mercer Roof Terrace
venues.description: Chic rooftop venue for creative local eats & drinks, plus views of The Shard & St. Paul's Cathedral.

reviews.text:
The food & service was brilliant. We came for my mum’s 60th birthday lunch and the whole experience was perfect.
Great views and a quiet atmosphere (we came on a Thursday)
We thoroughly enjoyed the food and the cocktails were also great!

Beautiful quiet and off the busy roads restaurant-cum-hotel. Close to station. The restaurant is on the rooftop terrace and offers sitting inside or outside.
While it's beautiful, there's something missing to add to the magic of a rooftop dining experience.
The service and staff were good but it doesn't quite hit the 5 star.

Mercer roof top terrace boasts a fantastic location with stunning views over St. Paul’s Cathedral. The atmosphere is chic yet relaxed, perfect for any occasion. Service was impeccable—attentive and friendly throughout. The food was a highlight: beautifully presented surf and turf, absolutely delicious desserts.Highly recommended!

venues.image_alt: Mercer Roof Terrace — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Kitty Hawk
venues.description: Kitty Hawk is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Kitty Hawk provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.
venues.address: 8 St. Martin's Pl, London WC2N 4JH, UK
venues.vicinity: Charing Cross Underground Shopping Concourse, 8 St. Martin's Pl, London

reviews.text: Julio was amazing, very welcoming vibe! We came here for coffee and they were great! Lovely view of Trafalgar Square. Would recommend this place for drinks, brunch or even just a coffee. Fabulous interior!

Came on Sunday for roast, to celebrate my birthday with a friend. We were warmly welcomed by the gentlemen who checked us in downstairs. When arriving, the other host was ready to lead us to the table. Great start.
The waiter serving us was on training I believe, and he was very attentive and nice. Also, the person who seemed to be the manager was very attentive and present on the floor.
The down was the food - firstly they didn’t have oysters which I was craving for but fine, I had a great cauliflower soup. However, the roast itself, although the veggies were good, the chicken was pretty dry. Additionally, we had the chocolate fondant which was pretty bland.
I was also slightly disappointed as I expected a special touch, maybe a candle or a happy birthday platter (anything really) as we had mentioned we were celebrating my birthday - which was nicely acknowledged on our arrival, by the host downstairs - but I guess that’s not the type of thing they do there (?)
Nice spot/view but the brunch was extortionate for what I got. £54 for a very average vegan burrata, tiny portion of pancakes and a beer. Wouldn’t return although staff were lovely and attentive

venues.name: 1 Leicester Square Rooftop Bar & Restaurant
venues.description: Rooftop bar serving cocktails, burgers and gourmet mains in a contemporary space with skyline views.

reviews.text: Fantastic views over Leicester Square and the London skyline.  Great cocktails and fantastic food - the halloumi fries were amazing and the best I’ve ever had!  Service was great too and yes; it’s a bit pricy - but what do you expect given the location?!  I do think it’s worth it though and reasonable value. Great place to start a day or night from.

I had a booking with my partner on a Tuesday afternoon to celebrate her birthday and we were both blown away by the attention and care we received. We were served by Victoria, who constantly checked on us and gave us the attention we desired and expected. I am also very grateful to the other three staff members: Jay, Pavlo, and Alp, who surprised us with a loving birthday gesture. They were all very attentive.

The view from the bar is surreal, with all of London visible (including Canary Wharf in the background, beautiful). And the food and drinks were even better than expected, somehow. We had an unforgettable experience, and it certainly added a lot to this special day.

We had breakfast at the 1 Leicester Square Rooftop Bar every day during our stay at Hotel Indigo, and it quickly became a highlight of our trip. The service was exceptional—Manager Ali and his team made us feel warmly welcomed and well taken care of. The food exceeded our expectations, both in quality and variety. And of course, the stunning view of the London skyline made every morning memorable. Highly recommended!

venues.name: Miradora Rooftop Restaurant Tequileria
venues.description: Views over the city are on offer from this modern 10th floor restaurant filled with live plants.
venues.address: above Assembly Hotel, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London WC2H 0LS, UK
venues.vicinity: above Assembly Hotel, Alhambra House, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London

reviews.text: This is a very fun restaurant! Great views of the city! The food was fine you’re mainly paying for the great views. All the workers were very friendly. It definitely can get pretty busy so you might want to book ahead.

We came for a Bottomless Brunch beforehand a theatre matinee. The menu is fixed price and it's clear before you arrive whats included so do take a look at the menu before booking to be sure it's right for you. We had  3 x soft tacos, rice and a dessert. All were great and quite filling. To drink, it was as much Prosecco and frozen margarita's as you fancy in the 2 hours.  The atmosphere is fun and loud. The views are great given it's a rooftop restaurant. Would recommend if you are looking for somewhere fun with friends especially if it's not all about the food and more about having a good time.

I had a really nice time here celebrating my friend’s graduation. First time experiencing a rooftop restaurant and was impressed. This was a nice intimate spot

We ordered a few large plates, though our chicken and potato dish wasn’t enough to share between 7 people. Food was lovely and flavourful.

Had a really lovely young waitress who served us.

reviews.text: Zohair was amazing ! Great and swift service. He gave great recommendations - will defo be back just for him !! The food was unreal. We ordered almost every dish and it came quickly and tasty. My fav was the prawns! It’s tapas but big portions in my opinion! Love it ! I myself don’t drink and the bartenders made some lovely alcohol-free options which I enjoyed. Very grateful. We stayed in the cute pods up top, great skyline view and warm too! Olly was a great help. Coming back asap! I’d be here everyday if it was summer🙏🏽🙏🏽💖
Great deals for Witching Hour on a Sunday afternoon. Good vibes, not too busy and good music. Friendly attentive staff (thanks Navya our lovely waitress) and great food/portion sizes and cocktails.

I chose this rooftop place to celebrate my birthday and I was so happy with the experience! We were a group of 10 and everyone loved the venue 🥳 We had such a nice celebration,  the Aperol Spritz was delicious and the appetizers were great too. Since it was my birthday, they even treated me to a free drink, which made me really happy 🥂 It’s self service place. The atmosphere is amazing, with warm colors that make you feel like you’re in a southern European café. Plus, it’s very close to the metro station. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to 🥰

reviews.text:
The quality of the food was more than I had expected as I was comparing to Gordon Ramsey in the Savoy. The quantity of food was certainly more than the Savoy. A good sized starter and main. We ordered sides of Fries mashed potato and salad which filled us up. A nice hot Brownie with ice cream finished the meal.
The service and staff were excellent. A very nice lunch which wasn't expensive. I can recommend and would use again.

Great service, friendly staff , nice atmosphere and good classic British food. Slightly pricey but it’s a well kept and fancy looking restaurant with an upmarket feel . Bonus that kids eat free. The kids Mac and cheese was very tasty . We also had the chicken & leek pie and the set menu chicken wings, Steak and fudge cake . All very good !

2nd attempt was finally worthy!
Our first try was back in summer, but we were rudely rejected at the door.
This time, however, we were warmly welcomed and seated promptly.
A very good spot to check out in the Stratford area!

reviews.text:
I had the pleasure of spending a sunny afternoon at Marlin’s on The Roof, and it was an experience worth highlighting. We began on the terrace, which offers truly stunning views of the city skyline and the swimming pool  accessible to hotel guests or members of the Blue Marlin Ibiza London Private Members’ Club. The setting was effortlessly chic, with a relaxed yet elevated atmosphere. My friend enjoyed a crisp white wine, while I sipped on a refreshing pineapple juice.

As the sun became quite intense, we moved indoors for lunch. The interior is beautifully designed airy, modern, and still allows you to enjoy the outdoor views, which adds a lovely continuity to the experience.

I ordered the Grilled Globe Artichoke with Foie Gras, and as someone who is very particular about foie gras, I was genuinely impressed. The foie gras mousse was smooth and rich, perfectly complemented by the tang of citric cherries. The dish was meticulously prepared, and every flavour was well balanced and considered. We ordered another round of pineapple juices, which continued to refresh and pair nicely with the meal.

The staff were warm, professional, and attentive throughout. Overall, it was an exceptional dining experience I would highly recommend Marlin’s for its ambience, culinary quality, and premium service.

We came here for drinks mainly but we did feel peckish so we did order some nibbles. Everything was perfect and the service was very efficient. What a perfect spot for when the sun comes out and you fancy some house music.

Located on level 7 of the Virgin Hotel, this is unfortunately a glorified bar. We mistakenly came here for dinner and was met with extremely loud music and poor service. The food we did receive was mostly quite good, but unfortunately was overshadowed by the missing main meal of mine and unavailable menu options.

venues.name: 1864 Rooftop Bar & Kitchen, Oxford Street
venues.description: Unique cafe fare and cocktails in a garden-like, rooftop setting at an upscale department store.
venues.vicinity: Handbags, Purses and Belts, 300 Oxford St, London

reviews.text:
1864 Rooftop Bar & Kitchen – A Hidden Gem Above Oxford Street

I stumbled upon 1864 Rooftop Bar and Kitchen almost by accident, and what a happy accident it turned out to be. Tucked away on top of John Lewis, right in the middle of Oxford Street’s chaos, this place is like a secret escape from the hustle below. The second you step out onto the rooftop, you’re hit with this incredible view of London—modern, buzzing, but somehow still peaceful.

There’s something effortlessly cool about this place. The mix of open sky (thanks to the retractable roof) and moody evening lighting gives it a laid-back but stylish feel. It’s the kind of spot where you could show up in jeans and still feel like you’re somewhere special. I went just as the sun was starting to set, and watching the sky change colors over the city with a drink in hand? Absolute magic.

I wasn’t expecting the food to be as good as it was—sometimes rooftop bars lean too hard on the view and forget about the menu, but not here. We ordered a few small plates to share, and everything was fresh, flavorful, and actually felt worth the price (which, let’s be real, isn’t always the case in central London).

But the real star? The mocktails. My friends are picky about drinks, and these didn’t disappoint. They’ve got all the classics, but their signature mixes are where they really shine. I don’t drink, and even I was raving about the mocktails—they clearly put as much thought into those as the boozy options.

What really stood out was how **warm and attentive** the staff were. No rushed orders, no disappearing acts—just really nice people who seemed to genuinely enjoy working there. Our server even recommended a cocktail based on what flavors I usually like, and it was spot on. Little touches like that make a difference.

1864 is one of those rare places that gets everything right. Amazing views without being pretentious, great drinks without the gimmicks, and food that’s actually worth ordering. Whether you’re a local looking for a new go-to or a visitor wanting a break from Oxford Street’s madness, this rooftop is a no-brainer.

I’ll definitely be back and bringing friends next time.

🌇 What a stunning rooftop! Especially on a sunny day though it's charming at night too ✨ Almost doesn't feel like the hustly bustly centre of London!

Lots of different areas, great for groups. The Benugo team is very professional and attentive...

At the moment there is a Martin Miller's Gin takeover whereby you can enjoy its botanicals around and 3 delicious and Instagrammeable Bramble cocktails 🍹🍸

From the moment you walk into this wonderful rooftop bar you realise very quickly that you’re going to be well looked after. We booked a table as a surprise birthday treat for our friend and we were treated like royalty. Gabriella the manager sat us in a private booth complete with a complimentary glass of Prosecco for the birthday girl then stepped back to let her amazing team deal with food and drinks which were all of unbelievable quality. We didn’t have to wait long and our glasses didn’t run dry! Our friend felt like a Princess and nothing was too much trouble. I’d highly recommend booking this gorgeous venue even for a break from shopping  in Oxford St as you won’t be disappointed. Well done team 1864!

venues.name: Blacklock Soho
venues.description: Atmospheric basement restaurant and bar for seared meat chops, plus cocktails from trolley carts.
venues.address: 24 Great Windmill St, London W1D 7LG, UK
venues.vicinity: Duke Of Argyll, 24 Great Windmill St, London

reviews.text:
Better than the average.
Their steak was fantastic. Went for the butchers cut, 300g sirloin, medium rare. Sadly a few inedible chewy bits which I had to  dispose of but the seasoning and sides were incredibly well thought and became a mini buffet, taking your buds on a culinary adventure. A special shout out to the Ash roasted sweet potato. The chips were the best I've had in a steak house. Think authentic hand cut chipppy chips, but cooked in beef fat and extra crispy and incredibly pillowy soft on the inside.
The bone marrow left me a little wanting, not a huge amount of flavour for something that is otherwise normally a flavour bomb.
The salad added a much needed cut through the overall richness and doubled as a convenient palate cleanser.
The white chocolate cheesecake was incredibly rich and ended what I felt was a very good meal.
The service was very good and our waiter was incredibly positive and helpful.
Thank you for a memorable meal, this was my first time and will definitely not be my last.

The place is so popular that you need to book a table in advance. We did not; but could still have dinner there after spending 2 hours in a nearby pub. The meat was grilled to perfection and the service excellent. The waiter knew everything in the menu and his advice was excellent for choosing the food. They were out of rib eye so we went for the rump cap which was very good. And finished everything with a more than generous portion of home made cheesecake. Will definitely go back next time in London.

Blacklock Soho is my favourite spot in London. If you like all kinds of meat, go for the All In Sunday Roast (£26) – beef, lamb, and pork with all the trimmings and endless gravy. Personally, I stick to the beef medium-well and it’s perfect every time. And don’t leave without the cheesecake – easily the best I’ve ever had. Great hospitality and service, easy booking. The atmosphere is relaxed but lively, perfect for a Sunday meal with friends or family.

reviews.text: I went with my girlfriends and we had such a great time. The atmosphere was lovely, the cocktails were amazing, and the food was absolutely delicious. I had the risotto and it was honestly one of the best dishes I’ve ever tasted. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Highly recommend this place — can’t wait to come back!

It’s a very nice atmosphere to have a nice meal with nice music and friendly staff. The food was amazing! We ordered the steak, schnitzel and risotto for dinner with appetizers and drinks. The steak was wonderful. The risotto was rich with flavor and the schnitzel was delicious. Definitely coming again!

Soho Social offers a delightful dining experience with its warm, inviting ambience that perfectly balances modern chic and cozy comfort. The food is flavorful and well-presented, with each dish crafted to satisfy both the palate and the eye. What truly sets the evening apart, however, is the exceptional service provided by two attentive and friendly ladies who made the entire visit feel personal and welcoming. Their professionalism and warmth added a special touch, making the evening not just a meal, but a memorable experience.

reviews.text: The dining area had a nice and cozy ambiance with dim lighting. It took about ten minutes to get the bread (7£ for four small slices is pretty steep). The mains took an approximate additional thirty minutes to arrive afterwards. The chicken breast was overcooked and dry and for 28£ it should have had more substance. The squash ravioli had the strangest flavor of sweetness and were absolutely not enjoyable to eat. Service charge included in the bill. Will definitely not be back or recommend this place for an enjoyable food experience.

The food was 10/10!! The service was a tad slow that night but staff were all very kind regardless. The pear, kale & squash salad was delicious, the whipped butter that came with the rolled out soda bread was so soft and airy, and of course the sea bream was absolutely divine, we literally ate in silence and didn't even spare time to snag a photo because it was THAT good. The mocktails and the jaffa dessert were also amazing! This’ll be on my top recommended!

Absolutely loved my visit to Nessa! The pancakes were epic—light, fluffy, and full of flavor. The chicken burger was also delicious: perfectly cooked, juicy, and packed with taste. The team was super friendly and welcoming, creating such a warm and relaxed atmosphere. Service was spot on without ever feeling rushed. A fab spot for brunch or a casual bite—can’t wait to go back!

venues.vicinity: The Devonshire, Devonshire Arms, 17 Denman St, London

reviews.text: Believe the hype. This restaurant serves up the best steaks and service, truly unforgettable both times I’ve been. The set menu is incredible value, however I do insist that their scallops are some of the best I’ve ever had in my life. Go for an early dinner, it’s an ideal spot for pre-theatre as well.

I was pleasantly surprised by everything this pub had to offer. Instagram gave it all the hype and it is well deserved. On walkup to the pub, I saw after-work patrons grabbing a pint. On entry, the acoustics were on par for a pub and the decor of the place matched that of a pub. Our hostess was accommodating of our early arrival and seated us promptly on the 3rd floor. Our waitress Siri and her trainee were nothing but phenomenal. For 146 pounds we had 2 glasses of wine, 1 Guinness, one 3 scallop appetizer,  one 12oz ribeye, 3 lamb chops, mashed potatoes, salad, and sticky toffee pudding with ice cream. At this price point I will certainly be returning. Also I would be remiss if I didn't highlight the details of each portion of our meal: the wine (Devonshire special) was spicy but a great pairing for red meat, the scallops were tender, the meat items were true to temperature, the mashed potatoes were delicate, the salad sufficient, the sticky toffee pudding was to die for: a warm coarse texture intricately balanced by cool smooth ice cream. The Devonshire deserves a 10/10 and nothing less.

Having lunch at the Devonshire was a brilliant and memorable experience. It's really popular for a good reason. We had the set menu which was £29 for three courses. Such fantastic value for what you get. Everything was so tasty, and the bread and butter that is also served with it is so good. Just a cracking experience and I highly recommend you book, if only for the wonderful pint of Guinness. It just tastes better! Thanks Devonshire and all the staff for making me and my wife's experience a memorable one. Shout out to the waiter on Saturday lunch time who served us, we were on table 28 if that helps! Brilliant service.

venues.name: The Seafood Bar
venues.description: The Seafood Bar is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.8-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, The Seafood Bar provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: I ate at The Seafood Bar in Amsterdam a number of years ago and thoroughly enjoyed it. So I was glad to see a location in London and it did not disappoint. I was able to get a seat at the counter even though it was a busy time. I started with the sea bass ceviche, followed by the octopus from Galicia, both dishes were very good. For my main, I order the fish and chips, and it was fantastic. Their signature fish batter had a nice flavorful kick to it making different than your usual fried fish.

The food here is genuinely exceptional. We ordered the 'Fruits de Mer' platter, oysters, and champagne, and it was a wildly satisfying experience. The quality and freshness of the seafood are undeniable and absolutely five-star worthy. The kitchen is clearly doing a phenomenal job. However, the reason for not giving a fifth star comes down to the service, which unfortunately did not match the quality of the food. For a meal at this level, you expect a certain standard of attentiveness that was missing. For example:
We had to pour our own champagne from the bottle throughout the meal.
I repeatedly had to get up from my table to find a waiter to ask for simple things like a finger bowl and, eventually, the bill.
It was very difficult to get anyone's attention, and while I understand they were very busy, the service shouldn't suffer to this extent. A final small point is that they dont accept cash and its a WiFi dead zone so I had to use their WiFi and again finding out the password required me to stand up and find a waiter. I paid by card without a problem, but its a policy some customers might appreciate knowing in advance. Overall, I would return for the incredible food, but I would have to adjust my expectations for the service. If the front-of-house could match the excellence of the kitchen, this would be an easy 5-star recommendation.

We had an incredible experience at The Seafood Bar. Everything we ordered was excellent. We shared several appetizers — octopus, scallops, and shrimp — each cooked perfectly and full of flavor. There’s a clear Spanish twist to many of the dishes that makes them stand out from traditional seafood fare. Our server, Yorkina was awesome!

The fish and chips were the best I’ve ever had — light, crispy, and beautifully seasoned, again with that subtle Spanish influence that makes the dish unforgettable. Even the fries deserve a mention: thick-cut, golden, and perfectly crispy.

Overall, The Seafood Bar delivers fresh, creative seafood with top-tier quality and presentation. Highly recommended for anyone who loves seafood done right.

venues.name: BAO Soho
venues.description: Intimate, wood-furnished space for steamed milk buns & other inventive Taiwanese eats & drinks.
venues.address: 53 Lexington St, Carnaby, London W1F 9AS, UK

reviews.text:
This place was great. It’s on the Michelin list. We walked in on a Friday and there was about a 30 minute wait for 2.

All the dishes we tried were good, but I loved the steak rice, mackerel bao, and daikon bao. The ambience is also nice - it’s a very cozy/intimate restaurant.

Good service as well. Reasonably priced. Would come back.

I decided to stop by this spot because of the positive reviews and it’s quite busy, but worth the wait!

I got the long day menu and extras. Overall it was a delicious dinner and well curated. The flavors were well matched and the fowl bowl was delicious along with the traditional Bao bun. The fried chicken was also phenomenal.

The drinks were just right and not too strong. The peanut drink at the end was a great way to recap the night! Overall a solid dine in with excellent customer service and I’d definitely come back again.

This place is a trendy Taiwanese restaurant. It's VERY popular, so I recommend that you book in advance.
For Mains: I had the Classic Pork Bao, 3 pieces of Taiwanese Fried Chicken Nuggets and Sweet Potato with Plum Pickle Ketchup.
For Drink: I had the House Roasted Peanut Milk.
For Dessert: I had the Horlicks Ice Cream Bao.
All very good and the total bill came to £29.15 (including service charge), which I thought was reasonable 👌🏽
The customer service was friendly and the waitress helped me pick the best options to suit my taste.
The place is a bit of a squeeze but I feel like that adds to experience 😊

venues.description: Kapara Soho is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.6-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Kapara Soho provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Got a £50 voucher, so give it a try with a friend!

We really appreciate the service by Jubear as he is very patient to explain all the drinks and food since the beginning. Thank you!

Overall food is really nice however it’s really pricey so maybe it’s best for celebration?
Or I will definitely revisit if I got the voucher again!

Food: HUMMUS WITH SHORT RIB, CEVICHE CATCH OF THE DAY (sea bream) SWEET POTATO WELLINGTON, and BLACK & GOLD.
Drinks: Tibi tibble and Passionfruit & Basil

What a great place to eat, especially for when the weather is nice and you can sit outside.
We were a group of 6 and ordered a large selection of items from the A la carte menu which we all shared including several bottles of wine.
Everything tasted fresh, was flavoursome and arrived pretty quickly. Out of all the dishes, my favourite had to be the beef short rib and burnt edge rice. It was succulent and full of flavour. The aubergine and dates was a close second.
The service was great too, attentive but not overbearing. We had a 50% discount voucher so our bill came to just under £70pp which could’ve easily have been £140pp if we had paid full price. So not cheap but definitely worth it. Would recommend.

We loved our dinner experience at Kapara. All of the staff were friendly, welcoming and helpful. Food was delicious, plentiful and beautifully presented. We had the vegetarian tasting menu and some ceviche. Can’t wait to go back!

venues.name: Dirty Bones Soho
venues.description: American plates and cocktails offered in a chill, industrial space lined with white-washed brick.

reviews.text: Myself and fiance stumbled across this place (we had been recommended the French restaurant around the corner). The cocktails are amazing and the food is fantastic. The lamb fries are so filling they could be a main not a side. The mac & cheese burger is so juicy. While we couldn't manage a dessert we would definitely go back.

Had a Bottomless Brunch at
Denman Street last weekend.

Firstly let me say the KEN our waiter was excellent.  Such a great example of how to  host a table properly.  He was attentive, knowledgable and made the whole lunch a very enjoyable experience - hence the star rating.

The options for food for the brunch were excellent either from a set menu or from some of the main menu.   The drinks were flowing as you’d hope at a Bottomless Brunch and we weren’t rushed during our allotted time.

Overall a very nice experience with quality meat and sides.

The majority of the food was good but, the portion sizes and the prices were not the best to say the least. The chicken tacos were good but the beef ones were below average if not worse. The chips were well received. Left the restaurant still hungry after spending £120 for a group of 4. The service was great tho and our main server was very chill and friendly.

venues.name: Noble Rot Soho
venues.description: Elegant, snug eatery with a European menu featuring seafood & meat plates, plus a robust wine list.

reviews.text:
Overall the dining experience was amazing.  We were warmly greeted, which was a great start!

Began with a variety of local breads, big meaty olives, and Cornish crab and Tomato salad.

Paired starters with a lovely dry summer Rose (in the picture)

Followed up with the Roasted Chicken and morels and rice pilaff. It was obviously prepared and roasted with care.

Some suggestions to elevate the experience: The service was excellent but more attention should be paid to the empty wine glasses.  I should not have to refill myself. Add some light background music to create a more relaxed and intimate atmosphere. Finally, when wait staff transitions, say goodbye and introduce colleagues.

Overall, I highly recommend a visit and will definitely return to try other items in the menu!

A beautiful meal in a lovely spot. The food really packed a punch on the flavour. I would say quite expensive as the portion sizes are on the smaller side - but it’s London, and you are paying for the name as it’s an institution. We got sea bream and a gorgeous rissotto with two sides of potatoes and a salad. Plus a bottle of wine it came to £130. A nice treat. Thank you also to our lovely waitress Mia.

Been to the Lambs Conduit location which I love but first time in Soho. Dined alone. Was seated in the cozy upstairs room. Service was impeccable. Had a lovely starter of cold tuna with courgette and capers. Perfect for a hot day. The Hake main was outstanding. This place couldn't provide a better dining experience.

venues.name: Flat Iron Soho
venues.description: Concise steak menu in an industrial-chic restaurant decorated with meat cleavers and aprons.
venues.address: 17 Beak St, Carnaby, London W1F 9RW, UK

reviews.text: The staff was friendly, the food was delicious and the atmosphere was great.   We ordered the flat iron steak with bone marrow mashed potatoes and truffle macaroni and cheese as sides.  We for ice cream as well, which we did not expect, and it was phenomenal.  The whole meal was amazing, 10/10.

A brilliant place to dine. The service was excellent. Crispin offered his expertise and opinions on everything we could order. Crispin was also very friendly; thank you for making a great experience. The food was amazing and was served perfectly in an efficient manner. The restaurant itself has a wonderful atmosphere. Would recommend for anyone. To top things off, they offer a complimentary ice cream at the end, which was a great way to end the meal ❤️

This steakhouse is quite well-known usually you’d need to book in advance, but the day I went, I only booked 30 minutes ahead 😅 Luckily, there was a table available, so I got to try it. I liked the popcorn they served as a complimentary snack a fun little touch. But honestly, I wasn’t too impressed with the steak I ordered… it was really dry 😅😂

One thing I did enjoy was the cute little knife they give you with your meal you can exchange it for ice cream after your steak. When I redeem it, I wanted to film a video of the staff making the ice cream, but they firmly told me Do not record the video😅 That kind of killed the ice cream mood for me (a bit😅😅)

venues.name: NOPI
venues.description: Serene destination with a chic vibe offering a creative menu of Mediterranean dishes.

reviews.text: Everything was absolutely impeccable! The service was unmatched and everyone was so lovely and attentive. The food was delicious and couldn’t fault a thing. And the ambiance of the restaurant was beautiful! Thank you very much for making our night so special and memorable

Delicious. I’m a big Ottolenghi fan so knew all the food choices on the menu would be right up my alley. Would highly recommend the aubergine, lamb kofta - phenomenal. Sea bass also delicious. The food portions were okay and pricing was a bit on the upper end but kind of what you’d expect for the upmarket location in London! Downstairs sharing tables work really well for groups / families.

This was my second visit to NOPI (my first was many years ago), and I was happy to find the food still consistently good and innovative. If you’re looking for bold combinations and layers of flavor in every dish, this is the place to go.

We ordered several dishes to share:
•	Burrata & Peach — Fresh and enjoyable. The peach could have been riper and softer, which would have elevated the dish, but overall I would happily order this again.
•	Heritage Tomato — Interesting mix, tossed with olives, caperberries, pickled red onions, and spices, served over a bed of mild feta. Well-executed, but the flavors just weren’t what I was searching for, so I probably wouldn’t reorder.
•	Grilled Ox Tongue — Cooked beautifully, with the right balance of chewiness and tenderness. Served in slices with a buttery sauce, watercress and parsley salad, and shredded fried potatoes. Each element worked on its own, but together the flavors didn’t quite harmonize. Perhaps it felt muted compared to the brightness of the other dishes.
•	Aubergine — One of NOPI’s signature dishes, and deservedly so. Creamy grilled aubergine paired with explosive flavors that linger. Absolutely delightful. If it had been served hot, it would have been next-level.
•	Buttermilk Pork Chop — My favorite dish of the night. Grilled to perfection and paired with a vibrant chimichurri sauce that made it feel fresh and light. It also came with a mousse reminiscent of a lighter, more airy liver pâté, which added a subtle creaminess that elevated the pork beautifully.

Note on seating: When making a reservation, you can choose between lower-level seating, counter seating, and ground-level seating. I recommend the ground level for the best ambiance. The lower level has large shared tables, great for smaller groups who enjoy a more communal setting with a view of the open kitchen.

Overall: NOPI delivers inventive dishes with bold flavors and thoughtful presentation. While not every plate hit perfectly for me, the creativity and execution make it a restaurant worth returning to.

venues.name: Bill's Soho Restaurant
venues.description: Contemporary European chain dishing up separate breakfast, afternoon tea, lunch and dinner menus.

reviews.text:
We had the absolute pleasure of being served by an amazing  girl named Katerina, at this marvelously spot in London! She was incredibly friendly, full of positive energy, and made our whole experience unforgettable. Her warm smile and attention to detail truly stood out — she made us feel so welcome, like we were old friends.

It’s rare to meet someone who combines professionalism with such genuine kindness. She went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect. If every place had someone like her, brunch in London would always be this special!

Highly recommend visiting — and if you’re lucky enough to be served by her, you’ll see exactly what I mean. 💫

Bill’s Soho Restaurant is a fantastic place that I highly recommend in the heart of London. I visited for a late breakfast (brunch), and it was an excellent experience from start to finish. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented – I tried the eggs with sides, and everything tasted perfect. The restaurant has a cozy, stylish atmosphere with a mix of modern and classic décor, making it a great spot for friends or family. The staff were friendly, attentive, and provided quick service with a smile, which made the visit even more enjoyable. A must-try in Soho!

A decent option for a quick bite in central London. Ensure though that you have booked a table in advance as it gets popular.
This restaurant has a number of vegan and vegetarian options.

venues.name: Kricket Shoreditch - Kafé, Restaurant & Bar
venues.description: Kricket Shoreditch - Kafé, Restaurant & Bar is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.9-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Kricket Shoreditch - Kafé, Restaurant & Bar provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text: Very friendly waiter and exquisite food. We asked the waiter to surprise us. That worked out very well! Indian with modern touch/feel to it. Fresh and comforty food, with subtle flavours as well as small explosion bombs, without being heavy or fatty. Loved the color scheme and the space. Hope to come back. In the meantime I hope the will consider a restaurant in Amsterdam.

Nice place and it did get very busy! The waiter telling us we only had 30 minutes to eat out mains was not good. Otherwise food is good, I recommend the venison. The coconut lassi was not for me and also if you order their chai tell them you want it hot otherwise they will serve it cold! Odd but true.

Went to Kricket in Shoreditch for dinner and had a really good time. The vibe was cool and relaxed, and the staff were friendly. Food was packed with flavour – a great mix of traditional Indian with a modern twist. They even brought out a grilled squash dish on the house, which was a nice surprise (and actually really good!). Everything we ordered was tasty and well put together.

venues.image_alt: Kricket Shoreditch - Kafé, Restaurant & Bar — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Padella Shoreditch
venues.description: Laid-back restaurant specialising in pasta dishes amid industrial-chic surroundings.
venues.address: Padella, Shoreditch, 1 Phipp St, London EC2A 4PS, UK

reviews.text:
Fresh pasta everyday - loved this place!

The food are absolutely delicious. The marinated peppers were really flavorful, combined with burrata over sourdough made for a heavenly food. The pasta are absolutely delicious. Simple ingredients but just burst with flavor.

Get the kitchen counter, so you can see the efficiency of the chefs cooking all the pasta - it was mesmerizing.

Service was great - constantly checking on us despite the fact that it was a busy lunch service.

We booked Padella for our summer team dinner (a group of 20) and honestly, it was flawless from start to finish!! 🥳

The pasta was exceptional! Fresh and full of flavour, and the tiramisu was one of the best we’ve ever had. The service was also fabulous. A massive thank you to Ajar, who went above and beyond to make sure we were looked after. Friendly, attentive, and made us feel really welcome.

Perfect spot for groups, incredible food, brilliant service. We’ll absolutely be back!

🍝🍝🍝🍝
The food was good. Service was a bit weird. Some of the front doors and staff were a bit odd toward us. But our waiter was really nice.

venues.name: Flat Iron Shoreditch
venues.description: Flat Iron Shoreditch is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.7-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Flat Iron Shoreditch provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Flat Iron has an efficient and friendly service. It is reasonably priced and tasty. An easy option to recommend to people looking for a quick and reasonably priced steak.

The sides are also good. I enjoy the creamed spinach and the cheesy aubergine.

I dont go often as my one issue is that the steak comes out too oily for my personal taste. But a relatively minor and personal preference point

Amazing experience. Christian was brilliant. He took our order and remembered everything we wanted exactly, brought it out perfectly and cleared our plates. He checked up on us regularly and genuinely cared about how we were doing. I have been to this branch multiple times but when I went on Wednesday, it was without a doubt one of the best experiences I have had. I also noticed he was treating other customers with the same level of care and attention. He was really attentive. He definitely deserves a raise!

We love to a lunch here. The best steaks in town, very well pre-selected and curated. The place is charming and Hygor was an excellent host, making us feel very welcome and comfortable. Thank you so much!

venues.name: Blacklock Shoreditch
venues.description: Set in a renovated furniture factory with mid-century, industrial interiors & modern, British menu.

reviews.text:
Fantastic food and generous portions.

My wife said it was the best lamb she’s ever had, and even as someone who doesn’t usually eat lamb, I thought it was perfectly cooked.

The brisket was tender, flavorful, and fell right off the bone.

The cauliflower mac and cheese was delightful as well.

Drinks were spot-on – balanced and not too sweet., and my server was extremely helpful in choosing the best ones.

The atmosphere has a lovely old English pub feel, which really adds to the experience. Highly recommend!

Delicious Sunday Roast Dinner! They sat me quickly & food was brought out hot & savory.  Very nice cuts of beef and yummy gravy.  Yorkshire pudding was phenomenal.  Carrots,
potatoes, and cabbage were perfect sides.  Nice wines by the glass and the martini was perfect. Great service.

We had an absolutely amazing dinner here! We did the all in which was £28 for some starter bites, 3 pieces of deliciously cooked meat, flatbread and a side each. Everything was cooked perfectly and flavoured so well. The staff were super friendly and helpful with the order too. Definitely recommend!

venues.image_alt: Blacklock Shoreditch — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: Popolo Shoreditch
venues.description: Popolo Shoreditch is a international restaurant located in London. With a 4.4-star rating, this establishment offers an authentic dining experience in the heart of London. The venue combines quality ingredients with traditional cooking methods to deliver memorable meals. Whether you're seeking a casual dinner or special celebration, Popolo Shoreditch provides a welcoming atmosphere for all occasions. Perfect for those looking to explore genuine international flavors in a comfortable setting.

reviews.text:
Great menu and a little overpriced, Italian tapas style. Loved the freshness and quality of the ingredients, really top notch.
Only natural wines, which was a deciding factor for me.
Overpriced for the size of the dishes and the size of the restaurant, and they will put the bill on the table as soon you put your fork down.

We went to Popolo because it was recommended in the local Michelin guide. The food and service was good, but we would not come back a second time, as we expected a bit more in this price range. Especially the size of the portions was a bit disappointing (£20 for 9 Gnocchi and £7.5 for 3 slices of Focaccia).

The food is nice. Favourite is actually the bread and pork cheek pasta. However, I find it hard to justify the price, especially the smaller portion you are getting. I mean the asparagus is fresh and juicy but 17 pound is a bit too steep. And the 6 piece of pasta for 28 pound. Ummmmm..

venues.image_alt: Popolo Shoreditch — international restaurant in Central London

venues.name: SMOKESTAK
venues.description: A smoker and grill take centre stage at this stylishly rustic barbecue joint with a bar and terrace.

reviews.text:
We shared this feast among 5 people, and it was absolutely perfect.

The brisket, pulled pork, and ribs were all smoky, tender, and rich in flavour — each with its own character but balanced beautifully together. The sausage added a nice contrast, juicy and slightly spicy. Everything came with thoughtful sides: pickles, chili slices, and that signature house BBQ sauce that ties it all together.
